An analysis of how risk is changing.

## Purpose
Monitors quality signals, the quality state and quality trends continuously. Monitoring shows quality as it changes rather than at fixed points.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor quality signals.
- Monitor the state of quality.
- Monitor the trend of quality.

## Outcome
A continuous view of the quality of the system.

## Purpose
Assesses quality against its attributes and its baseline. Assessment gives a judgement of how good the system is.

## Responsibilities
- Assess quality.
- Assess the quality attributes.
- Compare quality with the baseline.

## Outcome
A quality assessment that states how the system measures up.

## Purpose
Verifies that quality has been achieved by checking the evidence and the results. Verification confirms the quality claims that are made.

## Responsibilities
- Check quality.
- Verify the evidence of quality.
- Verify the quality results.

## Outcome
Verified quality claims or the failures to correct.

## Purpose
Detects deviations, regressions and anomalies in quality. Early detection limits the damage that a quality loss can do.

## Responsibilities
- Detect deviations from the expected quality.
- Detect regressions.
- Detect quality anomalies.

## Outcome
A list of quality deviations for investigation.

## Purpose
Identifies where quality falls short and what should be done to improve it. Identification directs improvement effort to where it matters.

## Responsibilities
- Detect gaps in quality.
- Identify improvements.
- Identify the corrective actions that are needed.

## Outcome
A list of quality improvements and corrective actions.

## Purpose
Collects knowledge, artefacts and experience from many projects. Aggregation is the first step in building organisational memory.

## Responsibilities
- Collect the knowledge of each project.
- Collect the artefacts of each project.
- Collect the experience of each project.

## Outcome
A collection of project knowledge ready for synthesis.

## Purpose
Compares projects to find what they have in common and where they differ. Synthesis across projects shows what is general and what is particular.

## Responsibilities
- Compare projects.
- Identify what the projects have in common.
- Analyse the differences between them.

## Outcome
A synthesis that distinguishes common practice from local variation.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns that recur across projects. Recurring patterns show what the organisation does repeatedly, well or badly.

## Responsibilities
- Discover patterns.
- Detect recurrence.
- Analyse patterns across projects.

## Outcome
Patterns that recur across projects.

## Purpose
Analyses patterns and outcomes to determine what the organisation has learned. Analysis finds the learning contained in experience.

## Responsibilities
- Discover patterns in experience.
- Analyse what has been learned.
- Analyse outcomes.

## Outcome
An analysis of what the organisation has learned.

## Purpose
Consolidates, correlates and generalises lessons so that they apply beyond the case in which they arose. Synthesis turns single lessons into general guidance.

## Responsibilities
- Consolidate lessons.
- Correlate lessons.
- Generalise lessons.

## Outcome
General lessons that can guide future work.

## Purpose
Applies what has been learned to practice, knowledge use and capability. Learning has value only when it changes how work is done.

## Responsibilities
- Adapt practices using the lessons.
- Apply knowledge to current work.
- Improve capability.

## Outcome
Practice and capability that have been changed by what was learned.

## Purpose
Assesses whether learning produced real improvement. Assessment shows whether the investment in learning pays off.

## Responsibilities
- Measure outcomes.
- Assess the improvement achieved.
- Assess how effective the learning is.

## Outcome
An assessment of the improvement that learning produced.

## Purpose
Measures the state and performance of a capability and assesses its gaps and maturity. Assessment establishes where a capability stands.

## Responsibilities
- Measure the capability.
- Assess the state of the capability.
- Assess its gaps, performance and maturity.

## Outcome
A capability assessment that states where the capability stands.

## Purpose
Analyses the structure, dependencies and performance of a capability. Analysis explains why a capability performs as it does.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the structure of the capability.
- Analyse the dependencies of the capability.
- Analyse the performance of the capability.

## Outcome
An analysis that explains the performance of the capability.

## Purpose
Measures performance, analyses its trend and finds bottlenecks. Performance analysis shows where effort will improve results.

## Responsibilities
- Measure performance.
- Analyse the trend of performance.
- Analyse bottlenecks.

## Outcome
A performance analysis that identifies where performance is limited.

## Purpose
Discovers opportunities for improvement and identifies the gaps in capability that justify them. Identification gives improvement effort a defined target.

## Responsibilities
- Discover improvement opportunities.
- Analyse gaps.
- Identify the improvements that are worth making.

## Outcome
A list of improvements worth making.

## Purpose
Optimises a capability by analysing options, simulating change, implementing it and evaluating the result. Optimisation changes capability on the strength of evidence.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse optimisation options.
- Simulate the effect of change.
- Implement the optimisation.
- Evaluate the outcome.

## Outcome
A capability that has been optimised with the outcome evaluated.

## Purpose
Discovers the signals of impact, the assets affected and the scope of a change. Discovery is the starting point of enterprise-wide impact analysis.

## Responsibilities
- Discover the signals of impact.
- Discover the assets that are affected.
- Discover the scope of the change.

## Outcome
A discovered scope of impact for the change.

## Purpose
Discovers and maps dependencies and traverses them to find what depends on what. Dependency analysis shows how far a change can reach.

## Responsibilities
- Discover dependencies.
- Map dependencies.
- Traverse dependencies.

## Outcome
A dependency map that shows how far a change can reach.

## Purpose
Analyses the impact of a change on other systems and on the portfolio as a whole. Changes often reach beyond the system in which they are made.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the dependencies between systems.
- Assess the impact on other systems.
- Analyse the impact on the portfolio.

## Outcome
An assessment of the effect of a change across systems.

## Purpose
Follows an impact through the chain of dependencies to find downstream and transitive effects. Propagation analysis finds impacts that are not visible at the point of change.

## Responsibilities
- Map the propagation of impact.
- Analyse the downstream impact.
- Analyse the transitive impact.

## Outcome
A map of how an impact propagates.

## Purpose
Collects stakeholder signals from meetings, tickets, support conversations and other communications. Signals show what stakeholders need without asking them again.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse meetings.
- Analyse tickets.
- Analyse support conversations.
- Analyse communications.

## Outcome
A collection of stakeholder signals for analysis.

## Purpose
Extracts the intent, needs, expectations and concerns that stakeholders express. Extraction turns communication into statements that can be acted on.

## Responsibilities
- Identify the intent in the signals.
- Extract needs.
- Extract expectations and concerns.

## Outcome
A set of stakeholder intents drawn from their communications.

## Purpose
Reconciles the differing intents of stakeholders into a consistent whole. Stakeholders often want incompatible things.

## Responsibilities
- Compare the intents.
- Reconcile conflicts between them.
- Consolidate the intents.

## Outcome
A consolidated set of intents in which conflicts have been resolved.

## Purpose
Converts reconciled intent into requirements. Synthesis keeps requirements connected to the needs from which they arise.

## Responsibilities
- Convert signals into requirements.
- Consolidate the requirements.
- Refine the requirements.

## Outcome
Requirements that are derived from stakeholder intent.

## Purpose
Keeps the requirement baseline aligned with current stakeholder intent. A baseline that is not maintained stops representing what stakeholders want.

## Responsibilities
- Update the baseline.
- Detect changes to requirements.
- Reconcile the baseline with current intent.

## Outcome
A requirement baseline that matches current intent.

## Purpose
Observes how the business actually behaves in its processes and transactions. Observed behaviour is the reference against which the domain model is judged.

## Responsibilities
- Observe business behaviour.
- Monitor process behaviour.
- Monitor transaction behaviour.

## Outcome
A record of how the business actually behaves.

## Purpose
Compares the domain model with the observed behaviour and with other versions of the model. Comparison shows where the model no longer fits.

## Responsibilities
- Compare the model with the behaviour.
- Compare versions of the model.
- Compare the structure of models.

## Outcome
A comparison that shows where the model and the behaviour differ.

## Purpose
Detects when the domain model has drifted from reality in its concepts, relationships or behaviour. Drift makes the model misleading.

## Responsibilities
- Detect drift in concepts.
- Detect drift in relationships.
- Detect drift in behaviour.

## Outcome
A list of drifts between the domain model and reality.

## Purpose
Brings the domain model back into agreement with the behaviour it describes. Reconciliation restores the usefulness of the model.

## Responsibilities
- Correct the model.
- Align the model with reality.
- Reconcile the model with observed behaviour.

## Outcome
A domain model that agrees with observed behaviour.

## Purpose
Validates the domain model against behaviour and for consistency. Validation confirms that the model can be relied on.

## Responsibilities
- Validate the model.
- Validate the behaviour it describes.
- Check the domain for consistency.

## Outcome
A validated domain model.

## Purpose
Analyses trends in the architecture, in technology and in usage. Trends show the direction in which the architecture is moving.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor trends in the architecture.
- Analyse technology trends.
- Analyse usage trends.

## Outcome
An analysis of the trends that affect the architecture.

## Purpose
Analyses the lifecycle of technologies, their support and their dependencies. Technologies that reach the end of their lifecycle become risks.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the lifecycle of technologies.
- Analyse their support lifecycle.
- Analyse the lifecycle of dependencies.

## Outcome
An analysis of where technologies stand in their lifecycle.

## Purpose
Detects the signals that parts of an architecture are becoming obsolete. Detection gives time to plan replacement.

## Responsibilities
- Detect obsolescence signals.
- Detect technology obsolescence.
- Detect pattern obsolescence.

## Outcome
A list of elements that are becoming obsolete.

## Purpose
Forecasts when and how parts of an architecture will become obsolete. Prediction lets replacement be planned before it is forced.

## Responsibilities
- Forecast obsolescence.
- Predict lifecycle events.
- Predict the risk of obsolescence.

## Outcome
Predictions of when obsolescence will occur and what it risks.

## Purpose
Discovers structural patterns in architectures and their dependencies. Patterns reveal common designs and common weaknesses.

## Responsibilities
- Discover architecture patterns.
- Discover structural patterns.
- Discover dependency patterns.

## Outcome
A set of discovered structural patterns.

## Purpose
Compares architectures, structures and dependencies across systems. Comparison shows where systems share a design and where they differ.

## Responsibilities
- Compare architectures.
- Compare structures.
- Compare dependencies.

## Outcome
A comparison of systems that shows similarities and differences.

## Purpose
Analyses, classifies and correlates patterns. Analysis explains what patterns mean and how they relate.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse patterns.
- Classify patterns.
- Correlate patterns.

## Outcome
Patterns that have been analysed, classified and correlated.

## Purpose
Detects structural weaknesses, recurring weaknesses and structural anomalies. Weaknesses that recur across systems point to a design problem.

## Responsibilities
- Detect structural weaknesses.
- Detect weaknesses that recur.
- Detect structural anomalies.

## Outcome
A list of structural weaknesses for correction.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns in code, including implementation patterns and patterns of fixes. Code patterns show what can be applied elsewhere.

## Responsibilities
- Discover code patterns.
- Discover implementation patterns.
- Discover the patterns of fixes.

## Outcome
A set of discovered code patterns.

## Purpose
Compares code, structure and dependencies across codebases. Comparison shows where a pattern from one codebase applies to another.

## Responsibilities
- Compare code.
- Compare structure.
- Compare dependencies.

## Outcome
A comparison of codebases that shows where they are alike.

## Purpose
Analyses whether a pattern applies to a codebase, which code is affected and how context changes the application. Applicability must be known before a pattern is propagated.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the applicability of the pattern.
- Identify the code that is affected.
- Analyse the differences in context.

## Outcome
An analysis of where a pattern applies and where it does not.

## Purpose
Applies a change that proved valuable in one place to equivalent places elsewhere. Propagation spreads a fix or improvement across codebases.

## Responsibilities
- Identify equivalent changes.
- Analyse the propagation of the change.
- Apply the change.

## Outcome
A change that has been applied across the codebases where it is relevant.

## Purpose
Verifies that a propagated change is correct, consistent and compatible. Verification confirms that propagation caused no harm.

## Responsibilities
- Verify the change.
- Verify consistency.
- Verify compatibility.

## Outcome
A propagated change that has been verified.

## Purpose
Collects configurations and monitors their state and their environments. Monitoring shows what configuration is actually in place.

## Responsibilities
- Collect configurations.
- Monitor the state of configurations.
- Monitor environments.

## Outcome
A current record of configuration across environments.

## Purpose
Compares configurations with the desired state, with other environments and across versions. Comparison finds differences that should not exist.

## Responsibilities
- Compare with the desired state.
- Compare environments.
- Compare versions.

## Outcome
A comparison that lists configuration differences.

## Purpose
Detects when configurations, environments and dependencies have drifted from what they should be. Drift causes environments to behave differently from one another.

## Responsibilities
- Detect configuration drift.
- Detect environment drift.
- Detect dependency drift.

## Outcome
A list of drifts to be investigated.

## Purpose
Classifies drift and analyses its impact and cause. Analysis shows which drift matters and why it occurred.

## Responsibilities
- Classify the drift.
- Analyse the impact of the drift.
- Analyse its cause.

## Outcome
An analysis that explains each drift and its significance.

## Purpose
Corrects and restores configurations so that they match the desired state. Reconciliation ends drift.

## Responsibilities
- Correct configurations.
- Restore configurations.
- Reconcile the actual state with the desired state.

## Outcome
Configurations that match the desired state.

## Purpose
Measures test coverage and analyses its level and its trend. Coverage shows how much of the system the tests exercise.

## Responsibilities
- Measure coverage.
- Analyse coverage.
- Analyse the trend of coverage.

## Outcome
An analysis of how well the tests cover the system.

## Purpose
Analyses historical defects, classifies them and correlates them with test coverage. Defect history shows where testing has been weak.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse historical defects.
- Classify defects.
- Correlate defects with coverage.

## Outcome
An analysis of defect patterns and their relation to coverage.

## Purpose
Predicts where gaps in test coverage are likely to let defects through. Prediction directs testing effort to where it matters.

## Responsibilities
- Predict gaps.
- Predict defect exposure.
- Predict the risk from coverage gaps.

## Outcome
Predictions of the coverage gaps that carry the most risk.

## Purpose
Identifies missing tests, weak coverage and scenarios that no test covers. Identification gives test design a defined target.

## Responsibilities
- Identify missing tests.
- Identify weak coverage.
- Identify scenarios that are not covered.

## Outcome
A list of test gaps to be closed.

## Purpose
Recommends the tests that should be added to close coverage gaps. Recommendations turn analysis into test work.

## Responsibilities
- Recommend test cases.
- Recommend test scenarios.
- Recommend coverage improvements.

## Outcome
Recommended tests that would close the identified gaps.

## Purpose
Identifies and scans for vulnerabilities and correlates the findings. Discovery is the first stage of assessing the security posture of a system.

## Responsibilities
- Identify vulnerabilities.
- Scan for vulnerabilities.
- Correlate vulnerability findings.

## Outcome
A set of discovered vulnerabilities for assessment.

## Purpose
Discovers and assesses how exposed a system is, including the size and shape of its attack surface. Knowing the exposure shows where an attacker could reach.

## Responsibilities
- Discover the points at which the system is exposed.
- Analyse the attack surface of the system.
- Assess the degree of exposure at each point.

## Outcome
An exposure analysis that shows where the system can be reached.

## Purpose
Assesses how serious each vulnerability is, how easily it can be exploited and what its impact would be. Assessment allows vulnerabilities to be ranked so that the most dangerous are fixed first.

## Responsibilities
- Assess the severity of each vulnerability.
- Assess how exploitable each vulnerability is.
- Assess the impact if the vulnerability were exploited.

## Outcome
Vulnerabilities ranked by severity, exploitability and impact.

## Purpose
Monitors vulnerabilities and the progress of their remediation. Monitoring shows whether the vulnerability position is improving.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor vulnerabilities as they are found and as they change.
- Track the state of each vulnerability.
- Monitor the progress of remediation.

## Outcome
A current view of open vulnerabilities and the progress made on them.

## Purpose
Measures the overall security posture of a system, including its exposure and its security state. Posture assessment gives a single picture of how secure the system is.

## Responsibilities
- Measure the security posture.
- Measure the exposure.
- Assess the state of security.

## Outcome
A security posture assessment that can be compared over time.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns in threats by analysing threat intelligence and the patterns of attacks. Patterns allow defenders to anticipate how attackers will behave.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse threat intelligence.
- Discover patterns that are emerging.
- Analyse the patterns of attacks.

## Outcome
A set of discovered threat patterns.

## Purpose
Correlates threats with assets, with vulnerabilities and across systems. Correlation shows which threats can actually harm the organisation.

## Responsibilities
- Correlate threats with the assets they could harm.
- Correlate threats with the vulnerabilities they could exploit.
- Correlate threats across systems.

## Outcome
Threats connected to the assets and vulnerabilities they affect.

## Purpose
Evaluates threats for their relevance and their impact. Assessment distinguishes threats that matter from those that do not.

## Responsibilities
- Evaluate each threat.
- Assess the relevance of the threat to the organisation.
- Assess the impact of the threat.

## Outcome
An assessment that states which threats matter most.

## Purpose
Predicts the patterns that threats will follow, forecasts them and predicts the exposure they will create. Prediction allows defences to be prepared before an attack.

## Responsibilities
- Predict threat patterns.
- Forecast threats.
- Predict the exposure that will result.

## Outcome
Threat predictions that guide preparation.

## Purpose
Analyses what can be done in advance to prevent a threat from succeeding. Preventive analysis moves effort from response to prevention.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse exposure before it is exploited.
- Analyse the preventive controls that are available.
- Identify preventive actions.

## Outcome
A set of preventive actions that reduce exposure.

## Purpose
Extracts, interprets and compares policies so that their requirements are understood precisely. Policies are often written in prose that must be interpreted.

## Responsibilities
- Extract policies from their sources.
- Interpret what each policy requires.
- Compare policies with one another.

## Outcome
Policies whose meaning is established and comparable.

## Purpose
Extracts rules from policies and compares them to find how they relate. Rule comparison is the basis for finding conflict.

## Responsibilities
- Extract rules from policies.
- Compare rules with one another.
- Analyse the relationships between rules.

## Outcome
A comparison of rules that shows how they relate.

## Purpose
Detects conflicts between policies, between rules and in the contradictions they contain. Conflicting policies cannot all be obeyed.

## Responsibilities
- Detect conflicts between policies.
- Detect conflicts between rules.
- Detect contradictions.

## Outcome
A list of detected conflicts.

## Purpose
Analyses a contradiction to understand its context and its impact. Analysis shows how serious a conflict is and where it arises.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the contradiction.
- Analyse the context in which it occurs.
- Analyse the impact it has.

## Outcome
An analysis that explains a contradiction and its consequences.

## Purpose
Analyses how a conflict between policies could be resolved, including alternative interpretations. Analysis prepares the decision that resolves the conflict.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the ways in which the conflict could be resolved.
- Analyse alternative interpretations.
- Analyse reconciliation options.

## Outcome
A set of analysed options for resolving the conflict.

## Purpose
Identifies, assesses and correlates the risks of a release. Understanding release risk supports the decision to go ahead or to wait.

## Responsibilities
- Identify release risks.
- Assess the risks.
- Correlate release risks with one another.

## Outcome
An analysis of the risks of the release.

## Purpose
Analyses the history of past releases, their outcomes and their failure patterns. History shows what is likely to go wrong again.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse historical releases.
- Analyse the outcome of each release.
- Analyse the patterns of failure.

## Outcome
An analysis of release history that shows recurring failure.

## Purpose
Predicts the risk, the likelihood of failure and the outcome of a release. Prediction allows the release to be adjusted before it is made.

## Responsibilities
- Predict release risks.
- Predict failure.
- Predict the outcome.

## Outcome
A forecast of release risk and outcome.

## Purpose
Monitors how release risk changes and detects new risk as it emerges. Monitoring keeps the risk picture current up to the moment of release.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor the trend of risk.
- Detect emerging risks.
- Track the state of each risk.

## Outcome
A current view of release risk.

## Purpose
Analyses what a release will change and what depends on those changes. Impact analysis shows the reach of the release.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the impact of the changes in the release.
- Analyse the impact on the dependencies of the release.
- Analyse the impact of the scope of the release.

## Outcome
An analysis of the effect of the release.

## Purpose
Collects and analyses telemetry from running systems. Telemetry is the raw signal from which incidents are anticipated.

## Responsibilities
- Collect telemetry.
- Analyse telemetry.
- Analyse the signals that it contains.

## Outcome
Analysed telemetry that shows how the system is behaving.

## Purpose
Detects anomalies, deviations in behaviour and breaches of thresholds. Anomalies are often the first sign of a developing problem.

## Responsibilities
- Identify anomalies.
- Detect deviations from normal behaviour.
- Analyse thresholds.

## Outcome
A list of anomalies for investigation.

## Purpose
Correlates events and signals, including how they relate in time. Correlation shows which events belong to the same problem.

## Responsibilities
- Correlate events.
- Correlate signals.
- Correlate events in time.

## Outcome
Events grouped into related sets.

## Purpose
Detects the precursors, the leading indicators and the failure signals that precede an incident. Precursors give time to act.

## Responsibilities
- Identify precursors.
- Detect leading indicators.
- Detect failure signals.

## Outcome
Precursors detected ahead of incidents.

## Purpose
Predicts incidents from patterns of past failure. Prediction allows preventive action.

## Responsibilities
- Predict the patterns of incidents.
- Predict failures.
- Forecast incidents.

## Outcome
Predictions of the incidents that are likely.

## Purpose
Discovers the causes of a failure, the chain of events that led to it and the factors that contributed. Discovery identifies what to examine.

## Responsibilities
- Identify the causes.
- Discover the chain of failures.
- Identify the contributing factors.

## Outcome
A set of candidate causes and contributing factors.

## Purpose
Analyses the causal relationships, dependencies and propagation of failure. Causal analysis explains why a failure spread.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the causal relationships between events.
- Analyse dependencies.
- Analyse how failure propagated.

## Outcome
A causal analysis that explains how the failure unfolded.

## Purpose
Correlates evidence from code, infrastructure, configuration and decisions. Correlation across these sources shows which evidence points to the same cause.

## Responsibilities
- Correlate code evidence.
- Correlate infrastructure evidence.
- Correlate configuration evidence.
- Correlate decision evidence.

## Outcome
Evidence from different sources connected into one account.

## Purpose
Reconstructs the timeline, state and changes of an incident. Reconstruction recreates what happened in order.

## Responsibilities
- Reconstruct the timeline.
- Reconstruct the state of the system.
- Reconstruct the changes that were made.

## Outcome
A reconstructed account of the incident.

## Purpose
Synthesises evidence into a chain of causes and an explanation of the root cause. Synthesis completes root-cause analysis with a defensible conclusion.

## Responsibilities
- Synthesise the cause chain.
- Synthesise the evidence.
- Explain the root cause.

## Outcome
A root-cause explanation supported by evidence.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns, common practices and recurring practices that could become standards. Discovery finds what the organisation already does consistently.

## Responsibilities
- Discover patterns of practice.
- Discover common practices.
- Identify practices that recur.

## Outcome
A set of candidate practices for standardisation.

## Purpose
Drafts a standard from a discovered practice, formulates its rules and specifies the practice. Formulation turns observed practice into a written standard.

## Responsibilities
- Draft the standard.
- Formulate its rules.
- Specify the practice.

## Outcome
A draft standard.

## Purpose
Evaluates, revises and optimises a standard. Refinement improves a standard in the light of experience.

## Responsibilities
- Evaluate the standard.
- Revise the standard.
- Optimise the standard.

## Outcome
A standard that has been improved.

## Purpose
Measures capabilities, their performance and their outcomes. Measurement provides the data for any comparison.

## Responsibilities
- Measure the capability.
- Measure performance.
- Measure outcomes.

## Outcome
Measurements of the capability that can be compared.

## Purpose
Compares capabilities with those of peers, with other instances and in performance. Comparison shows how a capability stands in relation to others.

## Responsibilities
- Compare with peers.
- Compare instances of the capability.
- Compare performance.

## Outcome
A comparison that shows relative capability.

## Purpose
Measures the maturity of a capability and analyses the gap to the maturity that is desired. Assessment shows how far a capability must develop.

## Responsibilities
- Measure maturity.
- Analyse the maturity gap.
- Assess the state of the capability.

## Outcome
A maturity assessment and the gap to the target maturity.

## Purpose
Constructs benchmarks, compares against them and analyses variance. Benchmarks give a common reference for comparison between organisations.

## Responsibilities
- Construct benchmarks.
- Compare against the benchmarks.
- Analyse variance.

## Outcome
A benchmark analysis that shows where performance differs from the benchmark.

## Purpose
Monitors the state of objectives and detects when they change. Monitoring keeps engineering aware of what the organisation currently aims for.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor the state of objectives.
- Detect changes to objectives.
- Track objectives over time.

## Outcome
A current view of objectives and the changes made to them.

## Purpose
Maps engineering work to objectives and analyses how well they align. Alignment analysis shows whether work serves the aims of the organisation.

## Responsibilities
- Map work to objectives.
- Analyse alignment.
- Analyse the contribution of the work to the objectives.

## Outcome
An analysis that shows how work contributes to objectives.

## Purpose
Detects when work or context has drifted away from objectives. Drift detection shows when effort is being spent on what no longer matters.

## Responsibilities
- Detect drift in alignment.
- Detect deviation from objectives.
- Detect drift in context.

## Outcome
A list of drifts between work and objectives.

## Purpose
Analyses the business context, the changes in it and the changes in the environment. Context analysis explains why objectives and alignment change.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor the business context.
- Analyse business change.
- Analyse changes in the environment.

## Outcome
An analysis of the business context and its changes.

## Purpose
Evaluates alignment between work and objectives and reconciles them. Assessment gives a judgement and a route to correction.

## Responsibilities
- Evaluate alignment.
- Evaluate the contribution of work.
- Reconcile objectives with work.

## Outcome
An alignment assessment that states where correction is needed.

## Purpose
Defines the approach that business analysis will take, including the methods and techniques. A defined approach makes analysis consistent and repeatable.

## Responsibilities
- Define the approach.
- Select the methods.
- Select the techniques.

## Outcome
A defined business analysis approach.

## Purpose
Plans the activities of business analysis and their order and schedule. Planned activities keep analysis effort predictable.

## Responsibilities
- Identify the activities.
- Sequence the activities.
- Schedule the activities.

## Outcome
A plan of analysis activities.

## Purpose
Plans the roles, responsibilities and resources that business analysis needs. Planning ensures the right people are available.

## Responsibilities
- Identify the roles needed.
- Assign responsibilities.
- Plan the resources.

## Outcome
A resource plan for business analysis.

## Purpose
Plans the deliverables of business analysis, including what they are and when they are due. Planned deliverables show what the analysis will produce.

## Responsibilities
- Identify the deliverables.
- Define each deliverable.
- Schedule the deliverables.

## Outcome
A plan of the deliverables of analysis.

## Purpose
Assesses the context in which analysis will take place, including its constraints and the stakeholder environment. Context assessment prevents an approach that does not fit.

## Responsibilities
- Assess the context.
- Assess the constraints.
- Assess the environment of the stakeholders.

## Outcome
An assessment of the context for the analysis.

## Purpose
Assesses, assigns and compares the priority of requirements. Priority tells the team what to do first when resources are limited.

## Responsibilities
- Assess the priority of requirements.
- Assign priorities.
- Compare priorities.

## Outcome
Requirements with an agreed priority.

## Purpose
Analyses the value that requirements deliver to the business, to stakeholders and in outcomes. Value is the principal basis for priority.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse business value.
- Analyse stakeholder value.
- Analyse the value of outcomes.

## Outcome
An analysis of the value of each requirement.

## Purpose
Analyses the cost, risk, dependencies and regulatory constraints that bear on requirements. Constraints limit what can be done and in what order.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse cost.
- Analyse risk.
- Analyse dependencies.
- Analyse regulatory constraints.

## Outcome
An analysis of what limits each requirement.

## Purpose
Orders requirements for implementation, taking their dependencies into account. A sound sequence avoids building on what does not yet exist.

## Responsibilities
- Sequence the requirements.
- Order the implementation.
- Order work according to dependencies.

## Outcome
A sequence in which requirements will be implemented.

## Purpose
Discovers the alternative solutions that could meet a need. Good decisions need real alternatives.

## Responsibilities
- Identify alternatives.
- Search for solutions.
- Generate options.

## Outcome
A set of solution options.

## Purpose
Analyses the benefits, costs, risks and constraints of each solution option. Analysis provides the facts on which the options are compared.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse benefits.
- Analyse costs.
- Analyse risks.
- Analyse constraints.

## Outcome
An analysis of each option.

## Purpose
Compares solution options, including the trade-offs and their relative value. Comparison shows which option is best for the need.

## Responsibilities
- Compare options.
- Analyse trade-offs.
- Compare value.

## Outcome
A comparison that shows how the options differ.

## Purpose
Assesses the expected value, outcomes and risks to value of each solution. Value assessment allows a solution to be justified.

## Responsibilities
- Assess the expected value.
- Assess the outcomes.
- Analyse the risks to value.

## Outcome
An assessment of the value of each solution.

## Purpose
Recommends a solution option, with its rationale and the evidence behind it. A recommendation gives decision makers a clear and supported proposal.

## Responsibilities
- Recommend an option.
- State the rationale.
- Provide the evidence.

## Outcome
A recommendation with rationale and evidence.

## Purpose
Assembles components and subsystems into a working whole. Assembly is the stage at which components first operate together.

## Responsibilities
- Assemble components.
- Integrate components.
- Integrate subsystems.

## Outcome
Components assembled into an integrated whole.

## Purpose
Connects interfaces and checks that they are compatible. Interface integration makes the boundaries between components work.

## Responsibilities
- Connect interfaces.
- Check interface compatibility.
- Integrate the interfaces.

## Outcome
Interfaces that are connected and compatible.

## Purpose
Verifies the integrated system by testing it and analysing the results. Verification shows whether the integration works.

## Responsibilities
- Carry out integration testing.
- Verify the integration.
- Analyse the results.

## Outcome
Integration results that show whether the integrated system works.

## Purpose
Resolves the conflicts between dependencies, interfaces and configurations that appear during integration. Resolved conflicts allow integration to complete.

## Responsibilities
- Resolve dependency conflicts.
- Resolve interface conflicts.
- Resolve configuration conflicts.

## Outcome
Integration conflicts that have been resolved.

## Purpose
Searches for existing engineering assets that could be reused, identifies them and retrieves them. Reuse avoids work that has already been done.

## Responsibilities
- Search for reusable assets.
- Identify assets.
- Retrieve assets.

## Outcome
A set of candidate assets for reuse.

## Purpose
Assesses whether an asset is suitable for reuse in terms of quality, security, compatibility and lifecycle. An unsuitable asset costs more than it saves.

## Responsibilities
- Assess quality.
- Assess security.
- Assess compatibility.
- Assess the lifecycle of the asset.

## Outcome
An assessment of how suitable the asset is.

## Purpose
Checks where an asset came from, who owns it and under what licence it may be used. Provenance determines whether an asset may legally be reused.

## Responsibilities
- Check provenance.
- Check ownership.
- Assess licensing.

## Outcome
An assessment of the provenance of the asset.

## Purpose
Compares assets and selects the one to reuse. Selection records the choice and supports the decision to reuse.

## Responsibilities
- Compare assets.
- Select the asset.
- Support the reuse decision.

## Outcome
A selected asset and the reasoning for it.

## Purpose
Integrates and adapts the selected asset and verifies that its reuse works. Incorporation completes the reuse.

## Responsibilities
- Integrate the asset.
- Adapt the asset.
- Verify the reuse.

## Outcome
An asset incorporated and verified in its new setting.

## Purpose
Examines the artefacts, activities and decisions of engineering work. Examination is the first step of a review.

## Responsibilities
- Examine artefacts.
- Examine activities.
- Examine decisions.

## Outcome
Engineering work that has been examined and noted.

## Purpose
Checks that work conforms to its requirements, to standards and to criteria. Conformance shows whether work meets what was expected of it.

## Responsibilities
- Check conformance to requirements.
- Check conformance to standards.
- Check against criteria.

## Outcome
An assessment of how far the work conforms.

## Purpose
Identifies deficiencies, deviations and issues in the work. Identification states what must be corrected.

## Responsibilities
- Detect deficiencies.
- Detect deviations.
- Identify issues.

## Outcome
A list of deficiencies found in the work.

## Purpose
Analyses and classifies review findings and communicates them. Clear findings let the author correct the work.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse findings.
- Classify findings.
- Communicate findings.

## Outcome
Review findings that are analysed and communicated.

## Purpose
Reviews corrections to confirm that findings have been resolved and can be closed. Re-review confirms that corrections work.

## Responsibilities
- Review the corrections.
- Review the closure of findings.
- Carry out the re-review.

## Outcome
Findings that have been confirmed as resolved or returned for further work.

## Purpose
Detects problems that recur, classifies them and identifies their patterns. Recurring problems signal causes that have not been removed.

## Responsibilities
- Detect recurrence.
- Classify problems.
- Identify the patterns of problems.

## Outcome
A list of recurring problems.

## Purpose
Analyses the root causes and contributing causes of problems and why they recur. Cause analysis finds what must change to stop the problem.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse root causes.
- Analyse contributing causes.
- Analyse the causes of recurrence.

## Outcome
An analysis of the causes of the problem.

## Purpose
Identifies, designs and plans corrective actions. Defined actions turn analysis into work.

## Responsibilities
- Identify corrective actions.
- Design corrective actions.
- Plan the actions.

## Outcome
A plan of corrective actions.

## Purpose
Implements corrective actions, tracks them and verifies them. Implementation carries out the plan.

## Responsibilities
- Implement actions.
- Track actions.
- Verify actions.

## Outcome
Corrective actions that have been implemented and verified.

## Purpose
Monitors for recurrence and verifies that corrective actions worked. Verification closes the problem only when it has stopped.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor recurrence.
- Verify the effectiveness of actions.
- Verify that the problem can be closed.

## Outcome
Confirmation that the problem no longer recurs.

## Purpose
Records defects together with the evidence and the information needed to reproduce them. Good capture makes defects easier to resolve.

## Responsibilities
- Record defects.
- Capture evidence of the defect.
- Capture information for reproduction.

## Outcome
A recorded defect that can be reproduced.

## Purpose
Classifies and diagnoses defects and assesses their impact. Analysis explains what a defect is and how much it matters.

## Responsibilities
- Classify defects.
- Diagnose defects.
- Assess impact.

## Outcome
An analysed defect with a classification and an impact.

## Purpose
Assesses severity, assigns priority and orders defects for resolution. Prioritisation applies effort where it is most needed.

## Responsibilities
- Assess severity.
- Assign priority.
- Order resolution.

## Outcome
Defects in the order in which they will be resolved.

## Purpose
Corrects defects through changes to the system. Resolution removes the defect.

## Responsibilities
- Correct defects.
- Make corrective changes.
- Implement the resolution.

## Outcome
A resolution that corrects the defect.

## Purpose
Verifies that a correction works and has not caused regression. Verification confirms the defect is resolved.

## Responsibilities
- Verify the correction.
- Verify that nothing regressed.
- Validate the resolution.

## Outcome
A verified resolution.

## Purpose
Assesses whether a defect can be closed, closes it and tracks deferred defects. Closure ends the life of the defect in an orderly way.

## Responsibilities
- Assess whether closure is justified.
- Close defects.
- Track deferred defects.

## Outcome
Defects that are closed or deliberately deferred.

## Purpose
Identifies, evaluates and selects suppliers. Good selection reduces the risk of relying on an outside party.

## Responsibilities
- Identify suppliers.
- Evaluate suppliers.
- Select a supplier.

## Outcome
A selected supplier with the reasoning for the choice.

## Purpose
Defines the contract, the services and the deliverables of a supplier arrangement. A clear arrangement sets the expectations of both parties.

## Responsibilities
- Define the contract.
- Define the services.
- Define the deliverables.

## Outcome
A defined supplier arrangement.

## Purpose
Monitors supplier performance and assesses their services and deliverables. Performance management shows whether the supplier delivers.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor performance.
- Assess services.
- Assess deliverables.

## Outcome
An assessment of how well the supplier performs.

## Purpose
Identifies, assesses and monitors the risks that arise from suppliers. Dependence on a supplier brings risks that need to be managed.

## Responsibilities
- Identify risks.
- Assess risks.
- Monitor risks.

## Outcome
A managed set of supplier risks.

## Purpose
Assesses a supplier's compliance and checks that requirements are met and the evidence reviewed. Compliance management protects the organisation from the supplier's failures.

## Responsibilities
- Assess compliance.
- Check compliance with requirements.
- Review the evidence.

## Outcome
An assessment of the compliance of the supplier.

## Purpose
Manages communication with a supplier, resolves issues and reviews the relationship. A sound relationship supports the arrangement.

## Responsibilities
- Communicate with the supplier.
- Resolve issues.
- Review the relationship.

## Outcome
A supplier relationship that is managed and reviewed.

## Purpose
Identifies gaps in capability, in maturity and in performance. Gap analysis shows where capability falls short of what is needed.

## Responsibilities
- Identify capability gaps.
- Analyse gaps in maturity.
- Analyse gaps in performance.

## Outcome
An analysis of the gaps in a capability.

## Purpose
Defines the objectives of capability evolution, plans it and prioritises it. Planning makes capability development deliberate.

## Responsibilities
- Define the objectives of evolution.
- Plan the evolution.
- Prioritise the steps.

## Outcome
A plan for the evolution of a capability.

## Purpose
Identifies and carries out improvements that enhance and expand a capability. Improvement raises capability toward its target.

## Responsibilities
- Identify improvements.
- Enhance the capability.
- Expand the capability.

## Outcome
A capability that has been improved.

## Purpose
Monitors progress, assesses maturity progress and assesses outcomes. Assessment shows whether evolution is achieving its aims.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor progress.
- Assess progress in maturity.
- Assess outcomes.

## Outcome
An assessment of how far a capability has progressed.

## Purpose
Captures proposed changes, records change requests and defines the scope of change. Identification begins the controlled management of change.

## Responsibilities
- Capture proposals for change.
- Record change requests.
- Define the scope of the change.

## Outcome
A recorded change request with a defined scope.

## Purpose
Assesses the justification, the risk and the consequences of a change. Assessment supports the decision on whether to make the change.

## Responsibilities
- Assess the justification for the change.
- Assess the risk of the change.
- Analyse the consequences of the change.

## Outcome
An assessment that supports the decision on the change.

## Purpose
Plans and schedules a change and coordinates its dependencies. Coordination ensures that changes happen in a workable order.

## Responsibilities
- Plan the change.
- Schedule the change.
- Coordinate dependencies.

## Outcome
A coordinated plan for the change.

## Purpose
Implements a change, integrates it and verifies it. Implementation puts the approved change into effect.

## Responsibilities
- Implement the change.
- Integrate the change.
- Verify the change.

## Outcome
A change that has been implemented and verified.

## Purpose
Records changes, tracks their history and records the state that results. Traceability makes every change explainable.

## Responsibilities
- Record the change.
- Track the history of the change.
- Record the resulting state.

## Outcome
A traceable record of the change.

## Purpose
Collects and prepares the data used to train and to evaluate models, and assesses its quality. Model quality depends on the quality of the data.

## Responsibilities
- Collect training data.
- Prepare the data.
- Assess data quality.
- Prepare evaluation data.

## Outcome
Training and evaluation data of known quality.

## Purpose
Trains and fine-tunes models and configures the training. Training produces the model that will be evaluated.

## Responsibilities
- Train the model.
- Fine-tune the model.
- Configure the training.

## Outcome
A trained model.

## Purpose
Evaluates the performance of a model, its acceptability and how it compares with others. Evaluation shows whether the model is good enough to use.

## Responsibilities
- Evaluate performance.
- Evaluate acceptance.
- Evaluate comparatively.

## Outcome
An evaluation of the model.

## Purpose
Assesses the quality of a model, its bias and its errors. Quality assessment shows whether the model is reliable and fair.

## Responsibilities
- Assess quality.
- Assess bias.
- Analyse errors.

## Outcome
A quality assessment of the model.

## Purpose
Assesses whether a model meets its acceptance criteria and is ready to be deployed. Readiness assessment is the gate before a model reaches use.

## Responsibilities
- Assess the acceptance criteria.
- Assess readiness for deployment.
- Validate the model.

## Outcome
A readiness decision for the model.

## Purpose
Writes the firmware that runs on embedded hardware, including its interfaces to that hardware and its features. Firmware implementation turns a hardware-aware design into code that executes on the device.

## Responsibilities
- Write the firmware code for the device.
- Implement the software interfaces to the hardware of the device.
- Implement the features that the embedded design requires.

## Outcome
Firmware that runs on the target device and provides its specified features.

## Purpose
Designs firmware so that it works within the limits of the hardware on which it runs. Embedded devices have small and fixed resources, and a design that ignores them fails in the field.

## Responsibilities
- Design the firmware to operate within the available memory.
- Design the firmware to meet its timing constraints.
- Design the firmware to operate within the power budget.

## Outcome
A firmware design that is shown to fit within the memory, timing and power limits of the device.

## Purpose
Integrates firmware with the hardware, its peripherals and the other parts of the device. Integration is where assumptions about the hardware are tested against the real device.

## Responsibilities
- Integrate the firmware with the hardware.
- Integrate the firmware with each peripheral.
- Confirm that the firmware and the hardware operate together as designed.

## Outcome
Firmware that operates correctly with the hardware and peripherals of the device.

## Purpose
Verifies that firmware behaves correctly on the device, including its timing and power behaviour. Embedded faults are costly to correct after release, so verification must use the real hardware or an accurate stand-in.

## Responsibilities
- Test the firmware.
- Test the firmware against the hardware using hardware-in-the-loop setups.
- Verify its timing and its power consumption.

## Outcome
Verification results that show whether the firmware meets its functional, timing and power requirements.

## Purpose
Finds and diagnoses faults in firmware while it runs on hardware. Debugging embedded systems requires tools and methods that reach into the running device.

## Responsibilities
- Debug the firmware at runtime.
- Debug faults that arise from the hardware.
- Diagnose the cause of each fault.

## Outcome
Faults in the firmware that have been diagnosed and are ready to correct.

## Purpose
Brings data from its sources into a pipeline. Ingestion is the entry point of every data pipeline and determines the completeness of what follows.

## Responsibilities
- Connect to each data source.
- Extract the data from the sources.
- Ingest the data into the pipeline.

## Outcome
Source data that is available inside the pipeline.

## Purpose
Changes data from the form in which it arrives to the form in which it is needed. Transformation makes data consistent and usable by its consumers.

## Responsibilities
- Transform the data.
- Map the source data to the target structure.
- Normalise the data so that equivalent values have a single form.

## Outcome
Data in the structure and form that consumers require.

## Purpose
Builds data pipelines from their parts and connects them. Construction turns a pipeline design into a working flow of data.

## Responsibilities
- Implement the pipeline.
- Orchestrate the steps of the pipeline.
- Integrate the pipeline with the systems it connects.

## Outcome
A working data pipeline.

## Purpose
Checks that the data flowing through a pipeline is valid and of acceptable quality. Poor data quality spoils everything that is built on the data.

## Responsibilities
- Check data quality.
- Validate the data against its rules.
- Detect anomalies in the data.

## Outcome
Data that has been checked, with quality problems identified.

## Purpose
Operates data pipelines in production by monitoring them, handling their failures and maintaining them. Pipelines must be kept running and correct after they are built.

## Responsibilities
- Monitor the pipeline.
- Handle the failures of the pipeline.
- Maintain the pipeline as sources and needs change.

## Outcome
A pipeline that runs reliably and is kept current.

## Purpose
Identifies the people and groups who are affected by a system or who influence it. A requirement set is only complete when every relevant stakeholder has been found.

## Activities
- Search the organisation, the users and the environment for the parties that have a stake.
- Record each stakeholder together with their relationship to the system.

## Outcome
A list of stakeholders that others can use to plan elicitation.

## Purpose
Draws out requirements and understanding by putting well-chosen questions to people. Questioning exposes needs that stakeholders have not thought to state.

## Activities
- Prepare questions that are open and specific to the topic.
- Ask follow-up questions that clarify answers and record them.

## Outcome
Recorded answers that clarify what stakeholders need.

## Purpose
Discovers the working context, concerns and constraints of each stakeholder. Context explains why a stakeholder needs what they ask for.

## Activities
- Learn how each stakeholder works and what they are accountable for.
- Record the concerns and constraints that shape their needs.

## Outcome
A description of the context of each stakeholder.

## Purpose
Gathers requirements by talking with individual stakeholders. Interviews allow detailed and candid discussion of needs.

## Activities
- Prepare the interview and agree its purpose with the stakeholder.
- Conduct the interview and record what the stakeholder says.

## Outcome
Interview records that state the needs of the stakeholder in their own terms.

## Purpose
Brings stakeholders together to develop and agree requirements. Workshops resolve differences between stakeholders in the room.

## Activities
- Plan the workshop and prepare its structured activities.
- Facilitate the discussion and record the outcomes the group agrees.

## Outcome
Requirements and decisions agreed by the workshop participants.

## Purpose
Learns what users need by watching how they actually work. Observation shows needs that users cannot describe and workarounds they no longer notice.

## Activities
- Observe users carrying out their work in their own setting.
- Record the tasks, difficulties and workarounds that are seen.

## Outcome
Observation notes that describe real working practice.

## Purpose
Writes down requirements as they are elicited. Recording prevents what stakeholders said from being lost or changed.

## Activities
- Record each requirement in a consistent format.
- Confirm the record against what the stakeholder meant.

## Outcome
A recorded set of requirements.

## Purpose
Organises requirements into a coherent structure. A structured set can be reviewed, navigated and analysed.

## Activities
- Group related requirements and arrange them in a hierarchy or other structure.
- Remove duplication and mark requirements that depend on others.

## Outcome
A structured set of requirements.

## Purpose
Records where each requirement came from. A known source allows a requirement to be questioned and kept in step with the source.

## Activities
- Record the stakeholder, document or event from which each requirement came.
- Link the source to the requirement.

## Outcome
Requirements that each carry their source.

## Purpose
Discovers the concepts that the business uses to describe its work. Concepts are the foundation of a domain model.

## Activities
- Study documents, conversations and systems to find the concepts in use.
- List each concept with a short definition.

## Outcome
A list of domain concepts with definitions.

## Purpose
Discovers the terms that the business uses and what they mean. Shared terminology prevents misunderstanding between business and engineering.

## Activities
- Collect the terms used by different groups.
- Note where the same term has different meanings or different terms mean the same thing.

## Outcome
A glossary of the terms in use.

## Purpose
Discovers the entities that the business manages. Entities become the core of the data and structure of a system.

## Activities
- Identify the things the business creates, tracks and relies on.
- Record the attributes that the business uses to describe each entity.

## Outcome
A set of entities with their attributes.

## Purpose
Discovers the processes by which the business achieves its results. Processes show what a system must support.

## Activities
- Identify the activities that make up each process and the order in which they occur.
- Record who performs each activity and what it produces.

## Outcome
A description of each business process as it is performed.

## Purpose
Models the concepts of the domain and the relationships between them. A concept model shows how the business thinks about its work.

## Activities
- Represent each concept in the model.
- Show how the concepts relate to one another.

## Outcome
A concept model of the domain.

## Purpose
Models entities, their attributes and their identity. Entity models become the basis for data structures.

## Activities
- Define each entity with its attributes and identifier.
- Show how entities are grouped and which are variants of others.

## Outcome
An entity model.

## Purpose
Models how entities and components are related, including the nature and the cardinality of each relationship. Relationships determine how parts of a system depend on one another.

## Activities
- Define each relationship and the parties it connects.
- State the cardinality and the meaning of each relationship.

## Outcome
A model of relationships that is consistent with the entities it links.

## Purpose
Models processes as steps, decisions and flows. A process model makes a process precise enough to analyse and to automate.

## Activities
- Represent the steps, decisions and flows of the process.
- Record the participants and the information that each step uses.

## Outcome
A process model.

## Purpose
Models the rules that govern business behaviour. Explicit rules can be checked and implemented consistently.

## Activities
- State each rule precisely and identify what it applies to.
- Show how rules relate to the processes and entities they govern.

## Outcome
A model of the business rules.

## Purpose
Captures knowledge from the people and sources that hold it so that it is not lost. Knowledge that is not captured leaves the organisation when people do.

## Activities
- Gather knowledge from experts, systems and documents.
- Record the knowledge in a form that others can find and use.

## Outcome
Captured knowledge that is available to others.

## Purpose
Records the terms of the domain and their definitions. Captured terminology gives all parties a common vocabulary.

## Activities
- Record each term with its agreed definition.
- Record the synonyms and the contexts in which the term is used.

## Outcome
A maintained glossary.

## Purpose
Captures the rules that the business follows. Rules that are known can be implemented and checked.

## Activities
- Extract each rule from the people, procedures and systems that apply it.
- Record the rule, its source and when it applies.

## Outcome
A recorded set of business rules.

## Purpose
Documents the domain so that engineers can understand it. Domain documentation supports new team members and later change.

## Activities
- Write the description of the domain, its concepts and its processes.
- Keep the documentation consistent with the domain model.

## Outcome
Documentation of the domain.

## Purpose
Confirms that the domain model correctly represents the domain. A model that has not been validated may mislead design.

## Activities
- Walk through the model with domain experts.
- Record the corrections they make and update the model.

## Outcome
A domain model that experts have confirmed.

## Purpose
Confirms that the recorded business rules are correct and current. Rules that are wrong cause a system to behave incorrectly.

## Activities
- Review each rule with the people who own it.
- Check each rule against examples of real behaviour.

## Outcome
Business rules that owners have confirmed.

## Purpose
Confirms that captured domain knowledge is accurate. Validated knowledge can be relied on.

## Activities
- Check the knowledge against its sources and against experts.
- Correct or remove knowledge that is wrong.

## Outcome
Domain knowledge that has been checked.

## Purpose
Examines each requirement to understand it fully. Examination finds ambiguity and omissions at the point where they are cheapest to fix.

## Activities
- Read each requirement closely and note what is unclear.
- Raise questions with the stakeholder who stated it.

## Outcome
Requirements whose meaning has been examined and questioned.

## Purpose
Interprets what a requirement means for the system. Interpretation turns the language of a stakeholder into the language of engineering.

## Activities
- State the intent of the requirement in engineering terms.
- Confirm the interpretation with the stakeholder.

## Outcome
An agreed interpretation of each requirement.

## Purpose
Breaks a requirement into smaller requirements that together satisfy it. Smaller requirements can be allocated, built and verified.

## Activities
- Divide the requirement into parts that are each simpler.
- Check that the parts together cover the original requirement.

## Outcome
A set of detailed requirements that together satisfy the parent requirement.

## Purpose
Makes a requirement more precise and more complete. Refinement removes vagueness so that the requirement can be designed and tested.

## Activities
- Add the detail needed to make the requirement unambiguous.
- Define measurable limits where the requirement is stated loosely.

## Outcome
A requirement that is specific enough to design and verify.

## Purpose
Assigns requirements to the parts of the solution that will satisfy them. Allocation connects requirements to the design.

## Activities
- Choose the component, subsystem or process responsible for each requirement.
- Record the allocation so that it can be traced.

## Outcome
Requirements that are each allocated to a part of the solution.

## Purpose
Analyses what depends on what, so that the effect of change can be understood. Dependencies determine the order of work and the reach of any change.

## Activities
- Identify the dependencies between the items under analysis.
- Analyse the strength and direction of each dependency.

## Outcome
A dependency analysis that shows what is affected by a change.

## Purpose
Analyses the relationships between items such as requirements. Understanding relationships shows how a change in one item affects others.

## Activities
- Identify the relationships between the items.
- Analyse what each relationship means for design and change.

## Outcome
An analysis of the relationships between items.

## Purpose
Analyses where items such as requirements conflict. Conflicts must be resolved or accepted before work proceeds.

## Activities
- Identify items that cannot all be satisfied together.
- Analyse the cause and the consequence of each conflict.

## Outcome
An analysis of conflicts with their causes and consequences.

## Purpose
Represents requirements in a model such as a diagram or a structured notation. Models make requirements more precise and easier to check.

## Activities
- Select the modelling notation that suits the requirements.
- Build the model and check it against the written requirements.

## Outcome
A requirement model.

## Purpose
Represents the constraints that limit a system or its requirements. Modelled constraints can be checked against designs.

## Activities
- Identify the constraints that apply.
- Represent each constraint in the model and link it to what it limits.

## Outcome
A model of the constraints.

## Purpose
Represents the dependencies between requirements. A dependency model shows which requirements must be satisfied before others.

## Activities
- Identify the dependencies between requirements.
- Represent them in a model that shows their direction.

## Outcome
A model of requirement dependencies.

## Purpose
Writes requirements into a precise and testable specification. The specification is the agreed statement of what the system must do.

## Activities
- Write each requirement in a clear and consistent form.
- Organise the requirements into the specification document.

## Outcome
A requirement specification.

## Purpose
Combines requirements from several sources into one coherent set. Consolidation removes duplicates and contradictions.

## Activities
- Merge requirements that say the same thing.
- Resolve or flag requirements that disagree.

## Outcome
A single consolidated set of requirements.

## Purpose
Prepares a set of requirements so that it can be approved as a baseline. A baseline is a stable reference for later change control.

## Activities
- Check that the set is complete, consistent and approved for baselining.
- Identify and version the requirements that are to be baselined.

## Outcome
A requirement set that is ready to be baselined.

## Purpose
Reviews requirements with the people who have an interest in them. Review finds errors before design relies on the requirements.

## Activities
- Present the requirements to the reviewers.
- Record the findings and track their resolution.

## Outcome
Review findings on the requirements.

## Purpose
Confirms that the requirements correctly state what stakeholders need. Validation ensures the right system is specified.

## Activities
- Compare the requirements with the stakeholder needs they came from.
- Record where the requirements fail to reflect those needs.

## Outcome
A validation result for the requirements.

## Purpose
Checks that requirements are acceptable to the stakeholders who must approve them. Acceptance gives the requirements authority.

## Activities
- Present the requirements to the approving stakeholders.
- Record each stakeholder's acceptance or objection.

## Outcome
A record of who has accepted the requirements.

## Purpose
Checks that all that is needed is present. Missing content is hard to see and costly to discover later.

## Activities
- Compare the item against its scope and the expected content.
- List what is absent.

## Outcome
A list of what is missing, or confirmation that nothing is.

## Purpose
Detects requirements that are needed but have not been stated. Missing requirements lead to systems that do not do what is needed.

## Activities
- Compare the requirements with the scope, the processes and the stakeholders.
- Identify needs that no requirement covers.

## Outcome
A list of missing requirements.

## Purpose
Checks that the boundary of the system and the scope of the requirements are clear. A vague boundary leads to disputes about what is included.

## Activities
- Check what is stated to be inside and outside the system.
- Identify requirements that fall in the unclear area.

## Outcome
A confirmed boundary or a list of boundary questions.

## Purpose
Checks that statements do not contradict one another. Inconsistent content cannot all be correct.

## Activities
- Compare statements that concern the same subject.
- List the places where they disagree.

## Outcome
A list of inconsistencies, or confirmation that none was found.

## Purpose
Detects statements that cannot be satisfied together. Conflicts found early are cheaper to resolve.

## Activities
- Compare items that concern the same subject.
- Record every pair or group that cannot all hold.

## Outcome
A list of detected conflicts.

## Purpose
Checks that stated dependencies are valid and consistent. Incorrect dependencies lead to wrong plans and wrong assumptions.

## Activities
- Check that each dependency exists in both directions where it should.
- Check that no dependency is circular or contradictory.

## Outcome
A result that confirms the dependencies or lists the faults.

## Purpose
Assesses whether something can be built with available technology and skills. Technical feasibility reveals requirements that cannot be met as stated.

## Activities
- Assess the technology, skills and time that the requirement needs.
- Identify the requirements that are at risk.

## Outcome
An assessment of what is technically feasible.

## Purpose
Assesses whether something can be operated and supported once it is built. A system that cannot be operated delivers no value.

## Activities
- Assess whether the organisation can run and support what is required.
- Identify the changes in practice that are needed.

## Outcome
An assessment of operational feasibility.

## Purpose
Assesses the constraints that limit what can be done. Constraints define the limits within which a solution must fit.

## Activities
- Identify the constraints of time, cost, technology, policy and law.
- Assess the effect of each constraint on the options.

## Outcome
An assessment of the constraints and their effects.

## Purpose
Checks that a requirement can be shown to be satisfied. A requirement that cannot be verified is a risk.

## Activities
- Check that each requirement can be demonstrated by test, inspection, analysis or demonstration.
- Identify requirements for which no method is possible.

## Outcome
A list of requirements that cannot be verified as stated.

## Purpose
Checks that a requirement can be tested. Testable requirements are stated precisely enough for a test to pass or fail.

## Activities
- Check that the requirement states an observable and measurable result.
- Identify requirements that are too vague to test.

## Outcome
A list of requirements that cannot be tested as stated.

## Purpose
Checks that each requirement has acceptance criteria that are clear and measurable. Criteria define when a requirement is met.

## Activities
- Check that criteria exist for each requirement.
- Check that each criterion is measurable and unambiguous.

## Outcome
Requirements that have acceptable criteria, with those that lack them identified.

## Purpose
Checks that items are traceable to their sources and to what satisfies them. Traceability allows the impact of a change to be found.

## Activities
- Follow the links from each item to its source and to its results.
- Identify items for which a link is missing.

## Outcome
A result that shows how complete traceability is.

## Purpose
Detects the places where traceability links are missing. Gaps show where the lineage of an item cannot be established.

## Activities
- Compare items with the links that exist.
- List the items that lack a link in either direction.

## Outcome
A list of traceability gaps.

## Purpose
Verifies that each requirement matches the source that it traces to. This shows that the requirement has not drifted from its origin.

## Activities
- Compare each requirement with its recorded source.
- Record the requirements that differ from their source.

## Outcome
A verification result linking each requirement to its source.

## Purpose
Models the boundary between a system and its environment. The boundary defines what the system is responsible for.

## Activities
- Identify what lies inside the system and what lies outside it.
- Represent the points at which the system meets its environment.

## Outcome
A model of the system boundary.

## Purpose
Divides a system into smaller parts. Decomposition makes a large system manageable.

## Activities
- Divide the system into parts that have clear purposes.
- Check that the parts together make up the whole system.

## Outcome
A decomposition of the system into parts.

## Purpose
Models the context in which a system operates, including the parties and systems that interact with it. A context model shows the surroundings that shape the system.

## Activities
- Identify the people and systems that interact with the system.
- Show each interaction in the model.

## Outcome
A context model.

## Purpose
Models the components that make up a system. Component models show the building blocks of a design.

## Activities
- Identify each component and its purpose.
- Show the components and their connections in the model.

## Outcome
A component model.

## Purpose
Models the states that something passes through and what causes it to change state. State models make lifecycle behaviour precise.

## Activities
- Define the states and the transitions between them.
- State the events and conditions that cause each transition.

## Outcome
A state model.

## Purpose
Models how parties exchange messages and responses. Interaction models show the dynamic cooperation between parts of a system.

## Activities
- Identify the parties and the messages that pass between them.
- Show the order and conditions of the exchange.

## Outcome
An interaction model.

## Purpose
Finds the dependencies of a design or system. Dependencies need to be known before they can be managed.

## Activities
- Examine the items to find what each relies on.
- Record each dependency with its direction.

## Outcome
A list of dependencies.

## Purpose
Maps the dependencies of a system so that they can be seen as a whole. A map shows chains and clusters that a list hides.

## Activities
- Place each dependency on a map linking the items.
- Highlight chains of dependency and heavily used items.

## Outcome
A dependency map.

## Purpose
Checks that a model is free from contradiction. An inconsistent model cannot be a reliable basis for design.

## Activities
- Check that the elements of the model agree with one another.
- List the contradictions found.

## Outcome
A consistency check result for the model.

## Purpose
Checks that a model covers all that it should. An incomplete model hides parts of the system.

## Activities
- Compare the model with the scope it is meant to cover.
- List the elements that are missing.

## Outcome
A completeness check result for the model.

## Purpose
Checks that a model behaves as the real system should. Validation shows that the model can stand in for the system.

## Activities
- Run or walk through the model with representative cases.
- Compare the behaviour with what is expected.

## Outcome
A validation result for the behaviour of the model.

## Purpose
Defines the structure of an architecture. The structure organises the whole system and guides all later design.

## Activities
- Define the layers, partitions or other structure of the architecture.
- State the rules by which the parts are arranged.

## Outcome
A defined architecture structure.

## Purpose
Defines each architectural component and its purpose. Defined components are the units of design and ownership.

## Activities
- Define each component and what it is responsible for.
- State the interfaces that the component provides and needs.

## Outcome
A definition of each component.

## Purpose
Allocates responsibilities to components so that each has a clear purpose. Clear allocation avoids duplication and gaps.

## Activities
- Assign each responsibility to the component best placed to carry it out.
- Check that no responsibility is left unassigned or assigned twice.

## Outcome
An allocation of responsibilities to components.

## Purpose
Divides components into smaller components. Smaller components are easier to design, build and own.

## Activities
- Divide a component that is too large into cohesive parts.
- Define how the parts work together.

## Outcome
A decomposition of components.

## Purpose
Divides a subsystem into components. Decomposition gives each team a unit of work of manageable size.

## Activities
- Identify the components that make up the subsystem.
- Define the interactions among them.

## Outcome
A decomposition of the subsystem.

## Purpose
Defines the interface through which a component is used. A defined interface lets components be built separately.

## Activities
- Define the operations, data and behaviour that the interface offers.
- State the conditions under which it may be used.

## Outcome
An interface definition.

## Purpose
Defines how components interact. Defined interactions prevent mismatch between components.

## Activities
- Define the sequence of messages and responses between components.
- State what each component guarantees and expects.

## Outcome
An interaction definition.

## Purpose
Defines the points at which a system connects to other systems. Defined boundaries make integration predictable.

## Activities
- Identify each point of integration with an external system.
- Define the data, protocols and responsibilities at each point.

## Outcome
A definition of the integration boundaries.

## Purpose
Evaluates whether an architecture meets its required qualities. Evaluation shows whether the architecture can be relied on.

## Activities
- Assess the architecture against each required quality attribute.
- Record its strengths, risks and weaknesses.

## Outcome
An evaluation of the architecture.

## Purpose
Evaluates alternative options against the criteria that matter. Evaluation supports a reasoned choice between alternatives.

## Activities
- Assess each alternative against the same criteria.
- Compare the results and record the strengths and weaknesses of each.

## Outcome
An evaluation of the alternatives.

## Purpose
Analyses what is gained and lost by each option. Trade-offs are unavoidable and should be made deliberately.

## Activities
- Identify the qualities or goals that conflict between options.
- Analyse the cost to each goal of favouring another.

## Outcome
A trade-off analysis that supports a decision.

## Purpose
Makes planned changes to an architecture. Controlled change keeps the architecture sound.

## Activities
- Define the change and assess its effect on the rest of the architecture.
- Apply the change and update the architecture description.

## Outcome
A changed architecture whose description is current.

## Purpose
Moves a system from one architecture to another. Migration allows an organisation to adopt a better structure without stopping its operation.

## Activities
- Plan the steps by which the system will move to the target architecture.
- Carry out the steps and verify the system at each stage.

## Outcome
A system that has been migrated to the target architecture.

## Purpose
Updates an architecture that has become dated. Modernisation restores the ability to evolve and to use current technology.

## Activities
- Identify the parts of the architecture that are outdated.
- Replace or restructure them in line with current needs.

## Outcome
A modernised architecture.

## Purpose
Analyses the options for an architectural decision. Sound analysis improves the quality of the decision.

## Activities
- Define the decision and the forces that bear on it.
