- Analyse each option against those forces.

## Outcome
An analysis that supports an architectural decision.

## Purpose
Selects the architectural patterns that the design will follow. Proven patterns reduce risk and give a common design vocabulary.

## Activities
- Identify the patterns that address the problem.
- Select the pattern that best fits the forces and record why.

## Outcome
A selected pattern with its rationale.

## Purpose
Resolves constraints that conflict or limit the design. Unresolved constraints block design progress.

## Activities
- Identify the constraints that conflict.
- Decide how to satisfy, relax or trade them off and record the decision.

## Outcome
A resolution of the conflicting constraints.

## Purpose
Builds a component from its design. Construction produces the working parts of the system.

## Activities
- Implement the component according to its design.
- Test the component to confirm it behaves as designed.

## Outcome
A working component.

## Purpose
Builds a feature of a system. A feature delivers a capability that users can see.

## Activities
- Implement the feature across the components it touches.
- Test the feature against its requirements.

## Outcome
A working feature.

## Purpose
Builds the implementation of an interface. A working interface lets components and systems connect.

## Activities
- Implement the operations that the interface defines.
- Test that it behaves as the definition states.

## Outcome
A working interface.

## Purpose
Implements an approved change. Implementation puts the change into effect.

## Activities
- Make the change to the affected items.
- Verify that the change does what was intended and nothing else.

## Outcome
A change that has been implemented.

## Purpose
Maintains a component so that it keeps working. Maintenance preserves the value of the component.

## Activities
- Correct faults and keep the component current with its dependencies.
- Keep the component's documentation and tests up to date.

## Outcome
A component that is maintained.

## Purpose
Develops a component as needs change. Evolution keeps the component fit for purpose.

## Activities
- Plan the changes that the component needs.
- Apply the changes without breaking those who depend on the component.

## Outcome
A component that has evolved to meet new needs.

## Purpose
Protects the design and quality of a component from erosion. Integrity keeps a component understandable and reliable over time.

## Activities
- Review changes to the component against its design.
- Correct changes that undermine its structure or quality.

## Outcome
A component whose integrity is preserved.

## Purpose
Reviews an implementation to see whether it matches its design and requirements. Review finds errors before they reach users.

## Activities
- Read the implementation against the design and requirements.
- Record the differences and defects found.

## Outcome
Review findings on the implementation.

## Purpose
Reviews code for readability, maintainability and adherence to standards. Quality review keeps code easy to change.

## Activities
- Review the code against the coding standards and good practice.
- Record the places that need improvement.

## Outcome
Review findings on code quality.

## Purpose
Identifies defects in work products. Identified defects can be recorded and corrected.

## Activities
- Examine the work product for behaviour or content that is wrong.
- Record each defect with enough detail to correct it.

## Outcome
A list of identified defects.

## Purpose
Combines components so that they work together. Integration shows whether parts developed separately fit.

## Activities
- Assemble the components according to the design.
- Test the combined behaviour.

## Outcome
Components integrated into a working whole.

## Purpose
Connects interfaces between components or systems. Correct connections allow parts to communicate.

## Activities
- Connect each interface to its counterpart.
- Test the exchange across the connection.

## Outcome
Interfaces that are connected and working.

## Purpose
Resolves conflicts that appear when parts are combined. Conflicts left unresolved prevent a system from working as a whole.

## Activities
- Diagnose the cause of each integration conflict.
- Apply and verify a resolution.

## Outcome
Integration conflicts that have been resolved.

## Purpose
Finds the cause of a defect. Diagnosis directs the correction to the right place.

## Activities
- Trace the symptom of the defect back through the system.
- Identify the faulty element and explain why it fails.

## Outcome
A diagnosis of the cause of the defect.

## Purpose
Reproduces a defect reliably. A defect that can be reproduced can be diagnosed and shown to be fixed.

## Activities
- Recreate the conditions under which the defect occurs.
- Record the steps and data needed to reproduce it.

## Outcome
A reliable way to reproduce the defect.

## Purpose
Implements the change that corrects a diagnosed defect. The correction must remove the defect without introducing new ones.

## Activities
- Write the change that removes the cause of the defect.
- Keep the change as small as the cause allows.

## Outcome
A change that corrects the defect.

## Purpose
Verifies that a correction removes the defect and breaks nothing else. Verification is required before a defect can be closed.

## Activities
- Repeat the steps that reproduced the defect and confirm that it no longer occurs.
- Run the related tests to confirm that nothing has regressed.

## Outcome
Evidence that the correction works.

## Purpose
Improves the structure of code while leaving its behaviour unchanged. Better structure makes later change cheaper.

## Activities
- Reorganise code into clearer units with well-defined responsibilities.
- Confirm that the behaviour is the same before and after.

## Outcome
Code with an improved structure and unchanged behaviour.

## Purpose
Reduces the complexity of code. Simple code is easier to understand, test and change.

## Activities
- Replace convoluted logic with simpler equivalent logic.
- Remove code that serves no purpose.

## Outcome
Simpler code that behaves as before.

## Purpose
Removes repeated code by consolidating it in one place. Duplicates drift apart and multiply the cost of change.

## Activities
- Find code that repeats the same logic.
- Replace the copies with a single shared implementation.

## Outcome
Code without needless duplication.

## Purpose
Finds the shortcuts and weaknesses in a system that will make later work harder. Debt that is not identified cannot be managed.

## Activities
- Examine the code, design and tooling for known shortcuts and weaknesses.
- Record each item of debt where it occurs.

## Outcome
A list of identified technical debt.

## Purpose
Assesses how costly and how risky each item of technical debt is. Assessment allows debt to be ranked.

## Activities
- Estimate the cost that each item adds to future work.
- Assess the risk it presents to quality and delivery.

## Outcome
An assessment of each item of debt.

## Purpose
Reduces technical debt by correcting the shortcuts and weaknesses. Reducing debt restores the speed of later change.

## Activities
- Apply the corrective work in the order of priority.
- Record the debt that has been removed and what remains.

## Outcome
A smaller body of technical debt.

## Purpose
Configures how software is built. A configured build is repeatable by anyone.

## Activities
- Define the steps, tools and settings of the build.
- Keep the configuration under version control.

## Outcome
A build configuration that produces the same result each time.

## Purpose
Translates source code into executable form. Compilation is the first check that the code is well formed.

## Activities
- Compile the source code using the configured build.
- Resolve the errors and warnings that the compiler reports.

## Outcome
Compiled code that is ready to be packaged.

## Purpose
Determines and obtains the dependencies that a build needs. Correct resolution ensures that the build uses the right versions.

## Activities
- Identify each dependency and the version that is required.
- Obtain the dependencies from their sources and verify them.

## Outcome
Resolved dependencies that make the build repeatable.

## Purpose
Assembles built output into a package that can be deployed. A package contains everything needed to install the software.

## Activities
- Gather the compiled output, resources and metadata.
- Create the package in the agreed format and give it a version.

## Outcome
A deployable package.

## Purpose
Automates repetitive tasks in the development process. Automation saves effort and removes error.

## Activities
- Identify manual tasks that engineers repeat.
- Build scripts and tools that carry them out.

## Outcome
Automated development tasks.

## Purpose
Provides small tools that help developers in their daily work. Utilities remove friction from development.

## Activities
- Provide the tools that developers ask for or need.
- Document and maintain the tools so that others can use them.

## Outcome
Utilities that developers can use.

## Purpose
Produces code automatically from models, templates or specifications. Generation gives consistent code and saves effort.

## Activities
- Define the source and the rules from which code is produced.
- Generate the code and check that it meets the standards of handwritten code.

## Outcome
Generated code.

## Purpose
Provides and supports the environments in which developers work. A reliable environment lets engineers focus on their tasks.

## Activities
- Set up the environment with the tools and access that developers need.
- Help developers resolve problems with their environments.

## Outcome
A working development environment.

## Purpose
Identifies the components that a design needs. Identification is the first step in splitting a design into parts.

## Activities
- Examine the requirements and architecture to find coherent units of function.
- Name and describe each component.

## Outcome
A list of components.

## Purpose
Designs the external structure of a component. A clear structure shows how the component is used and what it contains.

## Activities
- Define the parts of the component that other components see.
- Define how the component is organised.

## Outcome
A design of the structure of the component.

## Purpose
Designs the internal structure of a component. A sound internal structure keeps the component easy to change.

## Activities
- Define the internal parts of the component and how they cooperate.
- Allocate responsibilities among them.

## Outcome
A design of the internal structure of the component.

## Purpose
Designs how a component behaves. Behaviour design states what the component does in response to requests and events.

## Activities
- Define how the component responds to each request and event.
- Define the handling of errors and exceptional situations.

## Outcome
A design of the behaviour of the component.

## Purpose
Designs the contract that an interface offers and expects. A contract states each party's obligations.

## Activities
- State the conditions that callers must meet and the results that the provider guarantees.
- State how errors are reported.

## Outcome
An interface contract.

## Purpose
Designs the way that users or components interact. Good interaction design makes use simple and error-resistant.

## Activities
- Design the sequence of steps and responses in each interaction.
- Check that the design handles the cases that can go wrong.

## Outcome
An interaction design.

## Purpose
Defines the dependencies that a component has. Defined dependencies are explicit and can be managed.

## Activities
- Define each element on which the component relies and why.
- State the nature of each dependency.

## Outcome
A definition of the dependencies of the component.

## Purpose
Defines the rules that limit the dependencies between components. Constraints keep coupling under control.

## Activities
- State which dependencies are allowed and which are forbidden.
- Record the rule so that it can be checked.

## Outcome
A set of dependency constraints.

## Purpose
Checks that the parts of a design agree with one another. An inconsistent design cannot be implemented correctly.

## Activities
- Compare the parts of the design that concern the same subject.
- Record the inconsistencies found.

## Outcome
A consistency check result for the design.

## Purpose
Checks that requirements allocated to a component are fully addressed by its design. This shows that the design satisfies what was asked of it.

## Activities
- Compare the requirements assigned to the component with its design.
- Record any requirement that the design does not address.

## Outcome
A result that shows whether the design addresses its requirements.

## Purpose
Checks that a design follows the architecture. Conformance keeps the system coherent.

## Activities
- Compare the design with the rules and structure of the architecture.
- Record each departure from the architecture.

## Outcome
A conformance result for the design.

## Purpose
Identifies the items that will be placed under configuration control. Identification sets the scope of configuration management.

## Activities
- Select the items that need version and change control.
- Give each item a unique identity.

## Outcome
A list of configuration items.

## Purpose
Defines how configuration items are organised and related. Structure shows what belongs to what.

## Activities
- Define how items group into larger items.
- Define the relationships between items.

## Outcome
A defined configuration structure.

## Purpose
Defines the attributes that describe each configuration item. Attributes make items searchable and comparable.

## Activities
- Select the attributes that every item needs, such as version, owner and status.
- Define the permitted values of each attribute.

## Outcome
A definition of configuration attributes.

## Purpose
Creates a new version of a configuration item. Versions record each stage in the evolution of an item.

## Activities
- Assign the next version identifier according to the versioning rules.
- Record the content and the reason for the version.

## Outcome
A new version of the item.

## Purpose
Tracks the versions of items over time. Tracking shows which version is current and how versions relate.

## Activities
- Record each version with its date, author and predecessor.
- Keep the history available for comparison.

## Outcome
A tracked version history.

## Purpose
Manages the branches in which parallel work is done. Branches let teams work without disturbing one another.

## Activities
- Create and name branches according to the agreed strategy.
- Close branches that are no longer needed.

## Outcome
Branches that are organised and controlled.

## Purpose
Manages the merging of work from one branch into another. Controlled merging keeps parallel work consistent.

## Activities
- Plan and perform each merge in the agreed order.
- Resolve the conflicts that appear and check the result.

## Outcome
Merged work that is consistent.

## Purpose
Creates a baseline that fixes the state of a set of items. A baseline provides a stable reference point.

## Activities
- Select the versions of the items that make up the baseline.
- Record and identify the baseline.

## Outcome
A baseline.

## Purpose
Keeps baselines accurate as approved changes are made. A baseline that is maintained remains a valid reference.

## Activities
- Update baselines when approved changes are made.
- Keep a record of each change to the baseline.

## Outcome
Baselines that remain current.

## Purpose
Compares the current state with a baseline or one baseline with another. Comparison shows what has changed.

## Activities
- Compare the items in each baseline.
- List the differences.

## Outcome
A list of the differences between baselines.

## Purpose
Restores the state recorded by a baseline. Restoration returns to a known good state.

## Activities
- Retrieve the items in the selected baseline.
- Restore them to their working locations and verify the result.

## Outcome
A restored baseline.

## Purpose
Records each change that is made. A record shows who changed what and why.

## Activities
- Record the change, the author, the date and the reason.
- Link the record to the items affected.

## Outcome
A record of the change.

## Purpose
Associates changes with the configuration items they affect. Association shows the effect of each change.

## Activities
- Link each change to the items that it modifies.
- Keep the link available for later analysis.

## Outcome
Changes that are linked to the items they affect.

## Purpose
Keeps the history of changes made to an item. History explains how an item reached its current state.

## Activities
- Maintain the sequence of changes for each item.
- Make the history searchable.

## Outcome
A history of changes.

## Purpose
Records the status of each configuration item. Status shows whether an item is draft, approved or released.

## Activities
- Record the current status of each item.
- Update it when the status changes.

## Outcome
A record of configuration status.

## Purpose
Reports the status of versions. Reports show which versions are in use and which are approved.

## Activities
- Collect the status of each version.
- Present the status in a report for those who need it.

## Outcome
A report on the status of versions.

## Purpose
Reports the status of baselines. Reports show what has been baselined and what has changed since.

## Activities
- Collect the status of each baseline and its changes.
- Present the information in a report.

## Outcome
A report on the status of baselines.

## Purpose
Compares configurations to find differences. Comparison shows whether two configurations are equivalent.

## Activities
- Compare the items and settings of each configuration.
- List the differences.

## Outcome
A list of differences between configurations.

## Purpose
Checks that a configuration is complete and uncorrupted. Integrity shows that the configuration is what it claims to be.

## Activities
- Check that every expected item is present and unchanged.
- Report any item that is missing or altered.

## Outcome
An integrity result for the configuration.

## Purpose
Checks that a configuration can be rebuilt from its records. Reproducibility ensures that a past state can be recreated.

## Activities
- Rebuild the configuration from its recorded items.
- Compare the rebuilt result with the original.

## Outcome
A result that shows whether the configuration can be reproduced.

## Purpose
Defines what will be verified. A clear scope focuses effort and avoids gaps.

## Activities
- State the items and behaviours that verification covers.
- State what is outside the scope.

## Outcome
A defined verification scope.

## Purpose
Defines the criteria by which verification will succeed or fail. Criteria make the verdict objective.

## Activities
- State the conditions that must hold for each item to pass.
- Make each criterion measurable.

## Outcome
Verification criteria.

## Purpose
Plans the verification activities. A plan organises the work, the people and the schedule of verification.

## Activities
- Define the activities, resources and schedule.
- Assign responsibility for each activity.

## Outcome
A verification plan.

## Purpose
Designs scenarios that exercise the system in realistic situations. Scenarios test how the parts work together.

## Activities
- Define each scenario in terms of context, actions and expected results.
- Select scenarios that cover the important uses of the system.

## Outcome
A set of test scenarios.

## Purpose
Designs individual tests with their inputs and expected results. Each case checks one specific behaviour.

## Activities
- Define the inputs, conditions and expected result of each case.
- Select cases that cover the requirements and the risks.

## Outcome
A set of test cases.

## Purpose
Designs the data that tests need. Suitable data lets tests exercise normal, boundary and error conditions.

## Activities
- Define the data required by each test.
- Define how the data is created and kept up to date.

## Outcome
A design for the test data.

## Purpose
Runs tests and observes the results. Execution produces the evidence of how the system behaves.

## Activities
- Run each test as designed in the prepared environment.
- Record whether each test passed or failed.

## Outcome
Executed tests with recorded outcomes.

## Purpose
Records the results of testing. Recorded results can be analysed and audited.

## Activities
- Record the outcome of every test with the evidence of what happened.
- Store the results where they can be retrieved.

## Outcome
Captured test results.

## Purpose
Runs tests again after a correction. Retesting confirms that a fix works and that nothing else broke.

## Activities
- Run the tests that failed and the tests that could be affected.
- Record the new results.

## Outcome
Retest results.

## Purpose
Writes tests that run without manual effort. Automated tests can be repeated often at low cost.

## Activities
- Write scripts that carry out the designed tests and check the results.
- Keep the scripts readable and under version control.

## Outcome
Automated tests.

## Purpose
Runs automated tests as part of the development process. Frequent execution gives early warning of defects.

## Activities
- Run the automated tests at the agreed points in the process.
- Collect and report the results.

## Outcome
Results of automated test runs.

## Purpose
Keeps automated tests working as the system changes. Tests that are not maintained become unreliable.

## Activities
- Update the tests when the system changes.
- Remove or repair tests that fail for reasons other than defects.

## Outcome
Automated tests that remain reliable.

## Purpose
Detects when a system fails to behave as required. Detection begins the process of correction.

## Activities
- Observe the system for behaviour that departs from the requirements.
- Record each failure with the circumstances.

## Outcome
A record of detected failures.

## Purpose
Measures the quality of the system or its products. Measurement turns quality into numbers that can be tracked.

## Activities
- Select the measures that reflect the quality goals.
- Take the measurements and record them.

## Outcome
Quality measurements.

## Purpose
Collects the metrics that describe quality. Regular collection reveals trends.

## Activities
- Gather metrics from tools, tests and reviews.
- Store them in a consistent form.

## Outcome
A body of quality metrics.

## Purpose
Analyses quality results to understand what they show. Analysis turns data into conclusions and action.

## Activities
- Examine the results for trends and outliers.
- State what the results mean for quality.

## Outcome
An analysis of quality results.

## Purpose
Documents the technical aspects of a system. Technical documentation allows the system to be understood and used.

## Activities
- Describe the structure, behaviour and use of the system.
- Write for the engineers who will use the documentation.

## Outcome
Technical documentation.

## Purpose
Documents the design of a system. Design documentation explains how the system is built and why.

## Activities
- Describe the architecture, the components and the decisions behind them.
- Keep the description consistent with the actual design.

## Outcome
Design documentation.

## Purpose
Documents how a system is implemented. This helps engineers who must maintain the code.

## Activities
- Describe the structure of the code and its important mechanisms.
- Explain choices that are not obvious from the code.

## Outcome
Implementation documentation.

## Purpose
Documents how a system is operated. Operators rely on it to run, monitor and recover the system.

## Activities
- Describe the procedures for deployment, monitoring and recovery.
- State what to do when problems arise.

## Outcome
Operational documentation.

## Purpose
Writes the content of documents. Clear content is the purpose of all documentation.

## Activities
- Draft the content for the intended reader.
- Revise it until it is accurate and clear.

## Outcome
Authored content.

## Purpose
Explains technical subjects clearly to the reader. Good explanation makes difficult subjects understandable.

## Activities
- Explain the subject at a level suited to the reader.
- Use examples and diagrams where they help.

## Outcome
A clear technical explanation.

## Purpose
Writes procedures that can be followed. A good procedure lets a reader perform a task correctly.

## Activities
- Write the steps of the task in the order they are performed.
- Test the procedure by following it.

## Outcome
A procedure that can be followed.

## Purpose
Updates content so that it stays correct. Content that is out of date misleads readers.

## Activities
- Revise the content when the thing it describes changes.
- Record the change and the date.

## Outcome
Updated content.

## Purpose
Keeps documentation consistent with the system it describes. Synchronisation prevents drift.

## Activities
- Compare the documentation with the current state of the system.
- Correct the documentation where they differ.

## Outcome
Documentation that matches the system.

## Purpose
Removes content that is no longer valid. Removing obsolete content stops readers from relying on it.

## Activities
- Identify content that describes things that no longer exist or apply.
- Remove it or mark it clearly as obsolete.

## Outcome
Documentation without obsolete content.

## Purpose
Checks that content is factually correct. Accuracy protects readers from errors.

## Activities
- Compare the content with the system or source that it describes.
- Record and correct the errors found.

## Outcome
Content that has been checked for accuracy.

## Purpose
Organises information so that readers can find it. Organisation turns a collection of items into a usable resource.

## Activities
- Group related information and arrange it logically.
- Provide the navigation that readers need.

## Outcome
Information that is organised.

## Purpose
Classifies content by type, subject and audience. Classification supports searching and control of content.

## Activities
- Assign each item of content to the agreed categories.
- Keep the classification consistent.

## Outcome
Classified content.

## Purpose
Links related content to one another. Cross-references let readers move to related information.

## Activities
- Identify content that relates to other content.
- Add links or references between them.

## Outcome
Content that is cross-referenced.

## Purpose
Identifies assets so that they can be managed or protected. An asset that is not identified cannot be managed.

## Activities
- Find the assets within the scope.
- Record each asset with its owner and description.

## Outcome
A list of identified assets.

## Purpose
Classifies assets by their value and sensitivity. Classification determines the protection each asset needs.

## Activities
- Assign each asset a class according to the classification scheme.
- Record the reason for the class.

## Outcome
Classified assets.

## Purpose
Identifies the protection that each asset requires. Requirements make protection effort proportionate to the asset.

## Activities
- Determine the protection needed for each class of asset.
- Record the requirements.

## Outcome
A statement of the protection each asset requires.

## Purpose
Controls who can reach resources. Access control protects resources from unauthorised use.

## Activities
- Define the rules that allow or deny access.
- Apply the rules in the systems that hold the resources.

## Outcome
Controlled access to resources.

## Purpose
Manages the permissions that people and systems hold. Managed permissions give each party only the access it needs.

## Activities
- Grant, change and remove permissions as roles change.
- Review permissions regularly.

## Outcome
Permissions that are appropriate and current.

## Purpose
Protects the process by which identities are proven. Protected authentication prevents impersonation.

## Activities
- Apply strong methods of proving identity.
- Guard against attacks on credentials and sessions.

## Outcome
Authentication that resists attack.

## Purpose
Enforces what each authenticated party may do. Enforcement ensures that rules are followed in practice.

## Activities
- Check each request against the permissions of the requester.
- Refuse and record requests that are not permitted.

## Outcome
Authorisation that is enforced.

## Purpose
Classifies data by its sensitivity. Classification tells people how the data must be handled.

## Activities
- Assign each data set a class using the classification scheme.
- Label the data so that its class is visible.

## Outcome
Classified data.

## Purpose
Protects data against unauthorised access, loss and alteration. Protection preserves confidentiality, integrity and availability.

## Activities
- Apply the controls that the classification of the data requires.
- Check that the controls work.

## Outcome
Protected data.

## Purpose
Encrypts data so that it cannot be read by unauthorised parties. Encryption protects data at rest and in transit.

## Activities
- Select the encryption methods and manage the keys.
- Apply encryption to the data that requires it.

## Outcome
Encrypted data.

## Purpose
Defines and applies the rules for how data is used, stored and shared. Correct handling prevents misuse and leakage.

## Activities
- Define the handling rules for each class of data.
- Apply the rules in procedures and systems.

## Outcome
Data that is handled according to its class.

## Purpose
Identifies weaknesses that could be exploited. A weakness that is not found cannot be corrected.

## Activities
- Examine systems and code for known and new weaknesses.
- Record each vulnerability with where it occurs.

## Outcome
A list of vulnerabilities.

## Purpose
Assesses how serious each vulnerability is. Assessment decides which vulnerabilities to fix first.

## Activities
- Assess the severity and the ease of exploitation of each vulnerability.
- Assess the impact if it were exploited.

## Outcome
An assessment of each vulnerability.

## Purpose
Tracks vulnerabilities until they are resolved. Tracking ensures that none is forgotten.

## Activities
- Record the status of each vulnerability.
- Report on what remains open.

## Outcome
A record of the status of vulnerabilities.

## Purpose
Fixes or reduces the risk from a weakness. Remediation closes the gap that an attacker could use.

## Activities
- Apply the fix, patch or compensating control.
- Verify that the weakness no longer exists.

## Outcome
A weakness that has been remediated.

## Purpose
Identifies the threats that could harm a system. Threats must be known before defences are chosen.

## Activities
- Examine the system, its data and its environment for sources of harm.
- Record each threat and what it targets.

## Outcome
A list of threats.

## Purpose
Analyses the nature and likelihood of threats. Analysis shows which threats require attention.

## Activities
- Analyse how each threat could be carried out.
- Assess the likelihood and the consequence of each threat.

## Outcome
An analysis of threats.

## Purpose
Analyses how exposed an asset or system is to harm. Exposure shows where harm could reach.

## Activities
- Identify the paths by which harm could reach the asset.
- Assess how open each path is.

## Outcome
An analysis of exposure.

## Purpose
Watches systems for signs of attack or misuse. Monitoring allows a timely response.

## Activities
- Collect and examine security events.
- Raise alerts for activity that suggests an attack.

## Outcome
Security monitoring that detects attacks.

## Purpose
Monitors that protective controls are in place and working. A control that has failed gives false assurance.

## Activities
- Check the state of each control at regular intervals.
- Report any control that has failed or been disabled.

## Outcome
Confirmation that protection controls are operating.

## Purpose
Assesses whether protection is effective against the threats it addresses. Assessment shows where protection must improve.

## Activities
- Compare the controls with the threats they are meant to stop.
- Test the controls and record how well they work.

## Outcome
An assessment of the effectiveness of protection.

## Purpose
Defines the problem that a decision must solve. A clear definition ensures that the right question is answered.

## Activities
- State the problem, its context and the outcome that is needed.
- Agree the definition with those affected.

## Outcome
A defined decision problem.

## Purpose
Analyses the options available for a decision. Analysis shows what each option involves and implies.

## Activities
- Describe each option and what it would take to carry out.
- Analyse its benefits, costs and risks.

## Outcome
An analysis of the options.

## Purpose
Analyses what would follow from a decision or a risk if it came about. Understanding consequences allows the options to be compared honestly.

## Activities
- Trace the effects of the decision or event on the people, systems and goals involved.
- Distinguish the immediate consequences from those that appear later.

## Outcome
An analysis of the consequences.

## Purpose
Evaluates options against the criteria that were set for the decision. Criteria make the choice transparent and defensible.

## Activities
- Apply each criterion to each option using the available evidence.
- Record the result and the reasoning for each judgement.

## Outcome
A decision evaluation against the agreed criteria.

## Purpose
Evaluates the quality, relevance and consistency of evidence. Reasoning and compliance are only as sound as the evidence on which they rest.

## Activities
- Assess each piece of evidence for its reliability and its relevance to the question.
- Check whether the evidence is consistent with other evidence.

## Outcome
An evaluation that states how far the evidence can be trusted.

## Purpose
Establishes who has the authority to take a decision. A decision taken without authority may be invalid.

## Activities
- Identify the role or body that holds authority for the decision.
- Check that the decision falls within the limits of that authority.

## Outcome
A statement of who may decide.

## Purpose
Obtains and records the approval of a decision by those with authority. Approval makes a decision binding.

## Activities
- Present the decision and its supporting analysis to the approver.
- Record who approved it and when.

## Outcome
An approved decision.

## Purpose
Refers a decision to a higher authority when it exceeds the authority of the original decision maker. Escalation ensures that significant decisions reach the right level.

## Activities
- Identify decisions that exceed the available authority.
- Pass them to the appropriate authority with the necessary information.

## Outcome
A decision that has been escalated.

## Purpose
Records a decision when it is made. Capture preserves what was decided for the future.

## Activities
- Record what was decided and by whom.
- Record the date and the matters it concerned.

## Outcome
A recorded decision.

## Purpose
Records the reasons for a decision. Rationale lets others understand why a choice was made.

## Activities
- Record the reasoning, the alternatives considered and the factors that decided the matter.
- Link the rationale to the decision.

## Outcome
A recorded rationale.

## Purpose
Records the circumstances in which a decision was made. Context allows the decision to be judged fairly later.

## Activities
- Record the constraints, assumptions and objectives that applied at the time.
- Link the context to the decision.

## Outcome
A recorded decision context.

## Purpose
Links a decision to the evidence that supports it. Links let anyone check what a decision rests on.

## Activities
- Identify the evidence that was used.
- Create the link between the decision and each item of evidence.

## Outcome
A decision linked to its evidence.

## Purpose
Links a decision to the requirements it affects or satisfies. Links show how decisions connect to what the system must do.

## Activities
- Identify the requirements that the decision addresses.
- Create the link between the decision and each requirement.

## Outcome
A decision linked to its requirements.

## Purpose
Tracks the history of a decision, including its revisions and supersession. History shows how thinking changed.

## Activities
- Record each change, revision and replacement of the decision.
- Keep the sequence available for review.

## Outcome
A history of the decision.

## Purpose
Reconsiders a decision in the light of new information. Reassessment keeps decisions current.

## Activities
- Examine whether the facts behind the decision have changed.
- Decide whether the decision should stand or be revised.

## Outcome
A reassessed decision.

## Purpose
Reviews what resulted from a decision. Review shows whether the decision achieved its aim.

## Activities
- Compare the actual outcome with the outcome that was expected.
- Record the lessons for future decisions.

## Outcome
A review of the outcome.

## Purpose
Reviews whether a decision still holds. Circumstances change and a decision may no longer be valid.

## Activities
- Check the assumptions of the decision against the current situation.
- Record whether the decision remains valid.

## Outcome
A validity review of the decision.

## Purpose
Defines what a release will contain. A defined scope gives the release a clear boundary.

## Activities
- Select the features, fixes and changes that are included.
- Record what is excluded.

## Outcome
A defined release scope.

## Purpose
Sets when a release will take place. A schedule lets everyone plan around the release.

## Activities
- Choose the dates for each stage of the release.
- Coordinate the dates with the teams and systems affected.

## Outcome
A release schedule.

## Purpose
Analyses what a release depends on and what depends on it. Unseen dependencies are a common cause of release failure.

## Activities
- Identify the other releases, systems and teams that the release relies on.
- Determine the order and conditions that this imposes.

## Outcome
An analysis of release dependencies.

## Purpose
Prepares everything that is needed for a release to go ahead. Preparation reduces the risk of last-minute failure.

## Activities
- Check that the work, tests, approvals and documentation required for the release are complete.
- Resolve outstanding issues or record why they are accepted.

## Outcome
A release that is ready to proceed.

## Purpose
Configures the release for its target environment. Correct configuration ensures that the release behaves as intended once deployed.

## Activities
- Define the settings that the release needs in each environment.
- Verify that the settings are correct.

## Outcome
A configured release.

## Purpose
Prepares the environments and the procedures for deployment. Preparation makes deployment predictable.

## Activities
- Prepare the target environment and the deployment steps.
- Agree the plan for deployment and for rollback.

## Outcome
A deployment that is ready to be carried out.

## Purpose
Assembles the build that will be released. The released build must be the one that was tested.

## Activities
- Assemble the build from the approved versions of its components.
- Record what the build contains.

## Outcome
An assembled build.

## Purpose
Creates the package in which a release is delivered. A package makes a release easy to transport and install.

## Activities
- Package the build with its installation instructions and metadata.
- Verify that the package is complete.

## Outcome
A release package.

## Purpose
Gathers the artifacts that a release needs. A release is complete only when all its artifacts are present.

## Activities
- Collect the files, images and documents that belong to the release.
- Check each against the release contents.

## Outcome
An assembled set of release artifacts.

## Purpose
Verifies that a release is correct. Verification confirms that the release contains what it should and works.

## Activities
- Check the release against its definition and its test results.
- Record any discrepancy.

## Outcome
A verified release.

## Purpose
Tests a release to confirm that it is acceptable to those who will use it. Acceptance testing gives confidence before the release is deployed.

## Activities
- Run the acceptance tests in an environment that resembles production.
- Record whether each acceptance criterion is met.

## Outcome
Acceptance test results for the release.

## Purpose
Validates that a deployment has worked. Validation shows that the release is running as expected.

## Activities
- Check the deployed system against the expected state and behaviour.
- Record any difference and its significance.

## Outcome
A validated deployment.

## Purpose
Carries out the deployment of a release. Execution puts the release into the target environment.

## Activities
- Run the deployment steps according to the plan.
- Record what was done and any deviation.

## Outcome
A deployed release.

## Purpose
Moves a release from one environment to the next. Promotion takes a release toward production in controlled stages.

## Activities
- Release the package into the next environment in the sequence.
- Confirm that it behaves correctly before moving further.

## Outcome
A release promoted to the next environment.

## Purpose
Verifies a deployment after it has been carried out. Verification confirms that the correct version is running correctly.

## Activities
- Check the version, configuration and basic function of the deployed release.
- Record the result.

## Outcome
A verified deployment.

## Purpose
Tracks the status of each release. Tracking shows where a release stands in its lifecycle.

## Activities
- Record the stage and state of each release.
- Report the status to those who need it.

## Outcome
Current release status.

## Purpose
Tracks where each release is deployed. Tracking shows what is running in each environment.

## Activities
- Record the deployments of each release by environment and time.
- Keep the record current.

## Outcome
A record of deployments.

## Purpose
Tracks the results of a release after it is made. Tracking shows whether a release met its purpose.

## Activities
- Record the incidents, issues and usage that follow the release.
- Compare them with what was expected.

## Outcome
A record of the outcome of the release.

## Purpose
Monitors the condition of a system. Monitoring shows how the system behaves in operation.

## Activities
- Collect measures of the activity and condition of the system.
- Present them so that problems are seen quickly.

## Outcome
Monitoring of the system.

## Purpose
Monitors the services that a system provides. Service monitoring shows whether users are being served.

## Activities
- Measure the availability and response of each service.
- Report services that are not meeting expectations.

## Outcome
Monitoring of services.

## Purpose
Monitors the events that a system generates. Events record what has happened and reveal problems.

## Activities
- Collect and examine the events produced by the system.
- Raise attention for events that need action.

## Outcome
Monitoring of events.

## Purpose
Monitors whether a system is healthy. Health monitoring gives early warning of failure.

## Activities
- Check that the system's components are running and responding.
- Report components that are unhealthy.

## Outcome
Monitoring of health.

## Purpose
Schedules the regular tasks of operation. A schedule ensures that routine tasks are done on time.

## Activities
- Define when each operational task is to run.
- Coordinate the schedule so that tasks do not conflict.

## Outcome
An operational schedule.

## Purpose
Carries out the regular tasks that keep a system running. Routine operation is the daily work of keeping the service available.

## Activities
- Perform the standard operating tasks according to procedure.
- Record what was done and any problem found.

## Outcome
Routine operations carried out.

## Purpose
Maintains the operational condition of a system. Maintenance prevents decline in the service.

## Activities
- Perform housekeeping such as patching, cleaning and housekeeping of data.
- Check the system afterwards.

## Outcome
A system that is maintained.

## Purpose
Monitors how well something performs against its targets. Monitoring shows when performance falls below what is needed.

## Activities
- Collect the measures of performance.
- Compare them with the targets.

## Outcome
Performance monitoring.

## Purpose
Analyses performance measurements to understand their causes. Analysis shows where and why performance is limited.

## Activities
- Examine the measurements for trends, peaks and limits.
- Identify the factors that influence performance.

## Outcome
An analysis of performance.

## Purpose
Adjusts a system to improve its performance. Tuning makes better use of resources.

## Activities
- Identify the changes most likely to improve performance.
- Apply them and measure the result.

## Outcome
Improved performance.

## Purpose
Monitors how much of the available capacity is used. Monitoring shows how close the system is to its limits.

## Activities
- Measure the use of processing, storage and network capacity.
- Report the trend.

## Outcome
Capacity monitoring.

## Purpose
Analyses capacity use and the demands made on it. Analysis shows whether capacity is adequate.

## Activities
- Examine how demand and capacity relate over time.
- Identify the resources that will run short.

## Outcome
An analysis of capacity.

## Purpose
Forecasts the capacity that will be needed. Forecasts let capacity be added before it is short.

## Activities
- Project demand using trends and planned change.
- Translate the demand into the capacity required.

## Outcome
A capacity forecast.

## Purpose
Monitors whether services are available. Monitoring shows when users cannot use the service.

## Activities
- Check the availability of each service at regular intervals.
- Record the periods of unavailability.

## Outcome
Availability monitoring.

## Purpose
Analyses the availability that has been achieved. Analysis reveals the causes of lost availability.

## Activities
- Examine the outages and their causes.
- Compare the availability achieved with the target.

## Outcome
An analysis of availability.

## Purpose
Improves the availability of services. Improvement reduces the time that users cannot use the service.

## Activities
- Identify changes that would prevent or shorten outages.
- Apply the changes and check their effect.

## Outcome
Improved availability.

## Purpose
Handles issues that arise during operation. Prompt handling limits the effect on users.

## Activities
- Receive and assess the issue.
- Resolve it or pass it to those who can.

## Outcome
An operational issue that has been handled.

## Purpose
Restores a service that has been interrupted. Restoration returns users to a working service as quickly as possible.

## Activities
- Apply the quickest safe action that brings the service back.
- Confirm that the service is working.

## Outcome
A restored service.

## Purpose
Assists people who operate or use a system. Assistance helps them to complete their work.

## Activities
- Answer questions and give guidance on the system.
- Record recurring needs for improvement.

## Outcome
Assistance given to operators and users.

## Purpose
Finds where knowledge is held. Sources must be known before knowledge can be recovered.

## Activities
- Search the organisation for people, documents and systems that hold relevant knowledge.
- Record each source and what it holds.

## Outcome
A list of knowledge sources.

## Purpose
Finds the records of past work. Historical evidence shows what happened and why.

## Activities
- Search archives, repositories and records for evidence about past work.
- Record what each item shows.

## Outcome
A set of historical evidence.

## Purpose
Retrieves knowledge from its sources. Retrieval makes the knowledge available for use.

## Activities
- Obtain the relevant knowledge from each source.
- Record where it came from.

## Outcome
Retrieved knowledge.

## Purpose
Extracts structured information from unstructured material. Extraction turns documents and records into usable facts.

## Activities
- Read the material and identify the facts it contains.
- Record the facts in a structured form.

## Outcome
Extracted information.

## Purpose
Extracts the concepts that appear in material. Concepts are the vocabulary of the knowledge.

## Activities
- Identify the concepts used in the material.
- Define each and record it.

## Outcome
Extracted concepts.

## Purpose
Extracts the rules that are stated or implied in material. Extracted rules can be compared and checked.

## Activities
- Identify statements that impose obligations or conditions.
- Record each rule with its source.

## Outcome
Extracted rules.

## Purpose
Extracts the relationships between things. Relationships show how knowledge connects.

## Activities
- Identify how the concepts or entities in the material are related.
- Record each relationship with its type and direction.

## Outcome
Extracted relationships.

## Purpose
Reconstructs a process from the evidence of how it was carried out. Reconstruction recovers a process that was never documented.

## Activities
- Examine the records and artefacts to infer the steps taken.
- Describe the process and its order.

## Outcome
A reconstructed process.

## Purpose
Reconstructs the architecture of a system from its implementation. A recovered architecture lets the system be understood and changed.

## Activities
- Examine the code, configuration and runtime to find the components and connections.
- Describe the architecture that they imply.

## Outcome
A reconstructed architecture.

## Purpose
Reconstructs how a system behaves. Behaviour is often the least documented aspect of a system.

## Activities
- Examine the code, the data and the runtime to establish what the system does.
- Describe the behaviour in terms the business can check.

## Outcome
A reconstructed account of behaviour.

## Purpose
Reconstructs a decision that was taken without a record. Understanding past decisions helps to avoid repeating them or reversing them blindly.

## Activities
- Gather the evidence that shows what was decided and the circumstances.
- Infer the options and the rationale and record them as inferred.

## Outcome
A reconstructed decision.

## Purpose
Checks that evidence is genuine and sufficient. Validated evidence can be relied on.

## Activities
- Check where the evidence came from and whether it has been altered.
- Check that it supports the conclusion drawn from it.

## Outcome
Validated evidence.

## Purpose
Checks that items of knowledge do not contradict one another. Contradiction signals error.

## Activities
- Compare items of knowledge that concern the same subject.
- Record the contradictions.

## Outcome
A consistency check of the knowledge.

## Purpose
Checks that knowledge is correct. Accurate knowledge can be used with confidence.

## Activities
- Compare the knowledge with its sources and with those who know the subject.
- Correct or flag errors.

## Outcome
Knowledge that has been checked for accuracy.

## Purpose
Classifies knowledge by type and subject. Classification helps people find what they need.

## Activities
- Assign each item of knowledge to categories of the agreed scheme.
- Keep the scheme applied consistently.

## Outcome
Classified knowledge.

## Purpose
Represents knowledge in a model. A model shows the structure of the knowledge and allows it to be reasoned about.

## Activities
- Define the types of knowledge and the relationships between them.
- Populate the model with the knowledge that has been recovered.

## Outcome
A model of the knowledge.

## Purpose
Arranges knowledge so that it can be navigated. Organisation makes a body of knowledge usable.

## Activities
- Arrange related knowledge together under clear headings.
- Provide ways to browse and search.

## Outcome
Organised knowledge.

## Purpose
Links related items of knowledge. Links let readers follow a subject across sources.

## Activities
- Identify items that relate to one another.
- Create explicit links between them.

## Outcome
Linked knowledge.

## Purpose
Records incidents in detail. Captured incidents are the basis for learning from them.

## Activities
- Record what happened, when, and what was affected.
- Record the actions taken.

## Outcome
A recorded incident.

## Purpose
Captures experience from the operation of a system. Operational experience contains lessons that design alone cannot provide.

## Activities
- Collect observations and accounts from those who run the system.
- Record them in a form suited to later analysis.

## Outcome
Captured operational experience.

## Purpose
Captures experience of how performance has varied and why. Experience of performance guides future design and tuning.

## Activities
- Record the periods and conditions in which performance was good or poor.
- Record what was done and what effect it had.

## Outcome
Captured performance experience.

## Purpose
Analyses an incident to understand it. Analysis explains what occurred and why.

## Activities
- Examine the sequence of events and the evidence.
- Identify the causes and the conditions that allowed the incident.

## Outcome
An analysis of the incident.

## Purpose
Analyses a failure to find its causes. Understanding failure prevents repetition.

## Activities
- Examine how the failure arose and how it spread.
- Identify the underlying causes.

## Outcome
An analysis of the failure.

## Purpose
Finds patterns in data, work or experience. Patterns reveal regularities that single cases hide.

## Activities
- Examine many cases for features that recur.
- Describe each pattern and where it appears.

## Outcome
Discovered patterns.

## Purpose
Analyses how often something recurs and under what conditions. Recurrence shows which problems are systemic.

## Activities
- Count the occurrences and the circumstances in which they appear.
- Identify what the recurring cases have in common.

## Outcome
An analysis of recurrence.

## Purpose
Compares incidents to find what they share. Shared causes show where a general remedy is needed.

## Activities
- Compare the causes, conditions and effects of several incidents.
- Identify the common factors.

## Outcome
A cross-incident analysis.

## Purpose
Identifies the lessons that experience offers. A lesson must be recognised before it can be learned.

## Activities
- Review the experience for what went well or badly and why.
- State each lesson in terms that others can apply.

## Outcome
Identified lessons.

## Purpose
Extracts lessons from sources and states them clearly. Extracted lessons can be shared and applied.

## Activities
- Draw the lessons out of the records and accounts.
- State each lesson with its context.

## Outcome
Extracted lessons.

## Purpose
Checks that a lesson is sound before it is used. An invalid lesson can cause harm.

## Activities
- Test the lesson against the evidence and against other cases.
- Record whether it holds and where it applies.

## Outcome
Validated lessons.

## Purpose
Combines related lessons. Consolidation removes overlap and strengthens the message.

## Activities
- Merge lessons that say the same thing.
- Keep the context that distinguishes those that differ.

## Outcome
Consolidated lessons.

## Purpose
Combines experience from many cases into a coherent account. Synthesis shows what experience teaches taken as a whole.

## Activities
- Bring together the experiences from the different cases.
- Draw out the conclusions they support.

## Outcome
A synthesis of experience.

## Purpose
Combines knowledge from different sources into one consistent body. Integration removes the barriers between separate pieces of knowledge.

## Activities
- Reconcile the terms and structures of the sources.
- Merge the knowledge into a single body.

## Outcome
Integrated knowledge.

## Purpose
Observes how engineering is actually practised. Observation shows real practice, which often differs from the documented one.

## Activities
- Watch and record how teams carry out their work.
- Note variations between teams.

## Outcome
Observations of practice.

## Purpose
Analyses how engineering practices work. Analysis shows their strengths and weaknesses.

## Activities
- Examine each practice, how it is applied and what it produces.
- Identify what makes it succeed or fail.

## Outcome
An analysis of practices.

## Purpose
Compares practices. Comparison shows which practice gives better results.

## Activities
- Compare the practices of different teams or against a reference.
- Record the differences and their effect.

## Outcome
A comparison of practices.

## Purpose
Evaluates how effective a practice is. Evaluation shows whether a practice achieves its purpose.

## Activities
- Measure the results the practice produces against its aim.
- Judge whether the practice is worth keeping.

## Outcome
An evaluation of the effectiveness of a practice.

## Purpose
Analyses the outcomes of actions or decisions. Analysis shows what was achieved and what was not.

## Activities
- Compare the actual outcomes with the intended outcomes.
- Identify what accounts for the difference.

## Outcome
An analysis of outcomes.

## Purpose
Assesses a practice against a standard. Assessment shows how mature or compliant it is.

## Activities
- Compare the practice with the standard or reference.
- Record the gaps.

## Outcome
An assessment of a practice.

## Purpose
Identifies where improvement is possible. Identification gives improvement effort a target.

## Activities
- Examine performance and practice to find opportunities.
- Describe each improvement and the benefit it could bring.

## Outcome
A list of identified improvements.

## Purpose
Changes a practice to make it better. Modification applies what analysis has shown.

## Activities
- Define the change to the practice.
- Apply it and communicate it to those affected.

## Outcome
A modified practice.

## Purpose
Tunes a practice to get the best result from it. Optimisation refines a practice that already works.

## Activities
- Identify the steps in the practice that waste effort or time.
- Adjust them and check the effect.

## Outcome
An optimised practice.

## Purpose
Designs an experiment to test a change. A well-designed experiment gives a clear answer.

## Activities
- Define the hypothesis, the measures and the conditions.
- Define how results will be judged.

## Outcome
An experiment design.

## Purpose
Tries a new or changed practice on a small scale. Experiments show the effect of a practice before it is adopted widely.

## Activities
- Run the practice in a limited setting following the experiment design.
- Collect the results.

## Outcome
Results of an experiment with a practice.

## Purpose
Evaluates the results of an experiment. Evaluation shows whether the hypothesis was supported.

## Activities
- Analyse the results against the criteria that were set.
- State what was learned and what should follow.

## Outcome
An evaluation of an experiment.

## Purpose
Chooses the practices to be adopted. Selection ensures that the practices fit the need.

## Activities
- Compare the candidate practices against the need and the context.
- Choose the practice and record why.

## Outcome
A selected practice.

## Purpose
Introduces a practice to the people who will use it. Introduction gives people what they need to begin.

## Activities
- Explain the practice, train people and provide the supporting tools.
- Plan the transition from the previous way of working.

## Outcome
A practice introduced to its users.

## Purpose
Applies a practice in day-to-day work. Application is what makes the practice real.

## Activities
- Carry out work according to the practice.
- Note difficulties and adaptations.

## Outcome
A practice in use.

## Purpose
Assesses how far a practice has been adopted. Assessment shows whether the practice is really used.

## Activities
- Measure how widely and how faithfully the practice is followed.
- Identify the obstacles to adoption.

## Outcome
An assessment of adoption.

## Purpose
Detects changes in the business that may affect engineering. Early detection gives engineering time to respond.

## Activities
- Watch business objectives, markets, regulation and operations for signs of change.
- Record each change with its source and date.

## Outcome
A record of detected business changes.

## Purpose
Analyses the signals that suggest a change is under way. Signals are often weak and need interpretation.

## Activities
- Examine the signals together to judge which indicate a real change.
- Rule out signals that are noise.

## Outcome
An analysis of change signals.

## Purpose
Identifies the needs that a business change creates. Needs state what must be done in response to a change.

## Activities
- Work out what the business now requires because of the change.
- Record each need and who has it.

## Outcome
A list of identified needs.

## Purpose
Analyses what a change means for the business. Understanding the business impact shows how much the change matters.

## Activities
- Assess the effect of the change on the operations, customers and finances of the business.
- Rank the effects by significance.

## Outcome
An analysis of the business impact.

## Purpose
Analyses what a change means for engineering work. Impact analysis shows what must be changed or re-planned.

## Activities
- Identify the systems, artefacts and plans that the change touches.
- Estimate the effort and risk of the response.

## Outcome
An analysis of the engineering impact.

## Purpose
Analyses what a change means for the organisation's capabilities. Some changes require capabilities that the organisation does not yet have.

## Activities
- Identify the capabilities that the change affects.
- Assess whether each capability can meet the new demand.

## Outcome
An analysis of the capability impact.

## Purpose
Brings objectives into agreement with one another. Objectives that conflict cause effort to be wasted.

## Activities
- Compare the objectives that apply to the same work.
- Resolve differences or record the choice that is made.

## Outcome
Reconciled objectives.

## Purpose
Brings priorities into agreement. Reconciled priorities give teams a single order of work.

## Activities
- Compare the priorities set by different parties.
- Agree a single priority order.

## Outcome
Reconciled priorities.

## Purpose
Brings requirements into agreement with the changed need. Requirements that no longer reflect the need must be revised.

## Activities
- Compare the requirements with the current needs.
- Revise or remove those that differ.

## Outcome
Reconciled requirements.

## Purpose
Changes the direction of engineering work to follow the business. Realignment keeps engineering useful.

## Activities
- Decide how the direction of the work should change.
- Communicate the new direction to the teams.

## Outcome
A realigned direction of work.

## Purpose
Moves resources to where they are now needed. Realignment places effort where it has most value.

## Activities
- Identify where resources are no longer needed and where they are short.
- Reassign them accordingly.

## Outcome
Realigned resources.

## Purpose
Changes priorities to reflect the new situation. Realigned priorities direct the effort of teams.

## Activities
- Revise the priority order in line with the business need.
- Tell the teams affected.

## Outcome
Realigned priorities.

## Purpose
Observes the architecture as it is actually implemented. Observation is the basis for comparing reality with the design.

## Activities
- Examine the code, configuration and runtime to see the real structure.
- Record what is found.

## Outcome
An observed view of the architecture.

## Purpose
Tracks the state of the architecture over time. Tracking shows how the architecture has evolved.

## Activities
- Record the state of the architecture at regular points.
- Keep the records so that states can be compared.

## Outcome
A record of architecture states.

## Purpose
Detects changes to the architecture as they happen. Detection lets a change be reviewed promptly.

## Activities
- Compare the current architecture with the previous state.
- Report each difference.

## Outcome
Detected changes to the architecture.

## Purpose
Analyses the structure of a system. Structural analysis shows how the parts are arranged and connected.

## Activities
- Examine the components, layers and connections.
- Identify features of the structure that matter for quality.

## Outcome
An analysis of structure.

## Purpose
Analyses how well a design provides the qualities required of it. Quality attributes include performance, security and maintainability.

## Activities
- Examine the design against each quality attribute.
- Record where it succeeds and where it does not.

## Outcome
An analysis of quality attributes.

## Purpose
Compares architectures. Comparison shows what differs between the intended and the actual, or between systems.

## Activities
- Compare the elements and relationships of the two architectures.
- Record the differences.

## Outcome
A comparison of architectures.

## Purpose
Detects when something has moved away from its intended or previous state. Drift undermines the reliability of designs and configurations.

## Activities
- Compare the current state with the intended or earlier state.
- Report the differences that exceed the tolerance.

## Outcome
Detected drift.

## Purpose
Analyses how closely something follows a standard or design. Conformance shows whether rules are being followed.

## Activities
- Compare the implementation with the rules it should follow.
- Record each non-conformance and its significance.

## Outcome
A conformance analysis.

## Purpose
Identifies the risks that threaten an architecture. Risks must be recognised before they can be reduced.

## Activities
- Examine the architecture for weaknesses, limits and exposure to change.
- Record each risk with what it threatens.

## Outcome
A list of architecture risks.

## Purpose
Analyses how an architecture is declining in quality. Degradation shows where erosion is under way.

## Activities
- Measure signs of erosion such as growing coupling and rule violations.
- Identify the causes.

## Outcome
An analysis of architecture degradation.

## Purpose
Analyses the implications that new changes are beginning to have. Early understanding of implications gives time to respond.

## Activities
- Examine recent changes and trends for their likely consequences.
- Describe the implications for the architecture.

## Outcome
An analysis of emerging implications.

## Purpose
Analyses the changes that have been made to an architecture. Analysis shows whether change has been sound.

## Activities
- Examine each change and its effect on the structure.
- Judge whether it fits the architectural intent.

## Outcome
An analysis of architectural change.

## Purpose
Analyses the impact of the architecture's evolution on the system. Evolution has consequences for quality and cost.

## Activities
- Assess how the evolution of the architecture affects the system and those who depend on it.
- Record the significant impacts.

## Outcome
An analysis of the impact of evolution.

## Purpose
Analyses the options for how an architecture may evolve. Analysis supports choosing a sound direction.

## Activities
- Describe each option for the future of the architecture.
- Compare the options for benefit, cost and risk.

## Outcome
An analysis of evolution options.

## Purpose
Captures information as work proceeds. Information captured at the time is more complete and accurate.

## Activities
- Record the information that arises from the work as it is produced.
- Keep it in a form that can be used for documentation.

## Outcome
Captured information.

## Purpose
Captures changes to the system as they are made. A record of change is the basis for keeping documentation current.

## Activities
- Record each change and what it affects.
- Keep the record linked to the work.

## Outcome
Captured changes.

## Purpose
Produces documents from captured information. Generated documents reflect the work as it is.

## Activities
- Select the content for the document and arrange it in the document structure.
- Generate the document and check it.

## Outcome
A generated document.

## Purpose
Produces the content of documents from sources. Generated content saves effort and stays consistent.

## Activities
- Derive the text, tables and diagrams from the source information.
- Review the generated content for correctness.

## Outcome
Generated content.

## Purpose
Produces records of work that has been done. Records give evidence of what happened.

## Activities
- Generate a record for each piece of work from the information captured.
- Store the records where they can be retrieved.

## Outcome
Generated records.

## Purpose
Keeps documentation in step with the implementation. Documentation that follows the implementation can be trusted.

## Activities
- Detect changes to the implementation.
- Update the documentation to match.

## Outcome
Documentation synchronised with the implementation.

## Purpose
Keeps documentation in step with changes. Each change should be reflected in the documents it affects.

## Activities
- Identify the documents affected by each change.
- Update them.

## Outcome
Documentation synchronised with changes.

## Purpose
Keeps documentation in step with the current state of the system. Documentation should describe the system as it is.

## Activities
- Compare the documentation with the present state of the system.
- Correct the differences.

## Outcome
Documentation synchronised with the state of the system.

## Purpose
Finds content that is out of date. Detecting obsolescence stops readers from relying on wrong information.

## Activities
- Compare the content with the current system and sources.
- Mark content that no longer applies.

## Outcome
A list of obsolete content.

## Purpose
Improves content that is unclear or incomplete. Refinement raises the usefulness of documentation.

## Activities
- Review the content for clarity and completeness.
- Revise it where it falls short.

## Outcome
Refined content.

## Purpose
Finds how artefacts or items are related. Discovery shows connections that nobody recorded.

## Activities
- Examine the items for references, shared names and dependencies.
- Record each relationship found.

## Outcome
Discovered relationships.

## Purpose
Identifies the relationships between engineering artefacts. These relationships form the basis of traceability.

## Activities
- Determine which artefacts derive from, implement or verify others.
- Record each relationship and its type.

## Outcome
Identified artefact relationships.

## Purpose
Finds the dependencies between items. Dependencies need to be known before change.

## Activities
- Examine the items for use of one another.
- Record each dependency with its direction.

## Outcome
Discovered dependencies.

## Purpose
Creates traces between artefacts. Traces connect the stages of engineering work.

## Activities
- Create the link between each pair of related artefacts.
- Record the type of link.

## Outcome
Created traces.

## Purpose
Links artefacts to one another. Links allow navigation between related work.

## Activities
- Connect each artefact to the artefacts it relates to.
- Keep the links stored with the artefacts.

## Outcome
Linked artefacts.

## Purpose
Records relationships once they are found. A recorded relationship can be used and checked.

## Activities
- Store each relationship with its type, direction and evidence.
- Make the record available for queries.

## Outcome
Recorded relationships.

## Purpose
Updates traces after artefacts change. Updated traces stay accurate.

## Activities
- Find the traces that the change affects.
- Revise or replace them.

## Outcome
Updated traces.

## Purpose
Updates recorded relationships after the items change. Updated relationships remain true.

## Activities
- Re-examine the relationships of changed items.
- Update or remove those that no longer hold.

## Outcome
Updated relationships.

## Purpose
Keeps traces consistent with the artefacts they link. Synchronisation prevents stale traces.

## Activities
- Compare the traces with the current artefacts.
- Correct any that no longer match.

## Outcome
Synchronised traces.

## Purpose
Verifies that traces are correct. Verified traces can be relied on for impact analysis.

## Activities
- Check each trace against the artefacts it links.
- Record the traces that are wrong.

## Outcome
Verified traces.

## Purpose
Verifies that recorded relationships hold. Verification confirms that the relationships reflect reality.

## Activities
- Check each relationship against the items concerned.
- Record those that are false.

## Outcome
Verified relationships.

## Purpose
Checks that traces agree with one another. Inconsistent traces suggest errors.

## Activities
- Compare the traces that concern the same artefacts.
- Report the disagreements.

## Outcome
A consistency check of traces.

## Purpose
Analyses where an artefact came from and what came from it. Lineage explains how work products arose.

## Activities
- Follow the traces back to the origin and forward to the results.
- Describe the lineage.

## Outcome
An analysis of lineage.

## Purpose
Analyses how completely one set of items covers another. Coverage shows what has and has not been addressed.

## Activities
- Compare the items against the set they should cover.
- Report the proportion covered and the gaps.

## Outcome
A coverage analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses what a change would affect. Impact analysis reveals the reach of a change before it is made.

## Activities
- Follow the traces and dependencies from the changed item.
- List what could be affected.

## Outcome
An impact analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the code of a legacy system. The code is often the only complete description of what the system does.

## Activities
- Examine the code to understand its structure and logic.
- Record findings about what it does.

## Outcome
An analysis of legacy code.

## Purpose
Analyses what documentation exists for a legacy system. Documentation shows the intent, though it may be out of date.

## Activities
- Read the available documents and assess their reliability.
- Record what they say about the system.

## Outcome
An analysis of legacy documentation.

## Purpose
Analyses the surviving records of a system's history. History explains why the system is as it is.

## Activities
- Examine records such as tickets, correspondence and change logs.
- Draw out what they show about decisions and behaviour.

## Outcome
An analysis of historical evidence.

## Purpose
Analyses how a system behaves while running. Runtime behaviour shows what the system does in practice.

## Activities
- Observe the system in operation and record its actions and data.
- Describe the behaviour that results.

## Outcome
An analysis of runtime behaviour.

## Purpose
Recovers the business rules that a system applies. Rules embedded in code are often undocumented.

## Activities
- Examine the logic of the system for conditions and calculations that reflect business rules.
- State each rule in business terms.

## Outcome
Reconstructed business rules.

## Purpose
Recovers the workflows that a system carries out. Workflows show how work moves through the system.

## Activities
- Follow the paths of work through the system.
- Describe each workflow in order.

## Outcome
Reconstructed workflows.

## Purpose
Extracts the architecture from an existing system. An extracted architecture shows how the system is organised.

## Activities
- Analyse the code and its deployment to identify the major parts and links.
- Present them as an architecture description.

## Outcome
An extracted architecture.

## Purpose
Finds the components that make up a system. Components are the units that can be understood and changed.

## Activities
- Examine the system for coherent units of code and function.
- Name and describe each component.

## Outcome
Discovered components.

## Purpose
Rebuilds the structure of a system from its evidence. Structure shows how the parts fit together.

## Activities
- Combine the discovered components and relationships.
- Present the overall structure.

## Outcome
A reconstructed structure.

## Purpose
Finds the interfaces through which a system communicates. Interfaces are the points of contact with the rest of the world.

## Activities
- Examine the system for the points where it sends or receives data.
- Describe each interface.

## Outcome
Discovered interfaces.

## Purpose
Analyses how a system depends on data. Data dependencies are a common source of hidden coupling.

## Activities
- Identify which parts of the system read and write each data store.
- Describe the dependencies.

## Outcome
An analysis of data dependencies.

## Purpose
Validates knowledge recovered from a legacy system. Recovered knowledge is inferred and may be wrong.

## Activities
- Check the knowledge against the system, the evidence and people who know it.
- Correct or reject what is wrong.

## Outcome
Validated recovered knowledge.

## Purpose
Checks that stated behaviour matches real behaviour. Validation shows whether descriptions can be trusted.

## Activities
- Compare the described behaviour with the observed behaviour.
- Record the differences.

## Outcome
A validation of behaviour.

## Purpose
Identifies the obligations that a regulation or contract imposes. Obligations are what must be met.

## Activities
- Read the source and extract each requirement it creates.
- Record the obligations with their source.

## Outcome
Identified obligations.

## Purpose
Assesses whether an obligation applies. Not every obligation applies to every system.

## Activities
- Compare the obligation with the system, its data and its context.
- Record whether and how it applies.

## Outcome
An applicability assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses whether a system meets its obligations. Assessment gives a judgement of compliance.

## Activities
- Compare the system and its evidence with each applicable obligation.
- Record the result for each.

## Outcome
A compliance assessment.

## Purpose
Collects the evidence relevant to a question. Evidence is needed to establish facts and to show compliance.

## Activities
- Gather records, test results and other evidence.
- Store it in a way that preserves its integrity.

## Outcome
Collected evidence.

## Purpose
Extracts the relevant facts from evidence. Extraction makes large bodies of evidence usable.

## Activities
- Read the evidence and identify the facts that matter.
- Record them with references to the source.

## Outcome
Extracted evidence.

## Purpose
Identifies where something falls short. Gaps show what remains to be done.

## Activities
- Compare what is required with what exists.
- List each difference.

## Outcome
Identified gaps.

## Purpose
Detects where something does not meet its requirement. Detection allows correction before audit or harm.

## Activities
