- Check the system against each requirement.
- Record each case that fails.

## Outcome
Detected nonconformances.

## Purpose
Checks that requirements are met. Checking shows whether obligations are satisfied.

## Activities
- Compare the system with each requirement.
- Record whether it is met.

## Outcome
Requirement checks.

## Purpose
Verifies that controls operate as intended. A control that does not work gives no assurance.

## Activities
- Test each control against its purpose.
- Record whether it works.

## Outcome
Verified controls.

## Purpose
Verifies that evidence is valid and supports the claim. Unverified evidence is not reliable.

## Activities
- Check the origin, completeness and relevance of the evidence.
- Record whether it can be relied on.

## Outcome
Verified evidence.

## Purpose
Checks something repeatedly without interruption. Continuous checking replaces occasional audits.

## Activities
- Run checks automatically at short intervals or on each change.
- Report the failures as they occur.

## Outcome
Continuous checks.

## Purpose
Monitors whether compliance is maintained. Compliance may change from day to day.

## Activities
- Track the state of compliance for each obligation.
- Report changes in state.

## Outcome
Monitoring of compliance state.

## Purpose
Monitors changes that may affect something. Change monitoring shows when an earlier result may no longer hold.

## Activities
- Watch for changes in the system, the rules and the environment.
- Report those that matter.

## Outcome
Monitoring of change.

## Purpose
Finds evidence that bears on a question or decision. Evidence must be found before it can be used.

## Activities
- Search the sources where relevant evidence may be held.
- Record what is found and where.

## Outcome
Discovered evidence.

## Purpose
Links evidence to the decision or claim it supports. Links let others see what a conclusion rests on.

## Activities
- Associate each item of evidence with the decision it concerns.
- Record the nature of the support.

## Outcome
Evidence linked to decisions.

## Purpose
Identifies the evidence that supports a decision. Supporting evidence makes a decision defensible.

## Activities
- Review the evidence for what favours the chosen course.
- Record it.

## Outcome
Identified supporting evidence.

## Purpose
Extracts the reasoning behind a decision from records. Rationale is often scattered in discussions.

## Activities
- Read the records of discussion and decision.
- Draw out the reasons given.

## Outcome
Extracted rationale.

## Purpose
Records the assumptions on which a decision rests. Assumptions that are written down can be tested later.

## Activities
- State each assumption that the decision relies on.
- Link each to the decision.

## Outcome
Recorded assumptions.

## Purpose
Rebuilds the context in which a decision was taken. Context is needed to judge a decision fairly.

## Activities
- Gather evidence of the circumstances at the time.
- Describe the situation.

## Outcome
A reconstructed context.

## Purpose
Rebuilds the constraints that applied to a decision. Constraints limited the options that were available.

## Activities
- Identify the limits of time, cost, technology and policy at the time.
- Record them.

## Outcome
Reconstructed constraints.

## Purpose
Rebuilds the objectives that a decision pursued. Objectives show what the decision was meant to achieve.

## Activities
- Infer from the records what the decision makers were aiming for.
- State the objectives.

## Outcome
Reconstructed objectives.

## Purpose
Tracks what results from a decision over time. Tracking shows the outcome as it unfolds.

## Activities
- Record the results that follow the decision.
- Keep the record linked to the decision.

## Outcome
A tracked outcome.

## Purpose
Compares the actual outcome with the expected one. Comparison shows whether the decision worked.

## Activities
- Set the actual results against the expected results.
- Note and explain the differences.

## Outcome
An outcome comparison.

## Purpose
Analyses how effective a decision was. Analysis shows what made the decision succeed or fail.

## Activities
- Judge the decision against its objectives and its outcome.
- Identify what contributed to the result.

## Outcome
An analysis of the effectiveness of a decision.

## Purpose
Searches for evidence. A deliberate search finds more than chance.

## Activities
- Define what is being looked for.
- Search the likely sources systematically.

## Outcome
Search results.

## Purpose
Retrieves evidence from where it is held. Retrieval makes the evidence available for use.

## Activities
- Obtain the items of evidence that the search identified.
- Preserve their form and origin.

## Outcome
Retrieved evidence.

## Purpose
Identifies which items count as evidence for a question. Identification selects the relevant from the available.

## Activities
- Judge each item for relevance to the question.
- Record those selected.

## Outcome
Identified evidence.

## Purpose
Gathers evidence from many sources together. Aggregation lets the evidence be considered as a whole.

## Activities
- Collect the evidence in a common place.
- Arrange it by subject.

## Outcome
Aggregated evidence.

## Purpose
Merges evidence to remove overlap. Consolidation leaves a coherent body of evidence.

## Activities
- Combine items that say the same thing.
- Note where sources agree and differ.

## Outcome
Consolidated evidence.

## Purpose
Combines evidence into a picture of what it shows as a whole. Synthesis yields conclusions that single items cannot.

## Activities
- Weigh the items of evidence together.
- State what they establish.

## Outcome
Synthesised evidence.

## Purpose
Finds how information from different sources relates. Correlation shows corroboration and conflict.

## Activities
- Compare information about the same subject from different sources.
- Record agreements and disagreements.

## Outcome
A cross-source correlation.

## Purpose
Relates patterns to one another. Correlation shows which patterns occur together.

## Activities
- Compare patterns across cases or sources.
- Record those that coincide.

## Outcome
Correlated patterns.

## Purpose
Assesses how good evidence is. Quality determines how much weight evidence can bear.

## Activities
- Judge the reliability, completeness and age of the evidence.
- Record the assessment.

## Outcome
An assessment of evidence quality.

## Purpose
Assesses how relevant evidence is to a question. Relevant evidence bears on the question being asked.

## Activities
- Judge how directly each item addresses the question.
- Record the assessment.

## Outcome
An assessment of evidence relevance.

## Purpose
Assesses whether items of evidence agree. Consistent evidence is more credible.

## Activities
- Compare the items for agreement.
- Record any conflicts.

## Outcome
An assessment of evidence consistency.

## Purpose
Reasons about a question in light of its context. Reasoning without context can give the wrong answer.

## Activities
- Take account of the circumstances in which the question arises.
- State conclusions that apply to that context.

## Outcome
Context-sensitive conclusions.

## Purpose
Reasons about what constraints allow and forbid. Constraint reasoning shows which options are actually open.

## Activities
- Identify the constraints that bear on the question.
- Work out which options remain feasible within them.

## Outcome
Conclusions about what the constraints permit.

## Purpose
Reasons about what causes what. Causal reasoning explains why events occur and what would change them.

## Activities
- Examine the evidence for how one factor leads to another.
- State the causal explanation and how confident it is.

## Outcome
A causal explanation.

## Purpose
Reasons by comparing cases or options. Comparison shows what is distinctive and what is common.

## Activities
- Select comparable cases and the dimensions on which to compare them.
- State what the comparison shows.

## Outcome
Conclusions drawn from comparison.

## Purpose
Watches requirements over time. Monitoring shows when requirements change or lose validity.

## Activities
- Track the state and changes of each requirement.
- Report the changes that matter.

## Outcome
Monitoring of requirements.

## Purpose
Validates requirements again after circumstances change. Revalidation shows whether requirements remain correct.

## Activities
- Compare requirements with the current needs and context.
- Record those that no longer hold.

## Outcome
Revalidated requirements.

## Purpose
Checks repeatedly that requirements still agree with one another. Consistency can be lost as requirements change.

## Activities
- Compare requirements that concern the same subject after each change.
- Report any that now disagree.

## Outcome
A consistency check of requirements.

## Purpose
Detects changes made to requirements. Detection ensures that changes are noticed and reviewed.

## Activities
- Compare the current requirements with their earlier state.
- List the additions, deletions and amendments.

## Outcome
Detected requirement changes.

## Purpose
Detects when the intent behind requirements has shifted. Intent can change while the written requirement remains the same.

## Activities
- Compare current stakeholder intent with the intent recorded in the requirements.
- Report where they differ.

## Outcome
Detected intent drift.

## Purpose
Watches whether a set of items stays complete. Completeness can be lost as scope or context changes.

## Activities
- Check the set against its scope repeatedly.
- Report items that have become missing.

## Outcome
Monitoring of completeness.

## Purpose
Watches the boundary of scope. Boundaries move when change is not controlled.

## Activities
- Compare the current scope with the agreed boundary.
- Report items that have crossed it.

## Outcome
Monitoring of boundaries.

## Purpose
Watches for conflicts as items change. New conflicts appear when new items are added.

## Activities
- Check new and changed items against existing ones for conflict.
- Report conflicts when they appear.

## Outcome
Monitoring of conflicts.

## Purpose
Watches the dependencies between items. Dependencies change as items change.

## Activities
- Track the dependencies between items and their changes.
- Report dependencies that have become broken or circular.

## Outcome
Monitoring of dependencies.

## Purpose
Detects statements that contradict one another. Contradictions show that something is wrong.

## Activities
- Compare statements that concern the same subject.
- Report each pair that cannot both be true.

## Outcome
Detected contradictions.

## Purpose
Watches the state of traces. Monitoring shows when traces become stale.

## Activities
- Track the traces and the artefacts they link.
- Report traces that no longer match.

## Outcome
Monitoring of traces.

## Purpose
Detects where traces are missing. Gaps show where lineage cannot be shown.

## Activities
- Check each artefact for the traces it should have.
- List the missing ones.

## Outcome
Detected trace gaps.

## Purpose
Watches that traces stay consistent with one another. Inconsistency suggests an error in a link.

## Activities
- Compare traces that concern the same artefacts after each change.
- Report any that conflict.

## Outcome
Monitoring of trace consistency.

## Purpose
Detects the early signs of risk. Early signs give time to act.

## Activities
- Watch data and events for indicators that associate with risk.
- Raise the indicators for assessment.

## Outcome
Detected risk signals.

## Purpose
Discovers risks that threaten the work. A risk must be found before it can be handled.

## Activities
- Examine plans, systems and environments for sources of risk.
- Record each risk found.

## Outcome
Discovered risks.

## Purpose
Classifies risks by type and source. Classification helps to direct risks to those who can handle them.

## Activities
- Assign each risk to categories of the agreed scheme.
- Keep the classification consistent.

## Outcome
Classified risks.

## Purpose
Forecasts how risks will develop. A forecast shows which risks will grow.

## Activities
- Project the risks forward using trends and planned change.
- State the expected exposure over time.

## Outcome
A risk forecast.

## Purpose
Predicts how likely a risk is to occur. Likelihood is needed to rank risks.

## Activities
- Estimate the probability from history and current conditions.
- State the estimate and the basis for it.

## Outcome
A likelihood prediction.

## Purpose
Predicts how a risk is changing. Trends show whether a risk is rising or falling.

## Activities
- Extend the observed trend of the risk forward.
- State the expected direction and pace.

## Outcome
A risk trend prediction.

## Purpose
Analyses how risks relate to one another. Related risks can compound.

## Activities
- Identify risks that share causes or affect the same things.
- Describe how one risk influences another.

## Outcome
An analysis of risk relationships.

## Purpose
Relates current conditions to similar events in the past. Past experience helps to anticipate what may follow.

## Activities
- Find past cases that resemble the present.
- Compare what happened in them.

## Outcome
A historical correlation.

## Purpose
Relates risks across systems. A risk in one system can affect others.

## Activities
- Compare the risks of connected systems.
- Identify those that spread or share a cause.

## Outcome
A cross-system risk correlation.

## Purpose
Assesses the effect that something would have. Impact is needed to judge how much something matters.

## Activities
- Estimate the consequence for the people, systems and goals concerned.
- State the size and spread of the effect.

## Outcome
An impact assessment.

## Purpose
Monitors how risks change over time. Monitoring shows whether risk is growing.

## Activities
- Record the level of each risk at regular intervals.
- Report the direction of change.

## Outcome
Monitoring of risk trends.

## Purpose
Detects risks that are only beginning to appear. Early detection gives the most time to respond.

## Activities
- Watch for new patterns that suggest a risk is forming.
- Raise them for assessment.

## Outcome
Detected emerging risks.

## Purpose
Analyses the patterns that risks follow. Patterns help to predict future risk.

## Activities
- Examine many risks for common shapes and causes.
- Describe the patterns found.

## Outcome
An analysis of risk patterns.

## Purpose
Monitors the signals that indicate quality. Signals show changes in quality early.

## Activities
- Watch measures such as defects and test results.
- Report changes in them.

## Outcome
Monitoring of quality signals.

## Purpose
Monitors the present state of quality. State monitoring shows how good the system is now.

## Activities
- Track the current quality measures against the targets.
- Report where quality falls short.

## Outcome
Monitoring of quality state.

## Purpose
Monitors how quality changes over time. Trends show whether quality is improving or declining.

## Activities
- Record quality measures at regular intervals.
- Report the direction of change.

## Outcome
Monitoring of quality trends.

## Purpose
Assesses how good something is. Assessment gives a judgement against criteria.

## Activities
- Compare the item with its quality criteria.
- State how well it meets them.

## Outcome
A quality assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses a system against its quality attributes. Each attribute, such as security or performance, needs its own judgement.

## Activities
- Measure or judge each attribute against its target.
- Record the result for each.

## Outcome
A quality attribute assessment.

## Purpose
Compares quality with a baseline. Comparison shows whether quality has improved or declined.

## Activities
- Set the current measures beside the baseline measures.
- Report the differences.

## Outcome
A comparison with the quality baseline.

## Purpose
Checks that something meets its quality requirements. Checking confirms quality before something is accepted.

## Activities
- Compare the item with its quality requirements.
- Record whether each is met.

## Outcome
A quality check.

## Purpose
Verifies the evidence that is offered for quality. Evidence must be sound to support a quality claim.

## Activities
- Check the origin and completeness of the evidence.
- Record whether it supports the claim.

## Outcome
Verified quality evidence.

## Purpose
Verifies that quality results are correct. Incorrect results mislead decisions.

## Activities
- Check the results against the method and the data.
- Correct or flag those that are wrong.

## Outcome
Verified quality results.

## Purpose
Detects departures from what is expected. Deviations are the first sign of a problem.

## Activities
- Compare actual results with the expected ones.
- Report the differences that exceed tolerance.

## Outcome
Detected deviations.

## Purpose
Detects where something that used to work no longer does. Regression shows that a change has caused harm.

## Activities
- Compare current behaviour with earlier correct behaviour.
- Report each case that has got worse.

## Outcome
Detected regressions.

## Purpose
Detects unusual quality results. Anomalies can show a hidden problem.

## Activities
- Look for results that fall outside the normal range.
- Report them for investigation.

## Outcome
Detected quality anomalies.

## Purpose
Detects where quality falls short of what is needed. Gaps show where to direct improvement.

## Activities
- Compare quality with the targets for each attribute.
- List the shortfalls.

## Outcome
Detected quality gaps.

## Purpose
Identifies the actions that would correct a problem. Identified actions turn analysis into work.

## Activities
- Consider the causes of the problem and the ways to remove them.
- List the actions with their expected effect.

## Outcome
Identified corrective actions.

## Purpose
Collects the knowledge held in each project. Collection brings project knowledge to a common place.

## Activities
- Gather the lessons, decisions and records of each project.
- Record where each came from.

## Outcome
Collected project knowledge.

## Purpose
Collects the artefacts that projects produce. Artefacts are the concrete record of what was built.

## Activities
- Gather the documents, models and code of each project.
- Catalogue them.

## Outcome
Collected artefacts.

## Purpose
Collects the experiences of people and projects. Experience shows how work really went.

## Activities
- Gather accounts from those who did the work.
- Record them in a common form.

## Outcome
Collected experience.

## Purpose
Relates knowledge from different projects. Correlation shows connections across the portfolio.

## Activities
- Compare the knowledge of projects that share a feature.
- Record what relates them.

## Outcome
A cross-project correlation.

## Purpose
Relates knowledge from different domains. Correlation shows what is general and what is domain specific.

## Activities
- Compare knowledge from domains that differ.
- Record the patterns they share.

## Outcome
A cross-domain correlation.

## Purpose
Compares projects. Comparison shows what differs in approach and results.

## Activities
- Select the dimensions on which to compare the projects.
- Record the similarities and differences.

## Outcome
A project comparison.

## Purpose
Identifies what projects have in common. Commonalities are candidates for shared practice.

## Activities
- Compare projects for shared features.
- Record each commonality.

## Outcome
Identified commonalities.

## Purpose
Analyses how and why projects differ. Differences show where context matters.

## Activities
- Examine the differences identified between projects.
- Explain what accounts for each.

## Outcome
An analysis of differences.

## Purpose
Detects things that happen more than once. Recurrence turns isolated cases into patterns.

## Activities
- Search the records for repeated occurrences.
- Record where and how often they recur.

## Outcome
Detected recurrence.

## Purpose
Analyses patterns that appear across projects. Such patterns show organisation-wide habits.

## Activities
- Compare patterns found in different projects.
- Describe those that appear in several.

## Outcome
An analysis of cross-project patterns.

## Purpose
Removes duplicate knowledge. Duplicates waste effort and can contradict one another.

## Activities
- Identify items that carry the same knowledge.
- Merge them or remove the surplus.

## Outcome
Knowledge without duplicates.

## Purpose
Combines knowledge into a coherent whole. Consolidation produces a single, reliable body of knowledge.

## Activities
- Merge related items and resolve differences.
- Present the result in one place.

## Outcome
Consolidated knowledge.

## Purpose
Collects the outcomes of work. Outcomes show what was actually achieved.

## Activities
- Gather the results of completed work.
- Record them with the work they relate to.

## Outcome
Collected outcomes.

## Purpose
Collects events that occur. Events provide the raw record of what happens.

## Activities
- Gather events from systems and from people.
- Store them with time and source.

## Outcome
Collected events.

## Purpose
Extracts patterns from information. Patterns turn many cases into guidance.

## Activities
- Examine the information for recurring features.
- State each pattern in a reusable form.

## Outcome
Extracted patterns.

## Purpose
Extracts knowledge from information. Extraction makes knowledge explicit and usable.

## Activities
- Read the information and identify what it teaches.
- State the knowledge in a form others can use.

## Outcome
Extracted knowledge.

## Purpose
Analyses what the organisation has learned. Analysis shows whether learning is occurring.

## Activities
- Examine experience and outcomes for evidence of learning.
- State what has been learned.

## Outcome
A learning analysis.

## Purpose
Relates lessons to one another. Correlation shows lessons that support or contradict each other.

## Activities
- Compare lessons that concern similar situations.
- Record how they relate.

## Outcome
Correlated lessons.

## Purpose
Turns specific lessons into general ones. General lessons apply to more situations.

## Activities
- Identify what a set of lessons share.
- State a broader lesson that covers them.

## Outcome
Generalised lessons.

## Purpose
Adapts a practice using what has been learned. Adaptation makes a practice fit its context.

## Activities
- Decide what to change in the practice in the light of lessons.
- Apply the change.

## Outcome
An adapted practice.

## Purpose
Uses knowledge in the work. Knowledge has value only when applied.

## Activities
- Select the knowledge that applies to the task.
- Apply it and note the effect.

## Outcome
Knowledge applied to work.

## Purpose
Improves a capability. Improvement raises what the organisation is able to do.

## Activities
- Choose the changes that raise the capability.
- Carry them out and check the result.

## Outcome
An improved capability.

## Purpose
Measures outcomes. Measurement turns outcomes into numbers that can be compared.

## Activities
- Select measures that reflect the intended outcome.
- Measure and record them.

## Outcome
Outcome measurements.

## Purpose
Assesses how much improvement has been achieved. Assessment shows whether an investment paid off.

## Activities
- Compare results before and after the improvement.
- State the difference.

## Outcome
An assessment of improvement.

## Purpose
Assesses how well learning works. Assessment shows whether learning leads to better practice.

## Activities
- Examine whether lessons were applied and what followed.
- State how effective the learning has been.

## Outcome
An assessment of learning effectiveness.

## Purpose
Measures a capability. Measurement shows what the capability can do.

## Activities
- Select measures of the capability's output, quality and speed.
- Measure and record them.

## Outcome
Capability measurements.

## Purpose
Assesses the present state of a capability. State assessment shows where the capability stands now.

## Activities
- Compare the capability with its levels of maturity or performance.
- State where it lies.

## Outcome
A capability state assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses the gap between a capability and what is needed. The gap shows how much improvement is required.

## Activities
- Compare the capability with the needed level.
- State the size and nature of the gap.

## Outcome
A capability gap assessment.

## Purpose
Analyses how a capability is structured. Structure shows what makes up the capability.

## Activities
- Examine the roles, processes and tools that make up the capability.
- Describe how they fit together.

## Outcome
An analysis of capability structure.

## Purpose
Analyses what a capability depends on. Dependencies limit what the capability can do.

## Activities
- Identify the people, tools and inputs that the capability needs.
- Describe the effect of losing each.

## Outcome
An analysis of capability dependencies.

## Purpose
Analyses how well a capability performs. Analysis shows where performance is strong or weak.

## Activities
- Examine the measures of output, speed and quality.
- Explain the results.

## Outcome
An analysis of capability performance.

## Purpose
Measures performance. Measurement gives the facts on which analysis is based.

## Activities
- Define the measures and collect the data.
- Report the results.

## Outcome
Performance measurements.

## Purpose
Analyses how performance changes over time. Trends show improvement or decline.

## Activities
- Plot performance measures over a period.
- Interpret the direction and cause of the change.

## Outcome
A performance trend analysis.

## Purpose
Finds what limits throughput. Removing the bottleneck gives the largest gain.

## Activities
- Trace the flow of work to find where it slows or queues.
- Identify the constraint.

## Outcome
An analysis of bottlenecks.

## Purpose
Discovers opportunities to improve. Opportunities must be found before they can be pursued.

## Activities
- Examine work and results for waste and for ways to do better.
- Record each opportunity.

## Outcome
Discovered improvement opportunities.

## Purpose
Compares the current state with the desired state. Gap analysis shows what must change.

## Activities
- Describe the current and desired states.
- List the differences.

## Outcome
A gap analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses how something could be optimised. Analysis shows which changes will help most.

## Activities
- Examine the options for improvement and their effects.
- Select those worth pursuing.

## Outcome
An optimisation analysis.

## Purpose
Simulates the effect of a change before it is made. Simulation shows consequences without risk.

## Activities
- Model the change and its environment.
- Run the model and record the results.

## Outcome
Simulation results.

## Purpose
Carries out an optimisation. Implementation puts the improvement into effect.

## Activities
- Apply the chosen changes.
- Monitor the effect as they take hold.

## Outcome
An implemented optimisation.

## Purpose
Evaluates the result of a change. Evaluation shows whether the change worked.

## Activities
- Compare the result with the intended outcome.
- State what was achieved.

## Outcome
An outcome evaluation.

## Purpose
Discovers the signals that something will be affected. Signals mark where impact analysis must look.

## Activities
- Watch for changes and events that could spread.
- Record the signals found.

## Outcome
Discovered impact signals.

## Purpose
Finds the assets that a change affects. Knowing the affected assets scopes the response.

## Activities
- Trace from the change to the assets that depend on it.
- List them.

## Outcome
Discovered affected assets.

## Purpose
Finds how far a change reaches. Scope determines the amount of work and risk.

## Activities
- Follow the change through the dependencies.
- Describe its extent.

## Outcome
A discovered change scope.

## Purpose
Follows dependencies from one item to those it connects to. Traversal reveals chains of dependence.

## Activities
- Walk the dependency links from a starting item.
- Record each item reached and the path.

## Outcome
A traversal of dependencies.

## Purpose
Assesses the effect of a change. Assessment shows what the change will cost and risk.

## Activities
- Evaluate how each affected item is changed.
- Rate the effect.

## Outcome
A change impact assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses how a change affects requirements. Requirements may need to be changed or retested.

## Activities
- Identify the requirements touched by the change.
- Describe how each is affected.

## Outcome
A statement of requirement impact.

## Purpose
Assesses how a change affects the architecture. Architectural impact is often the costliest.

## Activities
- Identify the components, interfaces and rules touched by the change.
- Describe how each is affected.

## Outcome
A statement of architecture impact.

## Purpose
Assesses how a change affects the implementation. Implementation impact determines the work needed.

## Activities
- Identify the code, data and configuration touched by the change.
- Estimate the work to change each.

## Outcome
A statement of implementation impact.

## Purpose
Analyses dependencies between systems. Cross-system dependencies are often hidden.

## Activities
- Identify the interfaces and shared data between systems.
- Describe which depends on which.

## Outcome
A cross-system dependency analysis.

## Purpose
Assesses how a change in one system affects others. A local change may have wide effects.

## Activities
- Follow the change across the dependencies between systems.
- Rate the effect on each.

## Outcome
A cross-system impact assessment.

## Purpose
Analyses the effect of a change on a whole portfolio. Portfolio impact shows the total cost of a change.

## Activities
- Aggregate the effects across systems and projects.
- Identify where they are greatest.

## Outcome
A portfolio impact analysis.

## Purpose
Maps how an effect spreads. A map shows the route of impact.

## Activities
- Trace the effect from its origin through the dependencies.
- Draw the paths.

## Outcome
An impact propagation map.

## Purpose
Analyses what lies downstream of a change. Downstream items consume what changes.

## Activities
- Identify the items that use the changed item.
- Describe the effect on each.

## Outcome
A downstream impact analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses indirect effects that arise through intermediate items. Transitive effects are easy to miss.

## Activities
- Follow dependencies beyond the first step.
- Describe the indirect effects found.

## Outcome
A transitive impact analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses what is said in meetings to find stakeholder signals. Meetings hold decisions and concerns that are never written elsewhere.

## Activities
- Review the record of the meeting for needs and concerns.
- Record the signals with their speaker.

## Outcome
Signals drawn from meetings.

## Purpose
Analyses tickets to find stakeholder signals. Tickets show what users and teams ask for.

## Activities
- Review the tickets for requests, complaints and patterns.
- Record the signals found.

## Outcome
Signals drawn from tickets.

## Purpose
Analyses support conversations to find stakeholder signals. Support conversations show real difficulties in use.

## Activities
- Review the conversations for problems and unmet needs.
- Record the signals found.

## Outcome
Signals drawn from support conversations.

## Purpose
Analyses communications to find stakeholder signals. Communications carry needs and concerns that are not raised formally.

## Activities
- Review messages, emails and other correspondence for needs and concerns.
- Record the signals with their source.

## Outcome
Signals drawn from communications.

## Purpose
Identifies what a stakeholder intends or wants to achieve. Intent explains the purpose behind what stakeholders say.

## Activities
- Read the signals for the goal that the stakeholder is pursuing.
- State the intent in a clear sentence.

## Outcome
Identified intents.

## Purpose
Extracts the needs that stakeholders express. Needs are what the solution must satisfy.

## Activities
- Identify statements that describe something the stakeholder requires.
- Record each need separately from the solution suggested.

## Outcome
Extracted needs.

## Purpose
Extracts what stakeholders expect. Expectations shape how stakeholders judge a result.

## Activities
- Identify statements that describe what stakeholders assume will happen.
- Record each expectation.

## Outcome
Extracted expectations.

## Purpose
Extracts the concerns that stakeholders raise. Concerns point to risks and quality needs.

## Activities
- Identify statements that express worry or objection.
- Record each concern with its cause.

## Outcome
Extracted concerns.

## Purpose
Resolves conflicts between stakeholder intents. Unresolved conflict stops progress.

## Activities
- Identify the intents that conflict and the parties involved.
- Agree a resolution or record the decision.

## Outcome
Reconciled conflicts.

## Purpose
Compares the intents of stakeholders. Comparison shows where they agree and differ.

## Activities
- Place the intents side by side on the same subject.
- Record the agreements and differences.

## Outcome
An intent comparison.

## Purpose
Combines intents into a consistent set. Consolidation gives a single statement of what is wanted.

## Activities
- Merge intents that are the same and align those that overlap.
- Record the consolidated set.

## Outcome
Consolidated intents.

## Purpose
Converts stakeholder signals into requirements. Conversion gives signals a form that engineering can act on.

## Activities
- Interpret each signal as a statement of what the system must do.
- Write it as a requirement linked to its source.

## Outcome
Requirements derived from signals.

## Purpose
Updates a baseline to reflect agreed change. A baseline must follow approved change to stay valid.

## Activities
- Apply the approved changes to the items in the baseline.
- Record the new state of the baseline.

## Outcome
An updated baseline.

## Purpose
Aligns the baseline with current stakeholder intent. Reconciliation shows where the baseline has fallen behind.

## Activities
- Compare current intent with the baseline requirements.
- Propose changes to remove the differences.

## Outcome
A baseline reconciled with intent.

## Purpose
Observes how the business behaves. Observed behaviour is the reference for the domain model.

## Activities
- Watch how business activities are carried out.
- Record what is seen.

## Outcome
Observations of business behaviour.

## Purpose
Monitors how business processes run. Monitoring shows whether processes follow the model.

## Activities
- Collect data on process execution.
- Compare it with the modelled process.

## Outcome
Monitoring of process behaviour.

## Purpose
Monitors the transactions that the business carries out. Transactions show how the business uses its data.

## Activities
- Collect data on transactions as they occur.
- Examine their form and pattern.

## Outcome
Monitoring of transaction behaviour.

## Purpose
Compares the model with observed behaviour. Comparison shows where the model no longer fits.

## Activities
- Set the observed behaviour beside the modelled behaviour.
- Record the differences.

## Outcome
A model-to-behaviour comparison.

## Purpose
Compares versions of a model. Comparison shows how the model has changed.

## Activities
- Compare the elements of two versions.
- List the additions, removals and modifications.

## Outcome
A comparison of model versions.

## Purpose
Compares the structure of two things. Comparison shows where structures differ or match.

## Activities
- Compare their elements and relationships.
- Record the similarities and differences.

## Outcome
A structural comparison.

## Purpose
Detects when the concepts that the business uses have changed. Changed concepts make the model out of date.

## Activities
- Compare the concepts in the model with those in current use.
- Report those that have changed or been added.

## Outcome
Detected concept drift.

## Purpose
Detects when relationships between things have changed. Changed relationships make the model wrong.

## Activities
- Compare the modelled relationships with the real ones.
- Report the differences.

## Outcome
Detected relationship drift.

## Purpose
Detects when behaviour has moved away from the model. Behaviour drift shows that the model no longer describes reality.

## Activities
- Compare current behaviour with the modelled behaviour.
- Report the departures.

## Outcome
Detected behaviour drift.

## Purpose
Corrects errors in a model. Correction restores accuracy.

## Activities
- Identify the parts of the model that are wrong.
- Revise them to match the evidence.

## Outcome
A corrected model.

## Purpose
Aligns a model with what it represents. Alignment keeps the model useful.

## Activities
- Adjust the model so that its elements correspond to reality.
- Record the changes made.

## Outcome
An aligned model.

## Purpose
Reconciles observed behaviour with the model. Reconciliation decides whether to change the model or the behaviour.

## Activities
- Examine each difference between behaviour and model.
- Decide and apply the change.

## Outcome
Behaviour and model reconciled.

## Purpose
Checks that a model is correct for its purpose. Validation gives confidence that the model can be used.

## Activities
- Check the model against its source and its intended use.
- Record whether it is acceptable.

## Outcome
A validated model.

## Purpose
Checks that the domain model is internally consistent. Inconsistency indicates a modelling error.

## Activities
- Compare the parts of the domain model for agreement.
- Report contradictions.

## Outcome
A consistency check of the domain model.

## Purpose
Monitors how an architecture changes over time. Trends show the direction of evolution.

## Activities
- Record measures of the architecture at regular intervals.
- Report the direction of change.

## Outcome
Monitoring of architecture trends.

## Purpose
Analyses trends in technology. Trends show which technologies are rising or declining.

## Activities
- Examine the adoption and support of the technologies in use.
- Describe the direction of each.

## Outcome
A technology trend analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses how use of the system is changing. Usage trends show where demand is moving.

## Activities
- Examine measures of use over time.
- Describe the changes and what they imply.

## Outcome
A usage trend analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the stage of life that technologies have reached. Lifecycle shows when technologies will need replacing.

## Activities
- Identify where each technology stands from introduction to retirement.
- Describe the consequences.

## Outcome
A technology lifecycle analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses how long technologies will be supported. Support ending creates risk.

## Activities
- Find the dates on which support for each technology will end.
- Describe the exposure that results.

## Outcome
A support lifecycle analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the lifecycle of the things a system depends on. Dependencies that age can threaten the system.

## Activities
- Determine the lifecycle stage of each dependency.
- Describe the risk of each.

## Outcome
A dependency lifecycle analysis.

## Purpose
Detects the signs that something is becoming obsolete. Early signs give time to plan replacement.

## Activities
- Watch for declining support, use and compatibility.
- Report the signs.

## Outcome
Detected obsolescence signals.

## Purpose
Detects technologies that are becoming obsolete. Obsolete technology becomes costly and risky to keep.

## Activities
- Examine each technology for signs of obsolescence.
- List those affected.

## Outcome
Detected technology obsolescence.

## Purpose
Detects design patterns that are becoming obsolete. Patterns lose value when circumstances change.

## Activities
- Examine the patterns in use for signs they no longer suit.
- List those affected.

## Outcome
Detected pattern obsolescence.

## Purpose
Forecasts when things will become obsolete. A forecast lets replacement be planned.

## Activities
- Project the decline of each item from the observed signs.
- State the expected timing.

## Outcome
An obsolescence forecast.

## Purpose
Predicts how a lifecycle will unfold. Prediction shows when stages will end.

## Activities
- Use history and trends to estimate the remaining life.
- State the prediction and its basis.

## Outcome
A lifecycle prediction.

## Purpose
Predicts the risk that obsolescence creates. Prediction shows which obsolescence matters most.

## Activities
- Estimate the likelihood and the effect of each case.
- Rank the cases.

## Outcome
An obsolescence risk prediction.

## Purpose
Analyses how a problem could be remedied. Analysis shows the options and their cost.

## Activities
- Describe each way of remedying the problem.
- Compare their effort, risk and benefit.

## Outcome
A remediation analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses what could replace something. Analysis shows whether replacement is practical.

## Activities
- Identify the candidate replacements.
- Compare them against what is being replaced.

## Outcome
A replacement analysis.

## Purpose
Discovers architectural patterns in systems. Patterns show common solutions and their variants.

## Activities
- Examine architectures for recurring arrangements.
- Describe each pattern and where it appears.

## Outcome
Discovered architecture patterns.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns in structure. Structural patterns reveal common designs and common weaknesses.

## Activities
- Examine structures for repeated arrangements.
- Describe each pattern.

## Outcome
Discovered structural patterns.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns in dependencies. Dependency patterns show habits of coupling.

## Activities
- Examine dependencies for recurring forms.
- Describe each pattern.

## Outcome
Discovered dependency patterns.

## Purpose
Compares the dependencies of different systems or codebases. Comparison shows where they are alike.

## Activities
- Set the dependency structures side by side.
- Record the similarities and differences.

## Outcome
A dependency comparison.

## Purpose
Analyses patterns to understand them. Analysis shows what a pattern means and how it is used.

## Activities
- Examine each pattern's features, uses and effects.
- State what it implies.

## Outcome
A pattern analysis.

## Purpose
Classifies patterns into types. Classification makes patterns easier to find and compare.

## Activities
- Assign each pattern to categories of the scheme.
- Keep the classification consistent.

## Outcome
Classified patterns.

## Purpose
Detects weaknesses in structure. Structural weaknesses limit quality and change.

## Activities
- Examine structures for features that harm quality.
- Report each weakness.

## Outcome
Detected structural weaknesses.

## Purpose
Detects weaknesses that appear repeatedly. Recurrence points to a general cause.

## Activities
- Compare weaknesses across systems.
- Report those that recur.

## Outcome
Detected recurring weaknesses.

## Purpose
Detects unusual structure. Anomalies may be errors or deliberate exceptions.

## Activities
- Look for structure that departs from the norm.
- Report it for review.

## Outcome
Detected structural anomalies.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns in code. Code patterns show common solutions and common faults.

## Activities
- Examine code for repeated forms.
- Describe each pattern.

## Outcome
Discovered code patterns.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns in how things are implemented. They show the habits of those who write the code.

## Activities
- Examine implementations for repeated approaches.
- Describe each pattern.

## Outcome
Discovered implementation patterns.

## Purpose
Discovers patterns in how defects are fixed. Repeated fixes show where a general remedy applies.

## Activities
- Examine fixes for similar changes.
- Describe each pattern of fix.

## Outcome
Discovered fix patterns.

## Purpose
Compares pieces of code. Comparison shows where code is alike or differs.

## Activities
- Compare the code for structure and content.
- Record the similarities and differences.

## Outcome
A code comparison.

## Purpose
Analyses whether a pattern applies in a given place. Applying a pattern where it does not fit causes harm.

## Activities
- Compare the pattern's conditions with the target.
- State whether and how it applies.

## Outcome
A pattern applicability analysis.

## Purpose
Identifies the code that a pattern or change affects. Knowing it scopes the work.

## Activities
- Search the codebase for code that matches the pattern.
- List it.

## Outcome
Identified affected code.

## Purpose
Analyses how context changes the way a pattern should be applied. Context differences can invalidate a direct copy.

## Activities
- Compare the contexts of source and target.
- Describe the adjustments needed.

## Outcome
A contextual variation analysis.

## Purpose
Identifies the change in a target that is equivalent to a change made elsewhere. Equivalent change spreads a benefit.

## Activities
- Map the original change to the target code.
- Describe the matching change.

## Outcome
Identified equivalent changes.

## Purpose
Analyses how a change should be spread to other places. Analysis avoids spreading it where it would harm.

## Activities
- Assess each target for suitability.
- Plan the order and manner of propagation.

## Outcome
A change propagation analysis.

## Purpose
Applies a change to a target. Application puts the change into effect.

## Activities
- Make the identified change in the target.
- Record what was done.

## Outcome
An applied change.

## Purpose
Verifies that a change does what it should. Verification confirms the change is correct and safe.

## Activities
- Test the changed item against its expected behaviour.
- Record the result.

## Outcome
A verified change.

## Purpose
Verifies that things stay consistent after a change. Consistency shows the change did not split behaviour.

## Activities
- Check the changed items against each other.
- Report differences.

## Outcome
A consistency verification.

## Purpose
Verifies that a change remains compatible with what depends on it. Compatibility protects consumers.

## Activities
- Test the changed item with its consumers and dependencies.
- Report any breakage.

## Outcome
A compatibility verification.

## Purpose
Collects configurations from systems. Collected configurations are the basis for monitoring.

## Activities
- Gather the current settings and versions from each system.
- Store them with time and source.

## Outcome
Collected configurations.

## Purpose
Monitors the state of configurations. Monitoring shows changes as they occur.

## Activities
- Compare current configurations with the previous state.
- Report changes.

## Outcome
Monitoring of configuration state.

## Purpose
Monitors environments. Monitoring shows whether environments stay as intended.

## Activities
- Collect the state of each environment.
- Report departures from the expected state.

## Outcome
Monitoring of environments.

## Purpose
Compares the actual state with the desired state. Comparison reveals drift.

## Activities
- Set the actual configuration beside the desired one.
- Record the differences.

## Outcome
A desired-state comparison.

## Purpose
Compares environments with one another. Differences between environments cause failures that cannot be reproduced.

## Activities
- Compare the configurations of the environments.
- List the differences.

## Outcome
An environment comparison.

## Purpose
Compares versions. Comparison shows what changed between versions.

## Activities
- Compare the contents of the versions.
- List the differences.

## Outcome
A version comparison.

## Purpose
Detects when configuration has moved from its intended state. Drift makes systems behave unpredictably.

## Activities
- Compare the live configuration with the intended one.
- Report deviations.

## Outcome
Detected configuration drift.

## Purpose
Detects when environments have diverged. Divergence undermines testing.

## Activities
- Compare environments over time.
- Report the divergence.

## Outcome
Detected environment drift.

## Purpose
Detects when dependencies have changed from what was intended. Dependency drift brings unplanned behaviour.

## Activities
- Compare the versions in use with those expected.
- Report differences.

## Outcome
Detected dependency drift.

## Purpose
Classifies drift by type and seriousness. Classification decides how each drift is handled.

## Activities
- Assign each drift to categories of the scheme.
- Rate its seriousness.

## Outcome
Classified drift.

## Purpose
Analyses what a drift affects. Impact shows how much a drift matters.

## Activities
- Determine what depends on the drifted item.
- Describe the effect on each.

## Outcome
A drift impact analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses why drift occurred. Cause analysis prevents recurrence.

## Activities
- Examine the changes that led to the drift.
- Identify the underlying cause.

## Outcome
A drift cause analysis.

## Purpose
Corrects a configuration that is wrong. Correction restores intended behaviour.

## Activities
- Identify the settings that are wrong.
- Change them to the intended values.

## Outcome
A corrected configuration.

## Purpose
Restores a configuration to a known good state. Restoration undoes unwanted change.

## Activities
- Retrieve the known good configuration.
- Apply it and verify the result.

## Outcome
A restored configuration.

## Purpose
Brings an actual state into line with the desired state. Reconciliation ends drift.

## Activities
- Determine the changes needed to match the desired state.
- Apply them and confirm the match.

## Outcome
A reconciled state.

## Purpose
Measures how much of the system the tests cover. Measurement gives a number to coverage.

## Activities
- Run the tests with coverage tooling.
- Record the coverage figures.

## Outcome
Coverage measurements.

## Purpose
Analyses how coverage changes over time. Trends show whether testing keeps pace with change.

## Activities
- Plot coverage over successive builds.
- Interpret the direction.

## Outcome
A coverage trend analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses defects found in the past. History shows where defects cluster.

## Activities
- Examine past defects by location, cause and type.
- Describe the patterns.

## Outcome
A historical defect analysis.

## Purpose
Classifies defects by type and cause. Classification shows what kinds of defects occur.

## Activities
- Assign each defect to categories of the scheme.
- Keep the classification consistent.

## Outcome
Classified defects.

## Purpose
Relates defects to test coverage. It shows whether defects occur where tests are weak.

## Activities
- Compare the location of defects with coverage of those locations.
- Describe the relationship.

## Outcome
A defect-coverage correlation.

## Purpose
Predicts where gaps are likely to arise. Prediction directs attention before gaps cause harm.

## Activities
- Use trends and history to find where gaps are likely.
- State the predictions.

## Outcome
Predicted gaps.

## Purpose
Predicts where defects are most likely to escape. Prediction guides test effort.

## Activities
- Combine defect history with coverage to estimate exposure.
- Rank the areas by exposure.

## Outcome
A defect exposure prediction.

## Purpose
Predicts the risk that low coverage carries. Prediction shows which gaps matter.

## Activities
- Estimate the likelihood and the effect of failure in poorly covered areas.
- Rank the areas by risk.

## Outcome
A coverage risk prediction.

## Purpose
Identifies tests that should exist but do not. Missing tests leave behaviour unchecked.

## Activities
- Compare requirements and risks with the tests present.
- List the tests that are absent.

## Outcome
Identified missing tests.

## Purpose
Identifies areas where coverage is weak. Weak areas may hide defects.

## Activities
- Find parts of the system with low coverage.
- List them.

## Outcome
Identified weak coverage.

## Purpose
Identifies scenarios that no test exercises. Uncovered scenarios are untested behaviour.

## Activities
- Compare the scenarios that matter with those tested.
- List those not tested.

## Outcome
Identified uncovered scenarios.

## Purpose
Recommends test cases to add. Recommendations turn gaps into work.

## Activities
- Propose cases that would close the gaps.
- State what each would check.

## Outcome
Recommended test cases.

## Purpose
Recommends test scenarios to add. Scenarios test how parts work together.

## Activities
- Propose scenarios that cover untested situations.
- State the expected behaviour.

## Outcome
Recommended test scenarios.

## Purpose
Recommends how to improve coverage. Recommendations focus effort where it pays.

## Activities
- Propose the tests and changes that would raise coverage most.
- Rank them by value.

## Outcome
Coverage improvement recommendations.

## Purpose
Scans systems for known vulnerabilities. Scanning finds weaknesses at scale.

## Activities
- Run scanning tools against the systems and code.
- Collect the findings.

## Outcome
Vulnerability scan results.

## Purpose
Relates vulnerabilities to one another and to assets. Correlation shows which vulnerabilities combine into serious risk.

## Activities
- Link vulnerabilities to the assets and to other findings.
- Describe the combined exposure.

## Outcome
Correlated vulnerabilities.

## Purpose
Discovers where a system is exposed. Exposure must be known to be reduced.

## Activities
- Find the points at which a system can be reached.
- Record each.

## Outcome
Discovered exposure.

## Purpose
Analyses the attack surface of a system. The attack surface is the sum of the ways an attacker could enter.

## Activities
- Enumerate the entry points and the data they expose.
- Assess the size and risk of the surface.

## Outcome
An attack surface analysis.

## Purpose
Assesses how serious exposure is. Assessment ranks exposures for action.

## Activities
- Rate each exposure by how reachable and valuable the target is.
- Rank them.

## Outcome
An exposure assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses how severe an issue is. Severity decides priority.

## Activities
- Judge the consequence if the issue occurs.
- Assign a severity.

## Outcome
A severity assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses how easily a vulnerability can be exploited. Ease of exploitation drives urgency.

## Activities
- Judge the skill, access and conditions an attacker would need.
- State the ease of exploitation.

## Outcome
An exploitability assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses what harm an exploited vulnerability would do. Impact completes the picture of risk.

## Activities
- Judge the effect on data, service and reputation.
- State the impact.

## Outcome
A vulnerability impact assessment.

## Purpose
Monitors vulnerabilities over time. Monitoring shows the changing position.

## Activities
- Track newly found and changed vulnerabilities.
- Report the position.

## Outcome
Monitoring of vulnerabilities.

## Purpose
Tracks the state of each vulnerability. State tracking shows what is open and what is closed.

## Activities
- Record the status of each vulnerability from discovery to closure.
- Report what remains open.

## Outcome
Tracked vulnerability states.

## Purpose
Monitors the progress of remediation work. Monitoring shows whether weaknesses are being closed.

## Activities
- Track each remediation action against its plan.
- Report actions that are late or ineffective.

## Outcome
Monitoring of remediation.

## Purpose
Measures the security posture of a system. Measurement provides a baseline for comparison.

## Activities
- Select the measures that describe the strength of defences.
- Collect and record them.

## Outcome
Posture measurements.

## Purpose
Measures how exposed a system is. Measurement shows whether exposure is rising or falling.

## Activities
- Count and size the points of exposure.
- Record them over time.

## Outcome
Exposure measurements.

## Purpose
Assesses the overall security state of a system. Assessment gives a single judgement of how secure it is.

## Activities
- Combine the findings on vulnerabilities, controls and exposure.
- State the overall state.

## Outcome
A security state assessment.

## Purpose
Analyses intelligence about threats. Intelligence shows what attackers are doing.

## Activities
- Review reports and feeds on threat activity.
- Extract what is relevant to the organisation.

## Outcome
A threat intelligence analysis.

## Purpose
Discovers threat patterns that are only beginning to appear. Early discovery gives time to prepare.

## Activities
- Watch for new forms and combinations of attack.
- Describe each emerging pattern.

## Outcome
Discovered emerging patterns.

## Purpose
Analyses how attacks are carried out. Understanding attack patterns shows how to defend.

## Activities
- Examine the steps, tools and targets of attacks.
- Describe the typical pattern.

## Outcome
An attack pattern analysis.

## Purpose
Relates threats to the assets they could harm. Correlation shows which assets are at risk.

## Activities
- Match each threat with the assets it targets.
- Record the match.

## Outcome
Threats correlated with assets.

## Purpose
Relates threats to the vulnerabilities they could exploit. Correlation shows which weaknesses are urgent.

## Activities
- Match each threat with the weaknesses it could use.
- Record the match.

## Outcome
Threats correlated with vulnerabilities.

## Purpose
Relates threats across systems. A threat to one system may reach others.

## Activities
- Compare the threats facing connected systems.
- Describe those that cross systems.

## Outcome
Correlated cross-system threats.

## Purpose
Evaluates a threat. Evaluation shows how dangerous it is.

## Activities
- Judge the capability and intent behind the threat.
- State the level of danger.

## Outcome
A threat evaluation.

## Purpose
Assesses whether a threat is relevant to the organisation. Not every threat applies.

## Activities
- Compare the threat with the organisation's assets and exposure.
- State whether it is relevant.

## Outcome
A threat relevance assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses what harm a threat could do. Impact shows how much it matters.

## Activities
- Judge the effect on data, service and trust if the threat succeeded.
- State the impact.

## Outcome
A threat impact assessment.

## Purpose
Predicts how threat patterns will develop. Prediction shows where defences will be needed.

## Activities
- Extend observed patterns forward.
- State the expected forms of attack.

## Outcome
A threat pattern prediction.

## Purpose
Forecasts the threats that are likely to arise. A forecast guides preparation.

## Activities
- Combine intelligence and history to project threats.
- State the expected level and timing.

## Outcome
A threat forecast.

## Purpose
Predicts how exposure will change. Prediction shows where exposure will grow.

## Activities
- Project the effect of planned change and trends on exposure.
- State the expected exposure.

## Outcome
An exposure prediction.

## Purpose
Analyses exposure before it is exploited. Pre-emptive analysis closes gaps first.

## Activities
- Examine the system for exposure that has not yet been targeted.
- Rank it by likelihood of attack.

## Outcome
A pre-emptive exposure analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses which controls would prevent harm. Analysis shows which controls to apply.

## Activities
- Compare available controls with the exposures.
- Judge how well each would prevent attack.

## Outcome
A preventive control analysis.

## Purpose
Identifies actions that would prevent a threat. Identified actions turn analysis into work.

## Activities
- List the actions that would reduce the chance of harm.
- Describe the benefit and cost of each.

## Outcome
Identified preventive actions.

## Purpose
Extracts policies from source documents. Extraction makes policies available for comparison.

## Activities
- Read the documents and identify each policy statement.
- Record each with its source.

## Outcome
Extracted policies.

## Purpose
Interprets what a policy requires. Interpretation removes ambiguity.

## Activities
- Read the policy in its context.
- State what it requires in precise terms.

## Outcome
Interpreted policies.

## Purpose
Compares policies. Comparison shows where policies overlap or differ.

## Activities
- Set policies on the same subject side by side.
- Record agreements and differences.

## Outcome
A policy comparison.

## Purpose
Compares rules. Comparison shows where rules agree and conflict.

## Activities
- Compare the conditions and actions of rules that concern the same subject.
- Record the differences.

## Outcome
A rule comparison.

## Purpose
Analyses how rules relate to one another. Relationships show which rules depend on or override others.

## Activities
- Identify rules that refine, depend on or override others.
- Describe the relationships.

## Outcome
A rule relationship analysis.

## Purpose
Detects conflicts between policies. Conflicting policies cannot all be obeyed.

## Activities
- Compare policies for requirements that cannot both be met.
- Report each conflict.

## Outcome
Detected policy conflicts.

## Purpose
Detects conflicts between rules. Rules that conflict give contradictory instructions.

## Activities
- Compare rules for conditions that lead to opposite actions.
- Report each conflict.

## Outcome
Detected rule conflicts.

## Purpose
Analyses a contradiction. Analysis shows what lies behind it and how to resolve it.

## Activities
- Examine the statements that contradict.
- Explain the cause.

## Outcome
A contradiction analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the context in which a conflict arises. Context shows whether the conflict is real.

## Activities
- Examine the circumstances in which each conflicting item applies.
- State whether the contexts overlap.

## Outcome
A conflict context analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the effect of a conflict. Impact shows how urgent it is to resolve.

## Activities
- Identify what is affected by the conflict.
- Describe the consequence.

## Outcome
A conflict impact analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses ways of resolving a conflict. Analysis prepares the decision.

## Activities
- List the options for resolving the conflict.
- Compare their effects.

## Outcome
A conflict resolution analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses alternative readings of a statement. A different reading may remove an apparent conflict.

## Activities
- Describe the other plausible meanings.
- State what each would imply.

## Outcome
An alternative interpretation analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses how conflicting items could be brought into agreement. Reconciliation avoids discarding either side.

## Activities
- Identify the changes that would make the items agree.
- Compare them for cost and effect.

## Outcome
A reconciliation analysis.

## Purpose
Identifies the risks of a release. Risks must be known before release.

## Activities
- Examine the contents and circumstances of the release.
- Record the risks found.

## Outcome
Identified release risks.

## Purpose
Assesses the risks of a release. Assessment shows which risks need action.

## Activities
- Judge the likelihood and impact of each risk.
- Rank them.

## Outcome
A release risk assessment.

## Purpose
Relates release risks to one another. Correlation shows risks that compound.

## Activities
- Compare the risks for shared causes and effects.
- Describe those that combine.

## Outcome
Correlated release risks.

## Purpose
Analyses past releases. History shows what to expect.

## Activities
- Examine previous releases for scope, outcome and problems.
- Describe what they show.

## Outcome
A historical release analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses how releases turned out. Outcomes show how well releases went.

## Activities
- Compare the results of each release with its goals.
- State what accounts for the differences.

## Outcome
A release outcome analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the patterns in which failures occur. Patterns show what tends to go wrong.

## Activities
- Examine failures for common causes and conditions.
- Describe each pattern.

## Outcome
A failure pattern analysis.

## Purpose
Predicts the risk of a release. Prediction guides decisions about readiness.

## Activities
- Use history and current conditions to estimate release risk.
- State the prediction and its basis.

## Outcome
A release risk prediction.

## Purpose
Predicts failures. Prediction allows preventive action.

## Activities
- Use patterns and signals to estimate where failure is likely.
- State the prediction.

## Outcome
A failure prediction.

## Purpose
Predicts the outcome of something. Prediction shows what is likely to result.

## Activities
- Use history and current conditions to estimate the result.
- State the prediction and its confidence.

## Outcome
An outcome prediction.

## Purpose
Tracks the state of risks. Tracking shows which are open, reduced or closed.

## Activities
- Record the status of each risk over time.
- Report the current position.

## Outcome
Tracked risk states.

## Purpose
Assesses the impact of the changes in a release. It shows how much the release alters.

## Activities
- Examine each change in the release for its effect.
- Summarise the impact.

## Outcome
A release change impact assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses how a release affects its dependencies. Consumers may break if dependencies change.

## Activities
- Identify those that depend on what the release changes.
- Describe the effect on each.

## Outcome
A release dependency impact assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses the effect of the scope of a release. Larger scope usually brings larger risk.

## Activities
- Judge the effect of the amount and kind of content in the release.
- State the implications.

## Outcome
A release scope impact assessment.

## Purpose
Collects telemetry from systems. Collection provides the data for analysis.

## Activities
- Gather metrics, logs and traces from running systems.
- Store them with time and source.

## Outcome
Collected telemetry.

## Purpose
Analyses telemetry to understand system behaviour. Analysis turns raw data into insight.

## Activities
- Examine the telemetry for trends and changes.
- Describe what it shows.

## Outcome
A telemetry analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses signals in data. Signals indicate that something is happening.

## Activities
- Separate meaningful signals from noise.
- Describe what the signals indicate.

## Outcome
A signal analysis.

## Purpose
Identifies unusual data points. Anomalies may show a problem.

## Activities
- Compare observations with normal behaviour.
- List those that depart from it.

## Outcome
Identified anomalies.

## Purpose
Detects when behaviour deviates from its normal pattern. Deviation may signal a fault or an attack.

## Activities
- Compare current behaviour with the established pattern.
- Report the deviations.

## Outcome
Detected behavioural deviations.

## Purpose
Analyses the thresholds at which action should be taken. Good thresholds give timely warning without false alarms.

## Activities
- Examine how measures behave around alert levels.
- Recommend the thresholds.

## Outcome
A threshold analysis.

## Purpose
Relates events that belong together. Correlation shows which events share a cause.

## Activities
- Group events by time, source and effect.
- Describe the relationships.

## Outcome
Correlated events.

## Purpose
Relates signals from different sources. Correlation confirms that a signal is real.

## Activities
- Compare signals for agreement.
- Describe those that occur together.

## Outcome
Correlated signals.

## Purpose
Relates events by their timing. Timing shows which events lead to which.

## Activities
- Order the events in time.
- Describe the sequences that recur.

## Outcome
A temporal correlation.

## Purpose
Identifies the events that come before an incident. Precursors give warning.

## Activities
- Examine incidents for what preceded them.
- List the common precursors.

## Outcome
Identified precursors.

## Purpose
Detects the indicators that lead an event. A leading indicator moves before the event it predicts.

## Activities
- Search the measures for those that change first.
