Captures evidence of a defect. Evidence helps diagnosis.

## Activities
- Collect logs, screenshots and data showing the defect.
- Attach them to the defect record.

## Outcome
Captured defect evidence.

## Purpose
Captures the information needed to reproduce a defect. Without it, developers cannot recreate the problem.

## Activities
- Record the steps, data, environment and version in which the defect appears.
- Attach the information to the defect record.

## Outcome
Captured reproduction information.

## Purpose
Assesses what a defect affects. Impact determines how urgently it needs a fix.

## Activities
- Judge the effect on users, data and service.
- Record the impact.

## Outcome
A defect impact assessment.

## Purpose
Orders defects for resolution. Ordering applies effort to what matters most.

## Activities
- Rank the defects by severity and priority.
- Record the order.

## Outcome
An ordered list of defects.

## Purpose
Corrects a defect. Correction removes the fault.

## Activities
- Change the system to eliminate the cause of the defect.
- Record the change.

## Outcome
A corrected defect.

## Purpose
Makes the change that corrects a fault. A corrective change restores intended behaviour.

## Activities
- Write and apply the correction.
- Link it to the defect.

## Outcome
A corrective change.

## Purpose
Implements the chosen resolution. Implementation puts the resolution into effect.

## Activities
- Carry out the changes that resolve the defect.
- Hand the result to verification.

## Outcome
An implemented resolution.

## Purpose
Verifies that a correction caused no regression. Verification protects what already worked.

## Activities
- Run the tests that cover related behaviour.
- Record any new failure.

## Outcome
A regression verification.

## Purpose
Validates that a resolution solves the problem. Validation confirms that the fix meets the original need.

## Activities
- Check the resolved behaviour against the defect report.
- Record whether it is acceptable.

## Outcome
A validated resolution.

## Purpose
Assesses whether a defect can be closed. Assessment prevents premature closure.

## Activities
- Check that the defect is resolved, verified or properly deferred.
- State whether it can be closed.

## Outcome
A closure assessment.

## Purpose
Closes a defect. Closure ends its life in an orderly way.

## Activities
- Record the final state, the resolution and the date.
- Notify those concerned.

## Outcome
A closed defect.

## Purpose
Tracks defects that have been deferred. Tracking keeps them from being forgotten.

## Activities
- Record why each defect was deferred and the conditions to revisit it.
- Review them at agreed intervals.

## Outcome
Tracked deferred defects.

## Purpose
Identifies possible suppliers. Identification gives a pool to choose from.

## Activities
- Search for suppliers able to meet the need.
- List them.

## Outcome
Identified suppliers.

## Purpose
Evaluates suppliers. Evaluation shows which are suitable.

## Activities
- Assess each supplier against the criteria.
- Record the results.

## Outcome
Supplier evaluations.

## Purpose
Chooses a supplier. Selection commits the organisation to a supplier.

## Activities
- Compare the evaluations and choose the supplier.
- Record the reasons.

## Outcome
A selected supplier.

## Purpose
Defines a contract. A contract sets out the obligations of each party.

## Activities
- State the terms, deliverables, obligations and remedies.
- Agree them with the parties.

## Outcome
A defined contract.

## Purpose
Defines a service. A definition states what is provided and to what standard.

## Activities
- Describe the service, its levels and its limits.
- Agree it with the provider and consumer.

## Outcome
A defined service.

## Purpose
Assesses a service. Assessment shows whether it is delivered as agreed.

## Activities
- Compare the service provided with the agreed levels.
- Record the findings.

## Outcome
A service assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses a deliverable. Assessment shows whether it meets its definition.

## Activities
- Compare the deliverable received with its definition and criteria.
- Record the result.

## Outcome
A deliverable assessment.

## Purpose
Identifies the risks that a supplier brings. Dependence on a supplier brings specific risks.

## Activities
- Examine the supplier's finances, delivery record and dependencies.
- List the risks.

## Outcome
Identified supplier risks.

## Purpose
Assesses supplier risks. Assessment shows which risks need action.

## Activities
- Judge the likelihood and effect of each risk.
- Rank them.

## Outcome
A supplier risk assessment.

## Purpose
Monitors supplier risks. Monitoring shows changes in exposure.

## Activities
- Track the indicators of each risk.
- Report changes.

## Outcome
Monitoring of supplier risks.

## Purpose
Checks that a supplier meets requirements. Checking shows obligations are honoured.

## Activities
- Compare the supplier's work with the contract requirements.
- Record the gaps.

## Outcome
A requirement compliance check.

## Purpose
Reviews the evidence a supplier provides. Review shows whether the evidence is credible.

## Activities
- Examine reports, certificates and records.
- Record whether they support the claims.

## Outcome
An evidence review.

## Purpose
Communicates with a supplier. Clear communication keeps the arrangement working.

## Activities
- Exchange information and decisions with the supplier.
- Record what was agreed.

## Outcome
Supplier communication.

## Purpose
Resolves issues with a supplier. Resolution keeps the relationship productive.

## Activities
- Raise each issue and agree a solution.
- Track it to closure.

## Outcome
Resolved issues.

## Purpose
Reviews the relationship with a supplier. Review shows whether it should continue or change.

## Activities
- Assess performance, communication and value over the period.
- Record the findings and actions.

## Outcome
A relationship review.

## Purpose
Assesses the performance of a capability. Assessment shows how well it works.

## Activities
- Compare the measures of the capability with its targets.
- State the result.

## Outcome
A capability performance assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses the maturity of a capability. Assessment shows what stage it has reached.

## Activities
- Apply the maturity model to the capability.
- State the level reached.

## Outcome
A maturity assessment.

## Purpose
Analyses the gap between performance and its target. The gap shows where improvement is needed.

## Activities
- Compare actual performance with the target.
- Describe the shortfall.

## Outcome
A performance gap analysis.

## Purpose
Defines the objectives of capability evolution. Objectives give direction.

## Activities
- State what the capability should become.
- Agree the objectives.

## Outcome
Defined evolution objectives.

## Purpose
Plans the evolution of a capability. A plan shows the steps.

## Activities
- Set out the stages, actions and timing.
- Agree the plan.

## Outcome
An evolution plan.

## Purpose
Prioritises evolution steps. Priority puts the most valuable steps first.

## Activities
- Rank the steps by value, effort and dependency.
- Record the order.

## Outcome
Prioritised evolution steps.

## Purpose
Enhances an existing capability. Enhancement makes it do its work better.

## Activities
- Make changes that improve quality, speed or reach.
- Check the effect.

## Outcome
An enhanced capability.

## Purpose
Expands a capability. Expansion extends what the organisation can do.

## Activities
- Add new skills, tools or coverage.
- Check that they work.

## Outcome
An expanded capability.

## Purpose
Monitors progress. Monitoring shows whether work is on course.

## Activities
- Compare progress with the plan.
- Report differences.

## Outcome
Progress monitoring.

## Purpose
Assesses progress in maturity. Assessment shows whether the capability is developing.

## Activities
- Compare current maturity with earlier measures.
- State the progress made.

## Outcome
A maturity progress assessment.

## Purpose
Captures proposals for change. Capture ensures that suggestions are recorded.

## Activities
- Record each proposal with its originator and reason.
- Store it for review.

## Outcome
A captured change proposal.

## Purpose
Records change requests formally. A record allows control and traceability.

## Activities
- Enter the request in the change log with its details.
- Give it an identifier and status.

## Outcome
A recorded change request.

## Purpose
Defines the scope of a change. Scope sets what the change will and will not touch.

## Activities
- State the items affected and the extent of the change.
- Agree it.

## Outcome
A defined change scope.

## Purpose
Analyses the effect of a change on requirements. Requirements may need revising or retesting.

## Activities
- Identify the requirements that the change touches.
- Describe the effect on each.

## Outcome
A requirement impact analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the effect of a change on the architecture. Architectural effects are often the costliest.

## Activities
- Identify the components and interfaces the change touches.
- Describe the effect on each.

## Outcome
An architecture impact analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the effect of a change on the implementation. It determines the work needed.

## Activities
- Identify the code, data and configuration the change touches.
- Estimate the work for each.

## Outcome
An implementation impact analysis.

## Purpose
Analyses the effect of a change on dependencies. Dependent items may break.

## Activities
- Identify the items that depend on what changes.
- Describe the effect on each.

## Outcome
A dependency impact analysis.

## Purpose
Assesses whether a change is justified. Assessment avoids unnecessary change.

## Activities
- Compare the benefit with the cost and risk.
- State whether it is warranted.

## Outcome
A change justification assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses the risk of a change. Risk shows what could go wrong.

## Activities
- Judge the likelihood and effect of failure.
- State the level of risk.

## Outcome
A change risk assessment.

## Purpose
Analyses the consequences of a change. Analysis shows what will follow.

## Activities
- Trace the effects on people, systems and plans.
- Describe them.

## Outcome
A change consequence analysis.

## Purpose
Plans a change. A plan sets out how the change will be made.

## Activities
- Define the steps, owners and checks.
- Agree the plan.

## Outcome
A change plan.

## Purpose
Schedules a change. A schedule sets when the change will happen.

## Activities
- Choose a time that suits those affected.
- Record it.

## Outcome
A change schedule.

## Purpose
Coordinates the dependencies of a change. Coordination avoids clashes.

## Activities
- Identify related changes and the order they require.
- Arrange them.

## Outcome
Coordinated change dependencies.

## Purpose
Integrates a change with the rest of the system. Integration makes the change part of the whole.

## Activities
- Combine the change with other work.
- Test that they work together.

## Outcome
An integrated change.

## Purpose
Records the state that results from a change. It shows what the system looks like afterwards.

## Activities
- Capture the new configuration and versions.
- Link it to the change.

## Outcome
A recorded resulting state.

## Purpose
Collects data for training models. Training needs sufficient and relevant data.

## Activities
- Gather data from the sources identified.
- Record its origin and terms of use.

## Outcome
Collected training data.

## Purpose
Prepares data for use. Preparation makes data suitable.

## Activities
- Clean, label and format the data.
- Record the steps taken.

## Outcome
Prepared data.

## Purpose
Assesses the quality of data. Quality determines how good a model can be.

## Activities
- Check completeness, accuracy and balance of the data.
- Record the findings.

## Outcome
A data quality assessment.

## Purpose
Prepares the data used to evaluate models. Evaluation needs data separate from training.

## Activities
- Set aside and prepare data that represents real use.
- Keep it apart from the training data.

## Outcome
Prepared evaluation data.

## Purpose
Trains a model. Training produces a model that learns from data.

## Activities
- Run the training procedure on the prepared data.
- Record the settings and results.

## Outcome
A trained model.

## Purpose
Fine-tunes a model. Fine-tuning adapts a model to a specific purpose.

## Activities
- Continue training on specialised data.
- Record the settings and results.

## Outcome
A fine-tuned model.

## Purpose
Configures the training. Configuration governs how the model learns.

## Activities
- Set the parameters, data splits and resources.
- Record the configuration.

## Outcome
A training configuration.

## Purpose
Evaluates how well a model performs. Evaluation shows whether it is accurate enough.

## Activities
- Measure the model against the evaluation data.
- Record the measures.

## Outcome
A model performance evaluation.

## Purpose
Evaluates a model against acceptance criteria. Evaluation shows whether it is acceptable.

## Activities
- Apply each acceptance criterion to the model results.
- State whether each is met.

## Outcome
An acceptance evaluation.

## Purpose
Compares models. Comparison shows which is better.

## Activities
- Evaluate the models on the same data and measures.
- Present the differences.

## Outcome
A comparative evaluation.

## Purpose
Assesses a model for bias. Bias leads to unfair results.

## Activities
- Test the model's results across groups.
- Record any systematic differences.

## Outcome
A bias assessment.

## Purpose
Analyses the errors a model makes. Analysis shows where and why it fails.

## Activities
- Examine incorrect outputs for patterns.
- Describe the causes.

## Outcome
An error analysis.

## Purpose
Assesses whether acceptance criteria are met. Assessment is the basis for the readiness decision.

## Activities
- Compare each criterion with the evaluation results.
- State whether met.

## Outcome
An acceptance criteria assessment.

## Purpose
Assesses whether a model is ready to deploy. Assessment protects users from a model that is not ready.

## Activities
- Check quality, operations, monitoring and rollback readiness.
- State whether deployment may proceed.

## Outcome
A deployment readiness assessment.

## Purpose
Writes firmware code. Firmware code runs directly on the device.

## Activities
- Implement the functions the design requires.
- Follow the standards for embedded code.

## Outcome
Firmware code.

## Purpose
Implements the software interface to hardware. This lets firmware control the device.

## Activities
- Write the code that reads and writes registers, buses and signals.
- Test it against the hardware.

## Outcome
A hardware interface implementation.

## Purpose
Implements a feature of an embedded system. Features deliver value to users of the device.

## Activities
- Build the feature within the limits of the hardware.
- Test it on the device.

## Outcome
An implemented embedded feature.

## Purpose
Handles the limits of memory. Memory in embedded devices is small.

## Activities
- Design data and code to fit the available memory.
- Verify the use of memory.

## Outcome
Memory constraints handled.

## Purpose
Handles timing limits. Embedded systems must respond within set times.

## Activities
- Design tasks to meet their deadlines.
- Verify the timing.

## Outcome
Timing constraints handled.

## Purpose
Handles limits on power. Battery and thermal limits constrain devices.

## Activities
- Design behaviour to stay within the power budget.
- Verify the consumption.

## Outcome
Power constraints handled.

## Purpose
Integrates software with hardware. Integration shows whether the two work together.

## Activities
- Connect the software to the hardware.
- Test the combination.

## Outcome
Integrated hardware and software.

## Purpose
Integrates peripherals. Peripherals extend what the device can do.

## Activities
- Connect and configure each peripheral.
- Test its operation.

## Outcome
Integrated peripherals.

## Purpose
Integrates firmware with the hardware platform. Integration shows that the firmware runs on the real device.

## Activities
- Load the firmware onto the hardware.
- Test basic and full operation.

## Outcome
Integrated firmware and hardware.

## Purpose
Tests firmware. Testing shows whether it behaves correctly.

## Activities
- Run tests against the firmware requirements.
- Record the results.

## Outcome
Firmware test results.

## Purpose
Tests firmware with real hardware in a simulated environment. This reveals behaviour that pure simulation cannot.

## Activities
- Connect the hardware to a simulated environment.
- Run the tests and record the results.

## Outcome
Hardware-in-the-loop results.

## Purpose
Verifies that timing requirements are met. Failure to meet timing can be unsafe.

## Activities
- Measure response and execution times.
- Compare them with the deadlines.

## Outcome
A timing verification.

## Purpose
Verifies that power requirements are met. Excess power use shortens battery life.

## Activities
- Measure power use in the operating modes.
- Compare it with the budget.

## Outcome
A power verification.

## Purpose
Debugs firmware while it runs. Runtime debugging finds faults that occur in operation.

## Activities
- Observe the running device with debugging tools.
- Locate the fault.

## Outcome
A runtime debugging result.

## Purpose
Debugs faults that come from hardware. Hardware faults can look like software faults.

## Activities
- Use instruments to examine signals and behaviour.
- Isolate the hardware cause.

## Outcome
A hardware debugging result.

## Purpose
Diagnoses faults. Diagnosis finds the cause.

## Activities
- Examine symptoms, logs and measurements.
- State the cause.

## Outcome
A fault diagnosis.

## Purpose
Connects to data sources. A connection is needed before data can flow.

## Activities
- Configure access to each source.
- Test the connection.

## Outcome
Connected sources.

## Purpose
Extracts data from sources. Extraction retrieves what the pipeline needs.

## Activities
- Read the required data from each source.
- Record what was read.

## Outcome
Extracted data.

## Purpose
Brings data into a platform. Ingestion makes data available for use.

## Activities
- Load the extracted data into the target.
- Check that it arrived completely.

## Outcome
Ingested data.

## Purpose
Transforms data. Transformation changes data into the form needed.

## Activities
- Apply the rules that reshape, clean and enrich the data.
- Check the result.

## Outcome
Transformed data.

## Purpose
Maps data from one structure to another. Mapping states how fields correspond.

## Activities
- Define each field's source and target.
- Document the mapping.

## Outcome
A data mapping.

## Purpose
Normalises data. Normalisation gives equivalent values a single form.

## Activities
- Apply common formats and units.
- Check consistency.

## Outcome
Normalised data.

## Purpose
Implements a pipeline. Implementation builds the working flow.

## Activities
- Write the steps and configuration that make the pipeline.
- Test them.

## Outcome
An implemented pipeline.

## Purpose
Orchestrates the steps of a pipeline. Orchestration controls order and timing.

## Activities
- Define when and in what order the steps run.
- Handle dependencies and retries.

## Outcome
An orchestrated pipeline.

## Purpose
Integrates a pipeline with other systems. Integration lets data flow between systems.

## Activities
- Connect the pipeline to its sources, targets and tools.
- Test the connections.

## Outcome
An integrated pipeline.

## Purpose
Checks the quality of data. Checking protects consumers of the data.

## Activities
- Apply the rules for completeness, accuracy and consistency.
- Report failures.

## Outcome
Data quality checks.

## Purpose
Validates data. Validation confirms that data meets its rules.

## Activities
- Check data against schemas and rules.
- Reject or flag invalid data.

## Outcome
Validated data.

## Purpose
Detects anomalies in data. Anomalies may signal errors.

## Activities
- Compare data against expected patterns.
- Report unusual values.

## Outcome
Detected data anomalies.

## Purpose
Monitors a pipeline. Monitoring shows whether it is running correctly.

## Activities
- Watch execution, throughput and errors.
- Raise alerts for problems.

## Outcome
Pipeline monitoring.

## Purpose
Handles pipeline failures. Handling limits the damage.

## Activities
- Detect the failure, recover and restart the run.
- Record what happened.

## Outcome
Handled pipeline failures.

## Purpose
Maintains a pipeline. Maintenance keeps it working as sources and needs change.

## Activities
- Update the pipeline for changed sources, schemas and requirements.
- Test the changes.

## Outcome
A maintained pipeline.

description:
## Purpose
Plans engineering work by defining its scope, breaking it down and setting its milestones. A plan gives a team a shared understanding of what is to be delivered.

## Responsibilities
- Define the scope of the work.
- Break the work down into manageable parts.
- Plan the milestones.

## Outcome
A work plan with a defined scope, a breakdown and milestones.

## Purpose
Defines scope. Scope states what is included.

## Activities
- State the work in and out of scope.
- Agree it.

## Outcome
A defined scope.

## Purpose
Breaks work into smaller parts. Breakdown makes work plannable and assignable.

## Activities
- Divide the work into tasks of manageable size.
- Organise them in a hierarchy.

## Outcome
A work breakdown.

## Purpose
Plans milestones. Milestones mark progress.

## Activities
- Identify the points at which key results are reached.
- Set dates.

## Outcome
Planned milestones.

## Purpose
Estimates the effort that work will take and calibrates the estimates against experience. Estimates allow a plan to be judged for realism.

## Responsibilities
- Estimate the effort of the work.
- Calibrate estimates using actual results.

## Outcome
Effort estimates that are calibrated against past performance.

## Purpose
Estimates the effort of work. Estimates support planning.

## Activities
- Judge the effort each task needs using experience and data.
- Record the estimates and their basis.

## Outcome
Effort estimates.

## Purpose
Calibrates estimates against actual results. Calibration makes later estimates more reliable.

## Activities
- Compare past estimates with the effort actually spent.
- Adjust the estimating method for the bias found.

## Outcome
A calibrated estimating method.

## Purpose
Builds the schedule of work and assigns the resources needed to carry it out. A schedule turns a plan into dates and people.

## Responsibilities
- Construct the schedule.
- Allocate resources to the work.
- Sequence the work according to its dependencies.

## Outcome
A schedule with resources allocated and the work in a workable order.

## Purpose
Builds the schedule of work. A schedule shows when each task occurs.

## Activities
- Place tasks on a timeline according to duration and dependency.
- Check that the schedule meets the milestones.

## Outcome
A schedule.

## Purpose
Allocates people and other resources to tasks. Allocation makes sure that work can be done.

## Activities
- Match tasks with available people and tools.
- Resolve overloads.

## Outcome
An allocation of resources.

## Purpose
Orders tasks by their dependencies. Sequencing prevents work starting before its inputs exist.

## Activities
- Identify which tasks depend on others.
- Order them accordingly.

## Outcome
A dependency sequence.

## Purpose
Measures progress against the plan, analyses variances and updates forecasts. Tracking shows early whether delivery is on course.

## Responsibilities
- Measure progress.
- Analyse the variance from the plan.
- Update the forecast.

## Outcome
A current view of progress and a forecast of completion.

## Purpose
Measures progress. Measurement shows how much has been done.

## Activities
- Record work completed against the plan.
- Report the measures.

## Outcome
Progress measurements.

## Purpose
Updates the forecast of completion. An updated forecast reflects real progress.

## Activities
- Recalculate the remaining effort and dates.
- Report the new forecast.

## Outcome
An updated forecast.

## Purpose
Discovers the risks that threaten engineering work and records them. A risk that has not been identified cannot be managed.

## Responsibilities
- Discover risks.
- Register each risk.

## Outcome
A register of the risks to the engineering work.

## Purpose
Records risks in a register. A register makes risks visible and manageable.

## Activities
- Enter each risk with its description, cause and owner.
- Keep the register current.

## Outcome
A risk register entry.

## Purpose
Analyses each risk for its likelihood and its impact and ranks the risks. Analysis shows which risks need action first.

## Responsibilities
- Assess the likelihood of each risk.
- Assess the impact of each risk.
- Prioritise the risks.

## Outcome
A prioritised list of risks.

## Purpose
Assesses how likely a risk is. Likelihood is one half of risk exposure.

## Activities
- Judge the chance that the risk will occur.
- Record the rating and the reason.

## Outcome
A likelihood assessment.

## Purpose
Ranks risks. Ranking directs attention to the most serious risks.

## Activities
- Combine likelihood and impact into an exposure rating.
- Order the risks by exposure.

## Outcome
Prioritised risks.

## Purpose
Plans how each risk will be reduced and what will be done if it occurs. Mitigation turns risk analysis into action.

## Responsibilities
- Plan the mitigation of each risk.
- Plan the contingency for each risk.

## Outcome
Mitigation and contingency plans for the significant risks.

## Purpose
Plans how to reduce a risk. A plan states what will be done to lower likelihood or impact.

## Activities
- Define actions that reduce the risk.
- Assign owners and dates.

## Outcome
A mitigation plan.

## Purpose
Plans what to do if a risk occurs. A contingency plan limits damage.

## Activities
- Define the response that will be used if the risk materialises.
- State the trigger that starts it.

## Outcome
A contingency plan.

## Purpose
Tracks risks over time and detects the events that show a risk is about to occur. Monitoring keeps the risk register accurate and gives warning.

## Responsibilities
- Track the status of each risk.
- Detect the triggers that show a risk is materialising.

## Outcome
A current risk register with warnings of risks that are materialising.

## Purpose
Tracks risks over time. Tracking shows how each risk is changing.

## Activities
- Update each risk's status and ratings regularly.
- Report changes.

## Outcome
Tracked risks.

## Purpose
Detects the events that show a risk is occurring. Detection starts the contingency response.

## Activities
- Watch for the defined trigger conditions.
- Raise an alert when one is met.

## Outcome
Detected triggers.

## Purpose
Defines the scope of testing and the approach that will be used. A test strategy ensures that testing effort is directed at what matters.

## Responsibilities
- Define the scope of testing.
- Select the approach to testing.

## Outcome
A test strategy that states what will be tested and how.

## Purpose
Defines what testing will cover. A defined scope focuses effort.

## Activities
- State the features, risks and levels of testing.
- State what is excluded.

## Outcome
A defined test scope.

## Purpose
Selects how testing will be done. The approach determines methods and tools.

## Activities
- Choose the test levels, techniques and tools.
- Record why.

## Outcome
A selected test approach.

## Purpose
Designs the test cases and scenarios that verify the system and models the coverage they give. Good design finds defects efficiently.

## Responsibilities
- Design the test cases.
- Design the test scenarios.
- Model the coverage that the tests provide.

## Outcome
A designed set of tests with a known coverage.

## Purpose
Models what the tests cover. A coverage model shows what has and has not been exercised.

## Activities
- Define the dimensions of coverage such as requirements, paths and data.
- Map the tests to them.

## Outcome
A coverage model.

## Purpose
Designs the data that tests use and provides it when tests are run. Tests that lack suitable data cannot exercise the system properly.

## Responsibilities
- Design the test data.
- Provide the test data.

## Outcome
Test data that is available when tests run.

## Purpose
Provides data for testing. Tests need data to run.

## Activities
- Create or obtain the test data and load it into the environment.
- Keep it current and protected.

## Outcome
Provisioned test data.

## Purpose
Specifies and provides the environments in which tests run. A test is only as reliable as the environment it runs in.

## Responsibilities
- Specify the environment.
- Provision the environment.

## Outcome
Test environments that are specified and ready for use.

## Purpose
Specifies the environment for tests. A specification makes the environment reproducible.

## Activities
- Describe the hardware, software and settings required.
- Agree it.

## Outcome
An environment specification.

## Purpose
Provisions environments. Provisioning makes an environment available.

## Activities
- Create the environment according to its specification.
- Confirm that it works.

## Outcome
A provisioned environment.

## Purpose
Designs the framework and architecture of test automation. A sound design keeps automated tests maintainable as they grow.

## Responsibilities
- Select the automation framework.
- Design the architecture of the automation.

## Outcome
A test automation design that can be built on.

## Purpose
Selects the framework for test automation. The framework shapes all later tests.

## Activities
- Compare candidate frameworks against the needs.
- Choose one and record why.

## Outcome
A selected framework.

## Purpose
Designs the architecture of test automation. A sound architecture keeps tests maintainable.

## Activities
- Define the layers, shared components and conventions.
- Document them.

## Outcome
An automation architecture.

## Purpose
Develops automated test scripts and the mocks and stubs that they use. Scripts turn designed tests into repeatable ones.

## Responsibilities
- Develop the test scripts.
- Develop the mocks and stubs that isolate the system under test.

## Outcome
Automated test scripts that can be run repeatedly.

## Purpose
Writes automated test scripts. Scripts run tests without manual effort.

## Activities
- Implement each test case as a script.
- Check that it runs reliably.

## Outcome
Test scripts.

## Purpose
Develops mocks and stubs. They stand in for parts that are unavailable.

## Activities
- Build substitutes that behave like the real parts.
- Check that they are faithful enough.

## Outcome
Mocks and stubs.

## Purpose

Definition of a hypothesis, method, success criteria, time box, and decision rule for a prototype or experiment.
Systematic analysis of failure modes, their causes, effects, severity, and detection (IEC 60812).
Catalogue of automated, objective measures that verify architectural quality attributes continuously.
Time-ordered record of notifications and status updates issued to stakeholders during an incident.
Assessment of open-source and third-party licence obligations and conflicts for a release (SPDX).
Record of a model version released to an environment, with approver, configuration, and rollback reference.
Report of production model performance, data drift, and prediction quality against thresholds.
Structured plan for a new engineer covering access, tooling, context, and first deliverables.
Findings of authorised security testing with severity rating, evidence, and remediation guidance (OWASP, PTES).
Assessment of privacy risks of personal-data processing and the controls applied (GDPR Article 35 DPIA, ISO/IEC 29134).
Time-phased view of planned product outcomes and initiatives linked to objectives.
Baseline plan stating scope, schedule, resources, milestones, dependencies, and governance (PMBOK).
Periodic report of progress, variance against baseline, risks, issues, and forecast.
Findings of a prototype or experiment against its success criteria, with a proceed, pivot, or stop recommendation.
Non-functional requirements expressed as measurable quality-attribute scenarios (ISO/IEC 25010, SEI quality attribute workshop).
Planned structural code changes with scope, rationale, risk, and behaviour-preservation verification.
Register of applicable laws, regulations, and standards, mapped to obligations and controls.
Declared settings for a source repository including access, protected branches, required checks, and review rules.
Results of failover, recovery, and degradation testing against resilience targets.
Actions, owners, triggers, and contingency for treating identified risks (ISO 31000).
Register of identified risks with likelihood, impact, rating, owner, and status (ISO 31000, PMBOK).
Tested procedure and criteria for reverting a deployment to the last known good state.
Security requirements derived from risk and obligations, traceable to design and tests (OWASP ASVS).
Definition of service-level indicators, objectives, measurement windows, and error budgets (Google SRE).
Mapping of engineers to skills and proficiency levels used to identify gaps.
Machine-readable inventory of software components, versions, suppliers, and licences (SPDX, CycloneDX, NTIA minimum elements).
Record of a user support request, diagnosis, resolution, and closure with timestamps.
Register of identified technical debt with location, impact, estimated repayment cost, owner, and priority.
Test cases with preconditions, inputs, steps, expected results, and traceability (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3).
Prepared and protected data used to execute tests, with provenance and privacy treatment.
Definition of the hardware, software, data, and configuration required to execute tests.
Plan for a test effort covering scope, schedule, resources, entry and exit criteria (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3).
Organisation- or project-level approach to testing covering test levels, types, risk-based priorities, and tooling (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3).
Analysis of assets, trust boundaries, threats, and mitigations, for example using STRIDE (OWASP Threat Modeling).
Plan of training activities mapped to identified skill gaps, with schedule and success measures.
Findings of moderated or unmoderated usability testing, with task success, errors, and severity-rated issues (ISO 9241-210).
Synthesis of user feedback and support data into prioritised themes and recommendations.
Findings of user research including needs, personas, and journeys, with evidence.
Hierarchical decomposition of project scope into deliverables and work packages (PMBOK).
Model of expected load, user behaviour, data volumes, and targets used to design performance tests.

## Purpose
Designs the platform approach of a mobile application, including the platforms and devices it supports and how it works offline. These choices shape the whole of the application.

## Responsibilities
- Select the platform strategy.
- Define which devices and operating system versions are supported.
- Design offline operation and synchronisation.

## Outcome
A mobile platform design that states the strategy, the support matrix and the offline behaviour.

## Purpose
Selects the platform strategy. The strategy decides how apps are built across platforms.

## Activities
- Compare native, cross-platform and web approaches.
- Choose and record why.

## Outcome
A selected platform strategy.

default_label: Device And Os Support Matrix Definition
description:
## Purpose
Defines the devices and operating systems supported. The matrix sets what must be tested.

## Activities
- List the devices and versions covered.
- Agree them.

## Outcome
A support matrix.

## Purpose
Designs offline use and synchronisation. It lets the app work without a connection.

## Activities
- Define what is stored locally and how changes are merged.
- Handle conflicts.

## Outcome
An offline and synchronisation design.

## Purpose
Builds a mobile application, including its interface, its use of platform services and its performance. Construction produces the application that users install.

## Responsibilities
- Implement the user interface of the application.
- Integrate the platform APIs.
- Optimise the performance of the application on mobile devices.

## Outcome
A mobile application that works on its supported platforms.

## Purpose
Implements the interface of a mobile app. Implementation builds what users see.

## Activities
- Build screens and interactions to the design.
- Test on devices.

## Outcome
An implemented mobile interface.

## Purpose
Integrates a mobile app with the platform's services. Platform APIs give access to device features.

## Activities
- Call the operating system services the app needs such as camera, location and notifications.
- Handle permissions and platform differences.

## Outcome
Integrated platform APIs.

## Purpose
Optimises the performance of a mobile app. Performance on limited devices shapes the user experience.

## Activities
- Reduce start-up time, memory and battery use.
- Measure on real devices.

## Outcome
An optimised mobile app.

## Purpose
Verifies a mobile application across its devices, for security and for conformance to store guidelines. Mobile applications run on many devices and must meet the rules of the stores.

## Responsibilities
- Test across the device matrix.
- Test the security of the application.
- Review conformance to the app store guidelines.

## Outcome
Evidence that the mobile application is of acceptable quality and can be accepted by the stores.

## Purpose
Tests an app across the supported devices. Behaviour varies between devices and versions.

## Activities
- Run tests on each device and operating system in the matrix.
- Record failures by device.

## Outcome
Device matrix test results.

## Purpose
Tests the security of a mobile app. Mobile apps run on devices that users control.

## Activities
- Examine storage, communication and permissions for weaknesses.
- Report findings.

## Outcome
Mobile security test results.

## Purpose
Reviews an app against store guidelines. Non-conformance can cause rejection.

## Activities
- Compare the app with each store's rules.
- List what must change.

## Outcome
An app store conformance review.

## Purpose
Manages the release of a mobile application, including store submission, staged rollout and monitoring after release. Mobile releases are slow to correct, so careful management matters.

## Responsibilities
- Prepare the store submission.
- Manage the staged rollout.
- Monitor crashes and adoption.

## Outcome
A mobile release that reaches users in a controlled way and is monitored.

## Purpose
Prepares the app for submission to a store. Complete submissions avoid delay.

## Activities
- Assemble the build, listing, declarations and assets.
- Check against the store's requirements.

## Outcome
A prepared store submission.

## Purpose
Manages a staged rollout. Staging limits the exposure of a faulty release.

## Activities
- Release to increasing portions of users while watching results.
- Pause or roll back if problems appear.

## Outcome
A managed staged rollout.

## Purpose
Monitors crashes and adoption after release. Monitoring shows how the release fares in use.

## Activities
- Track crash rates and the spread of the new version.
- Report problems.

## Outcome
Crash and adoption monitoring.

## Purpose
Identifies hazards and assesses the risk each presents, then allocates the integrity level that the safety functions must achieve. Safety engineering starts from a clear understanding of what could cause harm.

## Responsibilities
- Identify hazards.
- Analyse each hazard and assess its risk.
- Allocate safety integrity levels.

## Outcome
An analysis of hazards and the integrity level required to control each.

## Purpose
Identifies hazards. Hazards are conditions that could cause harm.

## Activities
- Examine the system and its use for sources of harm.
- Record each hazard.

## Outcome
Identified hazards.

## Purpose
Analyses hazards and assesses their risk. Assessment shows which hazards need controls.

## Activities
- Judge the severity, exposure and controllability of each hazard.
- Rate the risk.

## Outcome
A hazard analysis and risk assessment.

## Purpose
Allocates integrity levels to safety functions. The level sets the rigour required.

## Activities
- Assign a level to each function from its risk.
- Record the basis.

## Outcome
Allocated safety integrity levels.

## Purpose
Derives safety requirements from the hazard analysis, allocates them to the design and keeps them traceable. Safety requirements state what the system must do to be safe.

## Responsibilities
- Derive safety requirements.
- Allocate safety requirements to parts of the design.
- Trace safety requirements to their origin and to their verification.

## Outcome
Safety requirements that are allocated and traceable.

## Purpose
Derives safety requirements from hazards. Requirements state what makes the system safe.

## Activities
- State a requirement for each hazard control.
- Make each verifiable.

## Outcome
Derived safety requirements.

## Purpose
Allocates safety requirements to parts of the design. Allocation shows who is responsible for each.

## Activities
- Assign each requirement to a component or procedure.
- Record the allocation.

## Outcome
Allocated safety requirements.

## Purpose
Traces safety requirements. Traceability shows that each is designed, implemented and verified.

## Activities
- Link each requirement to its source, design, code and tests.
- Check for gaps.

## Outcome
Safety requirement traceability.

## Purpose
Analyses the timing of a real-time design, including its timing budget, its worst-case execution time and its schedulability. A real-time system is correct only if it meets its deadlines.

## Responsibilities
- Define the timing budget.
- Analyse the worst-case execution time.
- Analyse whether the tasks can be scheduled to meet their deadlines.

## Outcome
A timing analysis that shows whether the design meets its deadlines.

## Purpose
Defines timing budgets. Budgets divide the available time among tasks.

## Activities
- State the allowed time for each task and path.
- Agree them.

## Outcome
Timing budgets.

## Purpose
Analyses the worst-case execution time of tasks. The worst case determines whether deadlines can be met.

## Activities
- Determine the longest time each task can take.
- Record the method.

## Outcome
Worst-case execution times.

## Purpose
Analyses whether tasks can be scheduled to meet deadlines. It shows whether the design is feasible.

## Activities
- Combine execution times, periods and priorities.
- State whether all deadlines hold.

## Outcome
A schedulability analysis.

## Purpose
Verifies a safety-critical system by checking conformance to coding standards, analysing structural coverage and testing with injected faults. Safety-critical systems must be verified more rigorously than other systems.

## Responsibilities
- Check conformance to coding standards.
- Analyse structural coverage.
- Test with injected faults.

## Outcome
Verification evidence that meets the standard required for safety.

## Purpose
Checks conformance to coding standards. Safety standards restrict how code is written.

## Activities
- Run checks and reviews against the standard.
- Record deviations.

## Outcome
A coding standard conformance check.

## Purpose
Analyses structural coverage of tests. It shows what code has been exercised.

## Activities
- Measure statement, branch or condition coverage.
- Explain code not covered.

## Outcome
A structural coverage analysis.

## Purpose
Tests with injected faults. It shows how the system reacts to failures.

## Activities
- Introduce faults in hardware or software.
- Observe the safety response.

## Outcome
Fault injection test results.

## Purpose
Builds the argument and the evidence that a system is safe and obtains independent assessment of it. Assurance is what regulators and customers rely on.

## Responsibilities
- Construct the safety case.
- Obtain independent safety assessment.
- Compile the evidence for certification.

## Outcome
A safety case and the certification evidence that supports it.

## Purpose
Constructs a safety case. A safety case argues that the system is acceptably safe.

## Activities
- State the claims, arguments and evidence.
- Keep them consistent.

## Outcome
A safety case.

## Purpose
Obtains independent assessment of safety. Independence adds credibility.

## Activities
- Provide the assessor with the case and evidence.
- Address their findings.

## Outcome
An independent safety assessment.

## Purpose
Compiles the evidence for certification. Certifiers require complete evidence.

## Activities
- Gather the plans, results and records the standard requires.
- Organise them for review.

## Outcome
Compiled certification evidence.

## Purpose
Decides which functions are performed in hardware and which in software, and allocates interfaces and performance budgets. Partitioning is a defining decision of hardware and software co-design.

## Responsibilities
- Partition functions between hardware and software.
- Allocate the interfaces between them.
- Allocate performance budgets.

## Outcome
A partition of the system that allocates functions, interfaces and budgets.

## Purpose
Decides which functions go in hardware and which in software. The choice shapes cost, speed and flexibility.

## Activities
- Compare the options for each function.
- Record the allocation.

## Outcome
A hardware-software partition.

## Purpose
Allocates the interfaces between hardware and software. Allocation defines the boundary.

## Activities
- Define the signals, registers and protocols.
- Assign owners.

## Outcome
Allocated interfaces.

## Purpose
Allocates performance budgets. Budgets divide limits across the parts.

## Activities
- Divide time, power and resources among hardware and software.
- Check the total.

## Outcome
Allocated performance budgets.

## Purpose
Simulates hardware and software together before the hardware exists. Co-simulation finds interface errors early.

## Responsibilities
- Develop virtual prototypes of the hardware.
- Execute co-simulations.
- Simulate conformance to the interface definitions.

## Outcome
Simulation results that show how hardware and software work together.

## Purpose
Develops a virtual prototype of the hardware. It lets software be built before the hardware exists.

## Activities
- Model the hardware behaviour in software.
- Validate the model.

## Outcome
A virtual prototype.

## Purpose
Runs hardware and software together in simulation. It finds interface errors early.

## Activities
- Execute the co-simulation with test scenarios.
- Record the results.

## Outcome
Co-simulation results.

## Purpose
Simulates conformance to interfaces. It shows whether both sides honour the interface.

## Activities
- Run scenarios that exercise the interface.
- Report deviations.

## Outcome
Interface conformance simulation results.

## Purpose
Verifies software against real hardware connected to a simulated environment. This verification exposes behaviour that simulation alone cannot show.

## Responsibilities
- Specify the test bench.
- Execute the tests on the test bench.
- Test scenarios in which the hardware fails.

## Outcome
Test results from software running against real hardware.

## Purpose
Specifies the test bench for hardware-in-the-loop testing. The bench provides the simulated environment.

## Activities
- Define the hardware, simulators and instruments required.
- Document the setup.

## Outcome
A test bench specification.

## Purpose
Runs tests on the hardware-in-the-loop bench. It shows behaviour with real hardware.

## Activities
- Run the test cases and record results.
- Investigate failures.

## Outcome
Hardware-in-the-loop results.

## Purpose
Tests scenarios in which hardware faults. It shows how software copes.

## Activities
- Cause hardware faults on the bench.
- Observe the response.

## Outcome
Hardware fault scenario results.

## Purpose
Brings hardware and software together, tests them as a whole and triages the defects found. Integration shows whether the two halves fit.

## Responsibilities
- Bring up the board.
- Test the integration of hardware and software.
- Triage the integration defects.

## Outcome
Hardware and software that work together, with the remaining defects triaged.

## Purpose
Brings up a new board. Bring-up shows that the hardware basically works.

## Activities
- Power up the board and test its basic functions.
- Record faults.

## Outcome
A brought-up board.

## Purpose
Tests hardware and software together. It shows whether the combination works.

## Activities
- Run integration tests on the real system.
- Record results.

## Outcome
Hardware-software integration test results.

## Purpose
Triages defects found in integration. Triage assigns them to the right owners.

## Activities
- Decide whether each defect is in hardware, software or the interface.
- Assign it.

## Outcome
Triaged integration defects.

## Purpose
Designs the mechanics of a game, models its balance and documents the design. Gameplay design determines whether a game is engaging.

## Responsibilities
- Design the gameplay mechanics.
- Model the balance of the game.
- Document the game design.

## Outcome
A documented gameplay design with a balanced model.

## Purpose
Designs the mechanics of play. Mechanics define what players do.

## Activities
- Define the rules, actions and goals.
- Test them in prototypes.

## Outcome
Gameplay mechanics.

## Purpose
Models game balance. Balance keeps play fair and engaging.

## Activities
- Model values such as strength, cost and reward.
- Test their effect.

## Outcome
A game balance model.

## Purpose
Documents the game design. Documentation shares the design with the team.

## Activities
- Describe mechanics, content and flow.
- Keep it current.

## Outcome
Game design documentation.

## Purpose
Engineers the runtime of a game, including its frame budget, its rendering pipeline and its asset pipeline. The runtime must meet its timing every frame.

## Responsibilities
- Define the frame budget.
- Implement the rendering pipeline.
- Implement the asset pipeline.

## Outcome
A runtime that renders within its frame budget.

## Purpose
Defines the frame budget. The budget limits the time to produce each frame.

## Activities
- State the time allowed per frame and its division among systems.
- Agree it.

## Outcome
A frame budget.

## Purpose
Implements the rendering pipeline. The pipeline turns game data into images.

## Activities
- Build the stages that draw each frame.
- Test them for speed and quality.

## Outcome
An implemented rendering pipeline.

## Purpose
Implements the asset pipeline. The pipeline prepares art, audio and data for the game.

## Activities
- Build the tools that convert and package assets.
- Test them.

## Outcome
An implemented asset pipeline.

## Purpose
Profiles and improves the performance of a game, including its frame rate, its memory and its load times. Performance determines how a game feels to play.

## Responsibilities
- Profile the frame rate.
- Profile memory use against the budget.
- Optimise load times.

## Outcome
A game that meets its performance budgets.

## Purpose
Profiles the frame rate. Profiling shows where time goes in each frame.

## Activities
- Measure the time of systems per frame.
- Find the slowest.

## Outcome
Frame rate profiles.

## Purpose
Profiles memory against the budget. Memory limits constrain games.

## Activities
- Measure the use of memory by category.
- Compare with the budget.

## Outcome
Memory budget profiles.

## Purpose
Optimises load times. Short loads keep players engaged.

## Activities
- Find and reduce delays in loading.
- Measure the improvement.

## Outcome
Optimised load times.

## Purpose
Verifies a game through playtesting, platform certification testing and hardware compatibility testing. Games must be fun, must pass platform rules and must run on varied hardware.

## Responsibilities
- Run playtests.
- Test for platform certification.
- Test compatibility with hardware.

## Outcome
A game that has been tested for play, certification and compatibility.

## Purpose
Tests a game by playing it. Playtesting shows whether it is fun and understandable.

## Activities
- Have players play and observe their behaviour.
- Collect their feedback.

## Outcome
Playtest results.

## Purpose
Tests against platform certification rules. A game must pass these to be released.

## Activities
- Run the platform holder's checks.
- Correct failures.

## Outcome
Platform certification test results.

## Purpose
Tests a game on varied hardware. Players use many configurations.

## Activities
- Run the game on a range of devices and settings.
- Record issues.

## Outcome
Hardware compatibility test results.

## Purpose
Operates a game as a live service by analysing telemetry, releasing content updates and running live events. A live game is changed continuously after launch.

## Responsibilities
- Analyse the telemetry of the live service.
- Release content updates.
- Operate live events.

## Outcome
A live game that is updated and operated in response to how it is played.

## Purpose
Analyses telemetry from a live game. Telemetry shows how players behave.

## Activities
- Examine usage and performance data.
- Draw conclusions for design and operation.

## Outcome
A live service telemetry analysis.

## Purpose
Releases content updates. Updates keep a live game fresh.

## Activities
- Prepare, test and publish new content.
- Monitor reception.

## Outcome
A released content update.

## Purpose
Operates live events. Events engage players over time.

## Activities
- Schedule and run the event and watch the service.
- Respond to problems.

## Outcome
Operated live events.
Decision record of native, cross-platform, or hybrid approach, supported platforms, and minimum operating-system versions, with rationale.
Matrix of supported devices, operating-system versions, form factors, and capabilities used to scope development and test coverage.
Assessment of a mobile application against OWASP MASVS and MASTG, with findings, severity, and remediation.
Identification of hazardous events and their risk classification, determining safety integrity levels (IEC 61508, ISO 26262 HARA, ARP4761).
Safety requirements derived from hazard analysis, allocated to components, and traceable to verification (IEC 61508-2, ISO 26262-3).
Worst-case execution time and schedulability analysis demonstrating that real-time deadlines are met.
Code coverage evidence (statement, decision, MC/DC) at the level required by the safety integrity level (DO-178C, ISO 26262-6).
Structured argument with evidence that the system is acceptably safe for its intended use (GSN, IEC 61508, UL 4600).
Allocation of functions between hardware and software with interface definitions, performance budgets, and rationale (ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288).
Results of simulating hardware models together with software, covering interface conformance and timing behaviour.

default_label: Hardware In The Loop Test Report
description: Results of executing software against real or emulated hardware on a test bench, including fault scenarios.
Record of board bring-up and hardware-software integration, with defects attributed to hardware or software.
Living specification of gameplay systems, mechanics, content, progression, and balance targets.
Allocation of frame time, memory, storage, and load-time budgets per platform and subsystem.
Findings of structured playtesting, covering fun, difficulty, usability, and defects, with player evidence.
Results of platform holder certification testing against technical requirements, with pass or fail by requirement.
Record of an applied capability optimisation, the measured performance delta, and the non-regression evidence.

Reconciled statement of stakeholder intent drawn from meetings, tickets, support conversations, and correspondence, with currency date and detected conflicts (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 stakeholder requirements).
Explainable record linking a decision to its supporting evidence, alternatives considered, approver, and outcome.
Recommendation derived from accumulated organisational evidence, with the evidence cited and the reasoning stated.
Recommendation to add, change, or retire capabilities in response to revised objectives and business signal.
Continuous metrics, logs, and traces emitted by running systems, expressed as OpenTelemetry signals.
Ordered, immutable log of platform events that can be replayed to reconstruct state and behaviour at any point in time.
Continuously maintained relationships among requirements, designs, code, tests, defects, and releases, with each link change emitted as it occurs (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148).
Stream of creations and modifications to engineering artefacts and models, with author, version, and diff.
Stream of commits, pull requests, and merges to source repositories, with author, scope, and review status.
Stream of deployment, configuration, and rollback events across environments, with version and actor.
Stream of test executions and results over time, per test, build, and environment.
Stream of creations, modifications, and status changes to requirements, with rationale and source.
Stream of changes to policies, standards, regulatory obligations, and decisions that govern engineering work.
Stream of stakeholder signals from meetings, tickets, support conversations, and correspondence.
Stream of observed business behaviour and market or organisational change that affects the business domain.
External structured feed of vulnerabilities, indicators, and attack patterns (STIX/TAXII, CVE, CISA KEV).

Finding that records an architectural pattern predicted to stop meeting scale or quality needs, with lead time, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records deployed configuration diverging from declared intent, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records the domain model diverging from observed business behaviour, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records a defect class that current test coverage is predicted to miss, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records the current risk to an in-progress release, with contributing factors, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records an engineering event that violates an applicable policy or obligation, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records a requirement that has become invalid, conflicting, or ambiguous through change, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records precursor conditions of a probable incident, with expected lead time, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records a location where a fix or improvement applies, and whether it was applied, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records a capability or practice improvement supported by accumulated evidence, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records a change in the security exposure of the system portfolio, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records the organisation's own exposure to a newly emerged attack pattern, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records engineering work that no longer serves its stated Objective, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records a latent contradiction among active policies, standards, or decisions, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records a deviation of quality evidence from defined criteria, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records stakeholder intent diverging from the current requirement baseline, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records an engineering risk forecast before it materialises, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
Finding that records a bottleneck limiting the performance of a capability, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.

Finding that records a recurring structural pattern, or anti-pattern, recognised across systems, with the subject, supporting evidence references, severity, confidence, detection time, and recommended action.
